unidentified.description: A sealed jar of clear amber-gold tallow carrying a faint scent of distant thunder.

items.name: Ōkami no Hone 狼の骨 (Mountain God's Bones)

description.value:
Ōkami no Hone 狼の骨 (Mountain God's Bones)

Category: Hone
Rarity: VeryRare
Source: One-time harvest — Yama-no-Ōkami
Preservation: Indefinite if kept dry. Raw bone benefits from cleaning and bleaching soon after harvest.
Tools: Woodcarver's or bonecarver's tools for shaping; butcher's cleaver for initial sectioning
Restrictions: Single-grade-locked. Does not follow standard grade progression — the nat-20 harvest check locked all bone material at 極上 Gokujō.

A clean butchering preserved the long bones of the legs, the heavy bones of the spine, and the great curved ribs. Bone of this size and density is genuinely uncommon — most predators in Hokori are smaller creatures whose bones snap rather than carve. A bone-carver can shape these into hilts, scabbard fittings, ornamental inlays, and the kind of polished accents that mark an expensive weapon or a noble's accessories. There is enough material here to keep a single craftsman supplied for years.

DM Notes

**One-time harvest.** Single-grade-locked at 極上 Gokujō. Party holds the full 350 lb of carving stock (tracked in `dm/campaign-state.md`). **Skill-Check Reveals** — one check per skill; nat-20 reveals all three. - **Religion (DC 13)** — Bones of a creature thought to be a kami avatar carry spiritual weight. Ground into bone meal and presented at a shrine, they constitute a significant offering. Carved into prayer beads or ritual implements, they serve as a permanent reminder of the offering and may carry the kami's favour with them. - **Nature (DC 11)** — Excellent carving stock. The character can identify which bones are best suited to which products — femurs for sword hilts, ribs for scabbard fittings, vertebrae for ornaments and beads. Knows the going rate per pound raw and per pound cut. - **Arcana (DC 14)** — The bone is *resonant* — it carries a faint sei echo when struck, a quality prized by arcane focus makers. Carved into a focus, it would suit a seimaster whose practice leans toward warding, banishment, or anti-spirit magics. Particularly valuable to seimasters in Sora and Kaze. Cross-references: See Kegawa → Ōkami no Kegawa; Hone → Ōkami no Zugai / Kiba / Tenohira; Niku → Ōkami-niku and related cuts.

unidentified.name: Unidentified Mountain God's Bones
unidentified.description: A large collection of unusually dense, pale grey bones from a massive wolf-like creature. Femurs as long as a man's arm, ribs curved like longbow staves, vertebrae the size of a clenched fist. Strike one against another and the sound carries oddly, lingering a moment longer than plain bone should.

items.name: Ōkami no Kegawa 狼の毛皮 (Mountain God's Pelt)

description.value:
Ōkami no Kegawa 狼の毛皮 (Mountain God's Pelt)

Category: Kegawa
Rarity: VeryRare
Source: One-time harvest — Yama-no-Ōkami
Preservation: Indefinite if properly cured and stored cool and dry. Requires specialist leatherworker for finishing (weeks of downtime work).
Tools: Leatherworker's tools for curing and finishing; ceremonial stitching requires a master, not a journeyman
Restrictions: Single-grade-locked. This entry does not follow the standard Nami/Jō/Tokujō/Gokujō grade progression — the nat-20 harvest check locked the pelt at 極上 Gokujō at the moment of butchering, and no lesser grade exists for this material.

A single enormous pelt taken from the back, flanks, and shoulders of the beast. The fur is silver-grey at the roots and deepens to charcoal at the tips, dense enough to turn a winter wind and long enough at the ruff that a man could bury both hands to the wrist in it. In low light the guard hairs catch a faint cool sheen — not luminous, but suggestive, the way frost catches starlight. Two further sections — one from the belly, one stitched from the limb hide — come off cleaner than any hunter could reasonably expect, bringing the total usable pelt to something well beyond a single cloak.

DM Notes

**One-time harvest.** Single-grade-locked at 極上 Gokujō. The party currently holds the full yield — 1 primary pelt + 2 secondary sections. Track in `dm/campaign-state.md`. **Skill-Check Reveals** — the full value of this component is not obvious. A character may attempt one check per skill when the pelt is first examined or investigated further. A natural 20 reveals everything across all three skills. - **Religion (DC 13)** — Wolves are sacred to many of the mountain kami, and a pelt of this clarity would be received as an extraordinary offering at any mountain shrine. A shrine receiving it would owe the giver a favour — the kind of favour that gets remembered for years. In Sora, Tsuchi, or upper Kaze, this could open doors that gold cannot. - **Nature (DC 12)** — The pelt is from a once-in-a-generation specimen. The character understands which sections are most valuable, how the hide must be cured, and that a master leatherworker (not a common one) is required to do the work properly. Identifies the leatherworkers of Heian, Kumo-no-Ue, and Akatsuki as having the requisite skill. - **Arcana (DC 15)** — The faint cool sheen in low light is real sei resonance — the creature's spiritual nature has imprinted on its fur. Worked into a ceremonial garment, the pelt could serve as an arcane focus for protection, divination, or ward-based magics. A seimaster who handles such a cloak would feel it. Cross-references: See Niku → Ōkami-niku and related cuts; Hone → Ōkami no Hone / Zugai / Kiba / Tenohira; Shushoku → Ōkami no Abura. All Yama-no-Ōkami components share the single-grade-locked Gokujō convention.

unidentified.name: Unidentified Mountain God's Pelt
unidentified.description: An enormous wolf pelt, silver-grey shading to charcoal, far larger than any ordinary wolf should grow. The fur is dense and heavy, catches the light oddly in dim rooms, and carries a faint cold smell of mountain stone.

items.name: Ōkami no Kiba 狼の牙 (Mountain God's Fangs)

description.value:
Ōkami no Kiba 狼の牙 (Mountain God's Fangs)

Category: Hone
Rarity: VeryRare
Source: One-time harvest — Yama-no-Ōkami
Preservation: Indefinite. Cleaning and polishing benefit the final product.
Tools: Bonecarver's tools for shaping; jeweler's tools for setting
Restrictions: Single-grade-locked. Does not follow standard grade progression.

The nat 20 harvest also yielded the long canine teeth clean and intact, drawn separately from the jaw before the skull was preserved. Each fang is as long as a man's hand and pale grey, tapering to a point still sharp enough to open skin. A bone-carver in any reasonably sized settlement will pay handsomely for worked fangs of this size, and a seimaster may recognise them as a viable reagent for a charm or focus.

DM Notes

**One-time harvest.** Single-grade-locked at 極上 Gokujō. Party holds 4 intact fangs (tracked in `dm/campaign-state.md`). **Skill-Check Reveals** — one check per skill; nat-20 reveals all three. - **Religion (DC 11)** — Long-standing tradition uses wolf fangs as protective charms, particularly for travellers crossing mountain passes. Hung from a cord at the throat or tied to a belt, a fang offers a small but real ward against being attacked by wild beasts. - **Nature (DC 10)** — Easily identified as adult predator canines in exceptional condition. Carving stock for amulets, daggerhilt accents, or ornamental inlays. - **Arcana (DC 13)** — Reagent for charm and focus crafting. Particularly suited to weapon enchantments — a fang set into the pommel of a blade can serve as a focus for spells that augment the weapon's bite. Cross-references: See Hone → Ōkami no Hone / Zugai / Tenohira; Kegawa → Ōkami no Kegawa.

unidentified.name: Unidentified Mountain God's Fangs
unidentified.description: Four long, curved canine teeth, pale grey and heavier than they look. The point of each is still needle-sharp.

items.name: Ōkami no Tenohira 狼の掌 (Mountain God's Paws)

description.value:
Ōkami no Tenohira 狼の掌 (Mountain God's Paws)

Category: Hone
Rarity: VeryRare
Source: One-time harvest — Yama-no-Ōkami
Preservation: Indefinite if properly cured and mounted; pads can dry and crack if neglected
Tools: Leatherworker's tools for pad preservation; bonecarver's tools for claw separation and shaping
Restrictions: Single-grade-locked. Does not follow standard grade progression.

Four massive paws, each broader than a man's chest and heavy enough to need both hands to lift, removed cleanly at the wrist joint. The pads are thick black leather, deeply callused from a lifetime walking on stone, and the dew claws and main claws are intact and unbroken — a testament to the quality of the harvest. In Hokori folk tradition, the paw of a great wolf is hung above the door of a household to ward off mountain spirits and protect those within from being lost in the wilds. Bone-carvers and amulet-makers will pay well for whole paws, and a seimaster will pay better.

DM Notes

**One-time harvest.** Single-grade-locked at 極上 Gokujō. Party holds 4 intact paws (tracked in `dm/campaign-state.md`). **Skill-Check Reveals** — one check per skill; nat-20 reveals all three. - **Religion (DC 12)** — The folk tradition of hanging a wolf paw above a household doorway is older than most temples — it predates the formal Shinto observances and is rooted in pre-imperial mountain beliefs. A paw mounted properly above a door is a genuine spiritual ward against being led astray in the wilds. Effective even for unbelievers. - **Nature (DC 14)** — The depth of callus on the pads tells the character that this creature walked exclusively on stone, not soft ground — confirming it lived its entire life in the high passes. The paws can be processed into trophy mounts, rugs, or grip-leather for weapon hilts. Identifies the proper preservation methods. - **Arcana (DC 13)** — The claws carry trace sei imprint and would serve as reagents for the crafting of protection charms, amulets against being lost, or low-level wards. Worth significantly more to a charm-maker than to a bone-carver. Cross-references: See Hone → Ōkami no Hone / Zugai / Kiba; Kegawa → Ōkami no Kegawa.

unidentified.name: Unidentified Mountain God's Paws
unidentified.description: Four enormous wolf paws, each the span of a grown man's chest, pad-down and heavy. Thick black calluses line the underside; the dark grey claws are unbroken and wickedly curved.

items.name: Ōkami no Zugai 狼の頭骸 (Mountain God's Skull)

description.value:
Ōkami no Zugai 狼の頭骸 (Mountain God's Skull)

Category: Hone
Rarity: VeryRare
Source: One-time harvest — Yama-no-Ōkami
Preservation: Indefinite. Should be cleaned and mounted soon after harvest; raw skulls benefit from bleaching and careful jaw stabilization.
Tools: Bone cleaning and mounting requires specialist work; shrine enshrinement requires priestly rites
Restrictions: Single-grade-locked. Does not follow standard grade progression.

The skull was lifted intact from the spine — a fanged mask the size and shape of a temple bell, its great jaws still locked in their final snarl, the orbital sockets large enough that a child could put a fist into one. The bone is pale grey and unusually heavy, threaded with fine darker veining beneath the surface. As an object it is genuinely arresting — visitors to a hall containing such a skull tend to fall silent on first seeing it, and stay that way longer than is comfortable.

DM Notes

**One-time harvest.** Single-grade-locked at 極上 Gokujō. Party currently holds the intact skull (tracked in `dm/campaign-state.md`). **Skill-Check Reveals** — one check per skill; nat-20 reveals all three. - **Religion (DC 14)** — The skull of a kami avatar is a relic. The mountain temples of Sora, upper Kaze, and Tsuchi maintain a tradition of enshrinement for such skulls — placing them in a sealed inner chamber, before which offerings are made for the spirit's onward journey. A temple receiving this skull would consider the giver to be marked by the kami in question, in a way that is generally considered fortunate but is occasionally not. - **Nature (DC 12)** — The wear on the teeth and the size of the orbital ridges suggest a creature in its prime, perhaps a century old. The character can read the diet from the molars (predominantly meat, but also some plant matter — unusual for a wolf) and identify the species characteristics that mark this as more than a normal beast. - **Arcana (DC 16)** — The skull retains a strong sei imprint — the strongest of any of the components. It could be turned into a ward-mask for ritual use, a powerful arcane focus, or a vessel for binding magics. A skilled seimaster could conceivably use it to commune with the creature's lingering essence, though doing so would risk drawing the attention of whatever kami the beast served in life. Detect Magic registers it clearly. Cross-references: See Kegawa → Ōkami no Kegawa; Hone → Ōkami no Hone / Kiba / Tenohira.

unidentified.name: Unidentified Mountain God's Skull
unidentified.description: An enormous wolf skull, pale grey and very heavy, with long curved canines still set in the jaw. The bone looks faintly veined beneath the surface. People who see it tend to stop talking for a while.

items.name: Oniuo 鬼魚 (Oni Fish) (極上 Gokujō)

description.value:
Oniuo 鬼魚 (Oni Fish)

Category: Niku
Rarity: Rare
Source: Hunted
Preservation: 1 day fresh; 10 days salted
Tools: Heavy fishing tackle, harpoon; the fish fights strongly and can injure
Grade: 極上 Gokujō (craft modifier: +5)

A deep-water ocean fish with a brutal, almost armoured head and a jaw lined with small inward-curving teeth. The flesh is pale and dense, carrying a rich salt-and-iron flavour unlike any other catch. Prized by coastal chefs for the single cut drawn from the upper back, which is considered one of the finest pieces of fish in the archipelago.

DM Notes

Traditionally taken by harpoon from small boats during Tatsunami, when the deep schools rise closer to the surface. Dangerous work — losses are accepted as the price of the catch.

unidentified.name: Unidentified Oni Fish
unidentified.description: A large, armoured-looking fish with a grotesque jaw and surprisingly pale, clean flesh beneath the ugly exterior.

description.value:
Rei-en 霊塩 (Spirit Salt)

Category: Chomiryo
Rarity: Rare
Source: Harvested (Saishū)
Preservation: Indefinite; holds faint sei-glow for weeks
Tools: Herbalism kit (advantage); shrine permission or discretion
Grade: 極上 Gokujō (craft modifier: +5)

Crystalline deposits found at the margins of sei-active springs and pools, where the interaction between sei energy and mineral-rich water produces salt crystals that are faintly warm and carry a subtle luminescence. The flavor is clean and bright — not quite salt, not quite sweet, but something adjacent to both. Dissolves instantly on contact with food.

**Shrine-held.** Unauthorized harvest is sacrilege; may draw spirit ire.

items.name: Reikokoro 霊心 (Spirit Heart)

description.value:
Reikokoro 霊心 (Spirit Heart)

Category: Niku
Rarity: Legendary
Source: One-Time (Yama-no-Ōkami harvest)
Preservation: 2 days fresh; indefinitely if salted
Tools: Cook's utensils at minimum; shrine-blessed preparation strongly indicated
Restrictions: One-time only; irreplaceable; ceremonial significance

The creature's heart, roughly the size of a man's head and several times heavier, still faintly warm hours after death. Dense, dark red, and threaded with silver-white veins that pulsed once when first exposed to air before going still. It takes two grown men working together to lift it cleanly from the chest cavity, and one of them will need both hands. Mountain hunters speak of the reikokoro only in hushed terms — one portion, one meal, one chance. In the entire recorded history of Hokori's mountain provinces, a handful of cooks have been trusted with such an organ. None of them ever forgot the meal. Suitable for a Masterwork dish that feeds the entire party.

DM Notes

**[SEALED]** *(The mechanical and spiritual weight of the Reikokoro is a campaign-level matter. See DM secrets below.)* - **Religion (DC 15)** — Eating the heart of a kami avatar is a profound act, and the tradition surrounding it is divided. Some mountain sects consider it transgressive — a violation of the spirit's onward journey. Others consider it sacred — a sharing of essence between the slain and the slayer. If the meal is prepared at a shrine with proper rites, the latter interpretation prevails, and the eaters may be marked by the kami's blessing for some time after. - **Nature (DC 13)** — The character recognizes the heart as exceptional spirit-flesh, understands that it must be cooked fresh or properly preserved, and knows that the preparation requires great care. Suggests cook's utensils proficiency at minimum. - **Arcana (DC 16)** — The heart retains a fragment of the creature's essence. A character with arcane training senses it on contact — a low, steady warmth like banked coals. Eating it grants more than ordinary nourishment; it transfers a small portion of the creature's spiritual nature to the eater. (DM: this is the mechanical justification for the Masterwork buff — the players don't need to know the mechanics, but a character who passes this check understands *why* the meal will matter.) Preparation should be a scene — not a roll. The meal is worth a session opening. ---

unidentified.name: Unidentified Spirit Heart
unidentified.description: An enormous organ the size of a man's head, dark red shot through with faint silvery veining, heavy enough to require both hands to lift. Still warm to the touch. There is an unmistakable sense of *presence* to it — as though something were watching from inside the meat.

items.name: Ryū no Namida 竜の涙 (Dragon's Tear) (極上 Gokujō)

description.value:
Ryū no Namida 竜の涙 (Dragon's Tear)

Category: Chomiryo
Rarity: VeryRare
Source: Foraged (Saishū)
Preservation: Indefinite in sealed crystal vessel
Tools: Herbalism kit (advantage); Arcana (Int) DC 15 to handle safely; crystal vial
Restrictions: Progenitor-cavern-gated
Grade: 極上 Gokujō (craft modifier: +5)

A liquid mineral seep found in the deepest chambers of Progenitor-associated cave systems — slow drops that fall from stone ceilings into shallow basins over decades. The liquid is perfectly clear, faintly warm, and carries no scent. On the tongue it produces a sensation of pure, complex flavor that defies categorization — every person who tastes it describes something different. A single drop can transform an entire dish. The basins are found near places where Progenitors rested.

DM Notes

Progenitor-gated. Legendary artefact-tier ingredient.

unidentified.description: A perfectly clear, faintly warm liquid pooling drop by drop in a shallow stone basin deep beneath the earth.

items.name: Ryū no Sake 竜の酒 (Dragon's Sake) (極上 Gokujō)

description.value:
Ryū no Sake 竜の酒 (Dragon's Sake)

Category: Shushoku
Rarity: VeryRare
Source: Imperial / ceremonial gift only
Preservation: Indefinite in sealed ceremonial flask
Tools: None
Restrictions: **Never sold**; a single Progenitor-blessed cask in continuous use
Grade: 極上 Gokujō (craft modifier: +5)

Sake brewed in a single cask that was blessed at a Progenitor shrine generations ago and has been in continuous use ever since. The rice is Tennō-mai, the water is drawn from a sei-active spring, and the fermentation is tended by a master brewer who inherited the position from their grandmother. The finished sake is faintly luminescent in dim light, and those who drink it describe a sensation of warmth settling into the bones. Served only at imperial observances and the highest Shinto ceremonies — never sold, and given only as the most meaningful of gifts.

DM Notes

Campaign-level gift. Use as recognition from an emperor-tier figure.

items.name: Ryū no Sake 竜の酒 (Dragon's Sake) (特上 Tokujō)

description.value:
Ryū no Sake 竜の酒 (Dragon's Sake)

Category: Shushoku
Rarity: VeryRare
Source: Imperial / ceremonial gift only
Preservation: Indefinite in sealed ceremonial flask
Tools: None
Restrictions: **Never sold**; a single Progenitor-blessed cask in continuous use
Grade: 特上 Tokujō (craft modifier: +2)

Sake brewed in a single cask that was blessed at a Progenitor shrine generations ago and has been in continuous use ever since. The rice is Tennō-mai, the water is drawn from a sei-active spring, and the fermentation is tended by a master brewer who inherited the position from their grandmother. The finished sake is faintly luminescent in dim light, and those who drink it describe a sensation of warmth settling into the bones. Served only at imperial observances and the highest Shinto ceremonies — never sold, and given only as the most meaningful of gifts.

DM Notes

Campaign-level gift. Use as recognition from an emperor-tier figure.

items.name: Ryūgame 竜亀 (Dragon Turtle) (極上 Gokujō)

description.value:
Ryūgame 竜亀 (Dragon Turtle)

Category: Niku
Rarity: VeryRare
Source: Hunted
Preservation: 2 days fresh; indefinitely smoked or salted
Tools: Heavy harpoon, ship-based hunt; cook's utensils essential — the shell is used in Hone
Grade: 極上 Gokujō (craft modifier: +5)

Flesh from the great dragon-turtles that live in the deepest channels of the Serenia-kai. The meat is dense, dark, and carries a flavour that shifts between fish and the richest game — salt and iron in the first bite, something almost sweet and smoky in the finish. A single successful hunt can feed a small village for a week.

DM Notes

Hunting a dragon turtle is a clan-scale endeavour — a year's worth of story for the crew that brings one home. The secondary materials from the kill (shell for Hone, hide for Kegawa) can be worth as much as the meat.

unidentified.name: Unidentified Dragon Turtle
unidentified.description: Enormous slabs of dense dark meat, heavier than they look, with an indefinable combination of fish-and-game scent.

items.name: Ryūjika 竜鹿 (Dragon Deer) (極上 Gokujō)

description.value:
Ryūjika 竜鹿 (Dragon Deer)

Category: Niku
Rarity: Rare
Source: Hunted
Preservation: 2 days fresh; indefinitely smoked or salted
Tools: Bow or polearm; cook's utensils for butchery
Grade: 極上 Gokujō (craft modifier: +5)

A rare, long-limbed deer of the high plateaus — said to carry a trace of dragon lineage in its bearing. The meat is darker than common venison and carries a subtle warmth in its flavour, as though the animal were faintly hot-blooded. Highly sought by noble hunters and by temple cooks preparing ceremonial meals.

DM Notes

Ryūjika are traditionally hunted only by samurai and only with express permission from the local daimyo; poaching is a serious offence. A kill usually also yields antler material for the Hone category.

unidentified.name: Unidentified Dragon Deer
unidentified.description: Dark, rich cuts of large-game meat — heavier and finer-grained than common deer, with a faint iron-and-smoke scent.

description.value:
Ryūketsu-bana 竜血花 (Dragon's Blood Flower)

Category: Yakuso
Rarity: Rare
Source: Foraged
Preservation: 7 days fresh; indefinitely dried
Tools: Herbalism kit; careful extraction (grows in stone cracks)
Restrictions: Associated with Progenitor sites; rare in general circulation
Grade: 極上 Gokujō (craft modifier: +5)

A deep crimson flower with gold-veined petals, found growing from cracks in stone near Progenitor-associated ruins. Blooms are small — no larger than a thumbnail — and extremely difficult to spot. The dried petals impart a metallic warmth to any dish.

DM Notes

Finding them requires patience and good light — a full-day forage in a Haikyo biome may yield only one or two. Common near Tenku-ji Temple's older stonework.

description.value:
Ryūkinoko 竜茸 (Dragon Fungus)

Category: Kinoko
Rarity: VeryRare
Source: Foraged (Saishū)
Preservation: Fresh 7 days; dries well but loses the shifting flavour; sei charge persists
Tools: Herbalism kit (advantage); sei-sense required to distinguish from deadly mimic
Restrictions: Only grows directly beneath a slumbering Progenitor
Grade: 極上 Gokujō (craft modifier: +5)

A large, golden-capped mushroom found only in caverns directly beneath Progenitor resting sites. The cap is warm to the touch and radiates a faint light in darkness. The flesh carries a flavor that shifts with each bite — savory, then sweet, then something that sits between warmth and music. Those who eat it describe a sensation of profound calm.

DM Notes

**Progenitor-gated.** Only accessible via dragon-slumber caverns. Sei-active; acts as a minor restoration effect when consumed by DM discretion.

items.name: Ryūsō 竜草 (Dragon Herb) (極上 Gokujō)

description.value:
Ryūsō 竜草 (Dragon Herb)

Category: Yakuso
Rarity: VeryRare
Source: Foraged
Preservation: 3 days fresh; cannot be dried without losing properties
Tools: Herbalism kit; ritual knowledge recommended
Restrictions: Cannot be cultivated — transplant kills the plant within hours
Grade: 極上 Gokujō (craft modifier: +5)

A small, leathery-leafed plant found growing directly on the stone of Progenitor shrine sites, its roots apparently drawing sustenance from the rock itself. The leaves are warm to the touch year-round and carry a faint metallic sheen. When consumed, the flavour changes depending on the shrine's associated Progenitor — fiery near Crimson sites, cool and bright near Azure.

DM Notes

Transplanting attempts always fail. The plant draws its properties from the shrine itself — uproot it and the effect dies with the roots. A character with Religion training recognises the ritual significance immediately.

unidentified.name: Unidentified Dragon Herb
unidentified.description: Small leathery leaves clinging to bare stone, warm to the touch regardless of weather, with a faint metallic sheen.

items.name: Sake 酒 (Rice Wine) (極上 Gokujō)

description.value:
Sake 酒 (Rice Wine)

Category: Shushoku
Rarity: Common
Source: Traded (brewed)
Preservation: Sealed flask keeps months; improves with age up to a point
Tools: None
Grade: 極上 Gokujō (craft modifier: +5)

Rice wine sold in small ceramic or bamboo flasks for travel. Drunk cold in summer and warm in winter, sake is also a cornerstone of cooking — a splash in broth, a rinse for fish, a glaze for grilled meat. Common grades are cheap and functional; named breweries command meaningful premiums. Every traveller carries at least a small flask, if only for the warming sip after a hard day's walk.

DM Notes

Social lubricant, cooking ingredient, warming agent.

items.name: Seidō-kōji 青銅麹 (Bronze Mold) (極上 Gokujō)

description.value:
Seidō-kōji 青銅麹 (Bronze Mold)

Category: Chomiryo
Rarity: Rare
Source: Foraged (Saishū) — restricted
Preservation: Active for months in sealed cool vessel
Tools: Herbalism kit (advantage); sterile cloth
Restrictions: Deep Seidōrin Mori is restricted — same legal risk as Seidōrin no Shio
Grade: 極上 Gokujō (craft modifier: +5)

A rare fermentation culture found on fallen bronze-bark in the deepest, dampest reaches of the Seidōrin Mori. The mold itself is a pale green-gold and imparts a unique metallic complexity to whatever it ferments. Used to produce a seasoning paste of extraordinary depth — savory, faintly sweet, with a lingering copper brightness. Harvesting requires entering restricted forest areas.

DM Notes

**Legal risk** as Seidōrin no Shio. Deep forest hazards.

unidentified.description: A pale green-gold mold culture growing inside a damp bronze-bark hollow, faintly metallic in sheen.

description.value:
Seikinoko 精茸 (Sei Mushroom)

Category: Kinoko
Rarity: Rare
Source: Foraged (Saishū)
Preservation: Fades of sei charge within 3 days of picking; dried caps retain flavour but lose resonance
Tools: Herbalism kit (advantage); sei-sense or Arcana (Int) DC 12 to identify active specimens
Grade: 極上 Gokujō (craft modifier: +5)

Luminescent mushrooms found deep within the Yōsei Mori and in caverns with active sei flow. They glow a soft violet-blue and the caps are warm to the touch. The taste is subtle — like forest air after rain — but the sei resonance within them is unmistakable.

DM Notes

Sei-resonant. Ingredients in seimaster brews. Not a common market item — most are handled by shrine suppliers.

items.name: Seirei-taka 精霊鷹 (Spirit Hawk) (極上 Gokujō)

description.value:
Seirei-taka 精霊鷹 (Spirit Hawk)

Category: Niku
Rarity: VeryRare
Source: Hunted
Preservation: 1 day fresh; 7 days salted
Tools: Bow with exceptional skill; the bird is nearly impossible to surprise
Grade: 極上 Gokujō (craft modifier: +5)

The flesh of a hawk that carries visible sei in its feathers and a faint heat in its living body. Eating it is considered a communion — the hunter takes the hawk's keen sight and sharp attention into themselves, briefly. Prepared only by chefs with both cook's utensils training and some form of spiritual authority.

DM Notes

Traditionally, a Seirei-taka kill is offered at a shrine before it is eaten — the shrine blessing is considered part of the preparation. A hunter who eats one without the ritual is said to be marked for misfortune.

unidentified.name: Unidentified Spirit Hawk
unidentified.description: A plucked bird of prey whose flesh carries a faint warmth that does not fade with death. The smell is clean and slightly metallic.

Seireiuo 精霊魚 (Spirit Fish)

Category: Niku
Rarity: Rare
Source: Hunted
Preservation: 1 day fresh; loses most of its properties if preserved
Tools: Fishing tackle; handled with care — the fish is cold to the touch and faintly luminescent
Grade: 極上 Gokujō (craft modifier: +5)

A pale, faintly luminescent fish found only in streams that run through sei-resonant woodland. The flesh carries a subtle warmth on the tongue unrelated to temperature — a sensation closer to a chord of music than a flavour. Favoured by seimasters for ritual meals and by healers as a restorative.

DM Notes

Found in Yōsei Mori streams and at sei-active spring mouths. Handling triggers a faint prickling in the hands of sei-sensitive characters. The fish loses its resonance within a day of dying — delay in cooking is a real loss.

description.value:
Seri 芹 (Water Parsley)

Category: Yakuso
Rarity: Common
Source: Foraged
Preservation: 2 days fresh; loses flavour when dried
Tools: Herbalism kit

Crisp, peppery water parsley found along streams and the margins of rice paddies. One of the very first wild greens to appear in spring — its arrival marks the true turning of the year for village cooks. A common addition to soups and rice dishes throughout the countryside.

A sign of winter's end in paddy country. Abundant in the Tambo and Kawa to Numa of Kusa, Hana, and Tsuchi.

unidentified.description: Slender stems with lace-like leaves, cool and wet from the water it grows in. A sharp green peppery scent.

items.name: Shiitake 椎茸 (Oak Mushroom) (極上 Gokujō)

description.value:
Shiitake 椎茸 (Oak Mushroom)

Category: Kinoko
Rarity: Common
Source: Foraged (Saishū)
Preservation: Dries indefinitely; keeps years when properly stored
Tools: Herbalism kit (advantage); unproficient forager rolls at disadvantage for identification
Grade: 極上 Gokujō (craft modifier: +5)

The universal cooking mushroom of Kagekuni. Broad, dark-brown caps with pale, pleated gills, found in colonies on fallen hardwood throughout Hana, Kusa, and Mizu. The flesh is dense and meaty with a rich umami that deepens when dried. Every travelling cook carries a string of them, and every village market has a basket for sale.

DM Notes

The workhorse mushroom of the Kagekuni pantry. Always in season in some form somewhere; always the safe default for a new forager.

unidentified.name: Unidentified Oak Mushroom
unidentified.description: A brown-capped mushroom with pale, pleated gills, growing from a fallen log in an overlapping colony. The flesh beneath the cap is thick and pale, and the stem is short and fibrous.

items.name: Shika 鹿 (Deer) (極上 Gokujō)

description.value:
Shika 鹿 (Deer)

Category: Niku
Rarity: Common
Source: Hunted
Preservation: 2 days fresh; indefinitely if smoked or salted
Tools: Bow, spear, or polearm; cook's utensils for butchery
Grade: 極上 Gokujō (craft modifier: +5)

Venison from Hokori's forest deer, dark and dense. The shoulder and haunch cuts slow-braise into tenderness; the tenderloin sears quickly and carries a clean iron flavour. Standard game meat throughout the wooded provinces, and the most reliable large-game harvest in the system.

DM Notes

Deer are ubiquitous in Hokori's forested provinces; a sustained hunt over a day will almost always reward a competent hunter. A single carcass yields both venison (Niku) and secondary materials in the Kegawa and Hone categories when fully processed.

unidentified.name: Unidentified Deer
unidentified.description: Dark red slabs of large-game meat, neatly butchered, heavy in the hand. A faint iron scent.

Source: Harvested (Saishū, coastal) or Traded

Harvested from evaporation pools along the Nami and Mizu coasts, or traded inland along the Emperor's Highway. The fundamental seasoning of Kagekuni cooking. Every market in Hokori sells it; every kitchen uses it; every pack contains at least a small cloth pouch.

The baseline seasoning. Travelers without salt are signalled as either destitute, new to the road, or very rich.

description.value:
Shio-take 塩茸 (Salt Stalk)

Category: Kinoko
Rarity: Uncommon
Source: Foraged (Saishū)
Preservation: Stable for months; natural salt crust preserves flesh
Tools: Herbalism kit (advantage); knowledge of tide cycles
Grade: 極上 Gokujō (craft modifier: +5)

A pale, crystalline-crusted mushroom found in coastal caves where seawater seeps through limestone. The natural salt crust makes it unique — it serves as both ingredient and seasoning simultaneously. Nami fishermen use them in chowder-like stews where the salt dissolves into the broth.

DM Notes

Tide-gated harvest — low tide required for access to deeper grottoes. --- **特上 Tokujō — Rare**

unidentified.name: Unidentified Salt Stalk
unidentified.description: A pale fleshy stalk with a visible crust of salt crystals clinging to it, growing from a damp limestone wall in a sea cave.

items.name: Shirokiba no Zui 白牙の髄 (White-Fang Marrow)

description.value:
Shirokiba no Zui 白牙の髄 (White-Fang Marrow)

Category: Niku
Rarity: Rare
Source: One-Time (Yama-no-Ōkami harvest)
Preservation: 4 days if kept cold
Tools: Cook's utensils (marrow extraction and preparation)
Restrictions: One-time only

Rich marrow drawn from the long bones of the forelimbs, pale as bleached bone and dense as cream. Roasted and spread on warm rice it produces an almost overwhelming umami. A cook with cook's utensils proficiency can split one portion across an entire party's meal.

DM Notes

One portion of marrow is enough to season an entire party's meal if spread judiciously. Considered a concentrator ingredient — raises the grade of any dish it is added to.

items.name: Shiso-mi 紫蘇の実 (Perilla Seeds) (極上 Gokujō)

description.value:
Shiso-mi 紫蘇の実 (Perilla Seeds)

Category: Chomiryo
Rarity: Common
Source: Foraged (Saishū)
Preservation: Dried a year or more; often salted for travel
Tools: Herbalism kit (advantage); cloth to catch shaken seeds
Grade: 極上 Gokujō (craft modifier: +5)

The dark, peppery seeds produced by mature perilla plants at the end of summer. Gathered by shaking ripe stalks over a cloth, then dried and cracked between the teeth or ground into a finishing dust. Adds a complex, almost medicinal depth to rice, fish, and pickles. Often mixed with salt for travel.

DM Notes

Travel preservation item; often gifted by rural shokunin. --- **上 Jō — Uncommon**

unidentified.name: Unidentified Perilla Seeds
unidentified.description: Tiny dark seeds caught in a cloth beneath a shaken shiso stalk, releasing a complex herbal aroma.

Category: Yakuso

Source: Foraged
Preservation: 3 days fresh; indefinitely dried (loses some character)

items.name: Sugihiratake 杉平茸 (Cedar Shelf) (極上 Gokujō)

description.value:
Sugihiratake 杉平茸 (Cedar Shelf)

Category: Kinoko
Rarity: Common
Source: Foraged (Saishū)
Preservation: Dries beautifully on strings; keeps for months
Tools: Herbalism kit (advantage)
Grade: 極上 Gokujō (craft modifier: +5)

Pale, fan-shaped mushrooms that grow in dense overlapping shelves on fallen cedar and cypress logs in mountain forests. The flesh is thin but flavourful, with a distinctive resinous note from the wood beneath. Mountain villagers in Sora and Kaze gather them in bulk during damp autumns and dry them in strings beneath the eaves.

DM Notes

The mountain villager's dry-stock mushroom.

unidentified.name: Unidentified Cedar Shelf
unidentified.description: Thin pale fan-shaped shelves overlapping on a fallen cedar log, faint resinous scent rising from the bark beneath.

items.name: Suppon 鼈 (Soft-shell Turtle) (極上 Gokujō)

description.value:
Suppon 鼈 (Soft-shell Turtle)

Category: Niku
Rarity: Uncommon
Source: Hunted
Preservation: Must be kept alive until cooking; prepared meat keeps 2 days
Tools: Traps, spear; cook's utensils essential (dangerous bite)
Grade: 極上 Gokujō (craft modifier: +5)

The flesh of Hokori's soft-shell turtles, prized in medicinal cuisine as a restorative for those who have overspent their strength. Slow-simmered in a clear broth with ginger and sake, the meat yields a mineral depth and a texture somewhere between fish and fowl. Considered a serious meal — not a casual one.

DM Notes

Sold live in markets across the rice provinces. Traditionally prepared for a recovering patient or a warrior before a duel. The bite is genuinely dangerous — handling without care risks a serious wound.

unidentified.name: Unidentified Soft-shell Turtle
unidentified.description: A living dark-green turtle in a shallow water-bucket, its head and neck unusually long, its bite plainly dangerous.

items.name: Suzume 雀 (Sparrow) (極上 Gokujō)

description.value:
Suzume 雀 (Sparrow)

Category: Niku
Rarity: Common
Source: Hunted
Preservation: 1 day fresh; 5 days smoked
Tools: Bird snares, sling; cook's utensils for dressing
Grade: 極上 Gokujō (craft modifier: +5)

Small songbirds netted in cultivated fields and eaves of village houses. The meat is dark and intensely flavoured for its size, traditionally grilled whole on a skewer — head, bones, and all. A peasant's protein, eaten without ceremony.

DM Notes

A village commonplace. Children often hunt them with slings or glue-sticks. Not considered refined food, but ubiquitous and reliable. Abundant near Tambo during rice-harvest season.

unidentified.name: Unidentified Sparrow
unidentified.description: Tiny plucked birds the size of a thumb, arranged on skewers or in a small bundle. Dark reddish flesh, almost all bone.

items.name: Tade 蓼 (Water Pepper) (極上 Gokujō)

description.value:
Tade 蓼 (Water Pepper)

Category: Chomiryo
Rarity: Common
Source: Foraged (Saishū)
Preservation: Fresh 2 days; dried loses most bite
Tools: Herbalism kit (advantage)
Grade: 極上 Gokujō (craft modifier: +5)

A slender, reed-edge herb whose leaves carry a sharp peppery bite — the wild cousin of cultivated spices. Fishermen along the Kinryūgawa use it as a traditional accompaniment to grilled river fish, and its leaves are often pressed onto sashimi as a pungent garnish. Abundant where clear water meets soft mud.

DM Notes

Fisherman's garnish; tie to river-travel encounters.

unidentified.name: Unidentified Water Pepper
unidentified.description: A slender green-leafed herb growing in a muddy stream bank, leaves carrying a sharp pungent tang when crushed.

items.name: Taka-usagi 鷹兎 (Hawk-Hare) (極上 Gokujō)

description.value:
Taka-usagi 鷹兎 (Hawk-Hare)

Category: Niku
Rarity: Uncommon
Source: Hunted
Preservation: 2 days fresh; 14 days salted
Tools: Bow, sling; requires fast shot — snares rarely catch them
Grade: 極上 Gokujō (craft modifier: +5)

The uncommon, long-eared hare of Hokori's open grasslands — larger, faster, and subtly more aromatic than its forest cousin. The meat carries a cleaner, sweeter flavour, and the fat yields a distinctly floral note from a diet of wild herbs. A hunter who takes one boasts for a week.

DM Notes

Natively adapted to the violet grasslands of Kusa and northern Tsuchi. Their speed makes them a prized target for falconers; their meat is a delicacy among rural lords. --- **Rare**

unidentified.name: Unidentified Hawk-Hare
unidentified.description: A large hare, perhaps twice the weight of a mountain cousin, with unusually long ears and a pale cream coat speckled dark.

The uncommon, long-eared hare of Hokori's open grasslands — larger, faster, and subtly more aromatic than its forest cousin. The meat carries a cleaner, sweeter flavour, and the fat yields a distinctly floral note from a diet of wild herbs. A hunter who takes one boasts for a week.

DM Notes

Natively adapted to the violet grasslands of Kusa and northern Tsuchi. Their speed makes them a prized target for falconers; their meat is a delicacy among rural lords. --- **Rare**

unidentified.name: Unidentified Hawk-Hare
unidentified.description: A large hare, perhaps twice the weight of a mountain cousin, with unusually long ears and a pale cream coat speckled dark.

items.name: Takenoko 筍 (Bamboo Shoot) (極上 Gokujō)

description.value:
Takenoko 筍 (Bamboo Shoot)

Category: Yakuso
Rarity: Common
Source: Foraged
Preservation: 3 days fresh; indefinitely pickled
Tools: Herbalism kit; simple blade; cook's utensils for preparation
Grade: 極上 Gokujō (craft modifier: +5)

Young bamboo shoots harvested in spring from the edges of bamboo groves. Must be boiled to remove bitterness before eating. The tender inner flesh is crisp, mildly sweet, and absorbs flavour from whatever it is cooked with. Abundant wherever bamboo grows — which is most of lowland Hokori.

DM Notes

A spring staple in Hana, Kusa, Mizu, and Tsuchi. The short season is a real constraint — a party arriving in summer finds far fewer available.

Rarity: Common
Source: Foraged

Tools: None; cook's utensils for preparation
Grade: 極上 Gokujō (craft modifier: +5)

Dark, palm-sized freshwater snails harvested from rice paddies and slow-moving streams. The meat is earthy, chewy, and carries a bitter-green finish that miso and sake soften into something worth eating. A staple of peasant cuisine in the rice provinces.

Gathered by hand while wading paddies; must be purged in clean water for a day before cooking. Essential ingredient in rural miso-stewed dishes.

items.name: Tanuki-take 狸茸 (Tanuki Mushroom) (極上 Gokujō)

description.value:
Tanuki-take 狸茸 (Tanuki Mushroom)

Category: Kinoko
Rarity: Uncommon
Source: Foraged (Saishū)
Preservation: Dries exceptionally; winter store staple
Tools: Herbalism kit (advantage)
Grade: 極上 Gokujō (craft modifier: +5)

A squat, round-bodied mushroom with a mottled brown cap found in deciduous forests across Kusa and Hana. Named for its resemblance to a sleeping tanuki curled into a ball. The flesh is dense, almost meaty, with a rich umami that intensifies when dried. Forest communities in Kusa preserve them in great quantities for winter stores.

DM Notes

Kusa/Hana cultural staple. Cute-name forage — good flavour for rural NPC recommendations.

items.name: Tennō-mai 天皇米 (Imperial Field Rice) (極上 Gokujō)

description.value:
Tennō-mai 天皇米 (Imperial Field Rice)

Category: Shushoku
Rarity: Rare
Source: Traded (imperial fields)
Preservation: As with kome
Tools: None
Restrictions: **Unauthorized possession technically a punishable offense**, though rarely enforced against recipients of gifts
Grade: 極上 Gokujō (craft modifier: +5)

Rice grown exclusively at a single imperial holding outside Heian, tended by farming families whose lineage predates the current dynasty. Each grain is pearl-white and slightly larger than common rice, cooking into a texture that noble diners describe as "clouds made solid." A single gō (roughly six ounces) is a gift fit for a daimyo. Possession without authorisation is technically a punishable offence, though the law is rarely enforced against those who receive it as a gift.

DM Notes

**Legal risk.** Gift item par excellence.

unidentified.name: Unidentified Imperial Field Rice
unidentified.description: Pearl-white rice grains noticeably larger than common rice, each one flawless.

items.name: Tsuchi-miso 土味噌 (Earth Miso) (極上 Gokujō)

description.value:
Tsuchi-miso 土味噌 (Earth Miso)

Category: Chomiryo
Rarity: Uncommon
Source: Harvested (Saishū, thermal clay)
Preservation: Stable months in clay vessel
Tools: Herbalism kit (advantage); **local guidance essential**
Restrictions: Not all deposits are safe; requires local knowledge to identify non-toxic strains
Grade: 極上 Gokujō (craft modifier: +5)

A wild fermented paste found in clay deposits near certain hot springs in Hi and Tsuchi provinces, where soil bacteria and mineral content produce a natural fermentation in accumulated organic matter. The result is a dark, intensely savory paste — rougher than manufactured miso, but with a depth that cultured products cannot match. Not all deposits are safe to eat — local knowledge is essential.

DM Notes

**Risk flag:** failed identification may yield toxic batch (Con save, poisoned condition for 1 hour).

items.name: Tsuchi-shōga 土生姜 (Earth Ginger) (極上 Gokujō)

description.value:
Tsuchi-shōga 土生姜 (Earth Ginger)

Category: Yakuso
Rarity: Uncommon
Source: Foraged
Preservation: 30 days fresh; indefinitely dried or pickled
Tools: Herbalism kit; simple digging tool
Grade: 極上 Gokujō (craft modifier: +5)

A knotty root found in the mineral-rich soil of Tsuchi province's agricultural valleys. Smaller and more intensely flavoured than cultivated ginger, with a sharp heat and an earthy undertone that reflects the volcanic soil it grows in. Farmers dig it up as a byproduct of plowing and sell it at local markets.

DM Notes

A byproduct of ordinary farming; Tsuchi market stalls sell it for next to nothing, which is part of why nobody outside the province recognises how superior it is. --- **Rare**

unidentified.name: Unidentified Earth Ginger
unidentified.description: Small knotty pale-golden roots, denser and more fibrous than market ginger, with a spicy-earth scent.

description.value:
Tsuchimogura 土藻鱼 (Earth Mole)

Category: Niku
Rarity: Rare
Source: Hunted
Preservation: 2 days fresh; 10 days salted
Tools: Specialized burrow traps; patience more than strength
Grade: 極上 Gokujō (craft modifier: +5)

An unusually large subterranean mammal — dense, short-limbed, and blind — whose meat is prized among farmers and foragers for its rich, dark flavour and the surprising tenderness of its flesh. Hunted with patience rather than force; a single earth mole can feed a small family for several meals.

DM Notes

Traditional prey of rural trappers working grassland and foothill edges. The burrow networks are extensive — a patient hunter sets traps at multiple exits and waits.

items.name: Tsuchimogura 土藻鱼 (Earth Mole) (上 Jō)

description.value:
Tsuchimogura 土藻鱼 (Earth Mole)

Category: Niku
Rarity: Rare
Source: Hunted
Preservation: 2 days fresh; 10 days salted
Tools: Specialized burrow traps; patience more than strength
Grade: 上 Jō (craft modifier: +0)

An unusually large subterranean mammal — dense, short-limbed, and blind — whose meat is prized among farmers and foragers for its rich, dark flavour and the surprising tenderness of its flesh. Hunted with patience rather than force; a single earth mole can feed a small family for several meals.

DM Notes

Traditional prey of rural trappers working grassland and foothill edges. The burrow networks are extensive — a patient hunter sets traps at multiple exits and waits.

items.name: Tsukemono 漬物 (Pickled Vegetables) (極上 Gokujō)

description.value:
Tsukemono 漬物 (Pickled Vegetables)

Category: Shushoku
Rarity: Common
Source: Traded (home-pickled)
Preservation: Keeps weeks to months in sealed vessel
Tools: None
Grade: 極上 Gokujō (craft modifier: +5)

An assortment of root vegetables, daikon, gourd, and leafy greens pickled in salt, vinegar, miso, or rice bran mash. Every region has its own tradition — Hi's fiery pepper pickles differ utterly from Sora's delicate salt-pickled turnip. Tsukemono keeps well on the road and adds colour, crunch, and acidity to otherwise monotonous trail meals.

DM Notes

Regional flavor — grade reflects provincial tradition.

items.name: Tsukimisō 月見草 (Moon-Viewing Herb) (極上 Gokujō)

description.value:
Tsukimisō 月見草 (Moon-Viewing Herb)

Category: Yakuso
Rarity: Uncommon
Source: Foraged
Preservation: 3 days fresh; indefinitely dried
Tools: Herbalism kit; light source managed to avoid spoiling petals
Restrictions: Harvested at night; petals close at dawn
Grade: 極上 Gokujō (craft modifier: +5)

Pale silver flowers that open only at night, found on high ground in Sora and along the ridgelines of Hana's mountains. The petals, dried and crumbled, produce a mild calming effect. Traditionally served as a tea before important negotiations.

DM Notes

Tsukimisō tea is part of the informal diplomatic vocabulary of the mountain courts. A cup served at the start of a talk is a signal that the host intends calm discussion.

unidentified.name: Unidentified Moon-Viewing Herb
unidentified.description: Pale silvery-white flowers with four broad petals, cool to the touch and faintly fragrant in moonlight.

items.name: Tsukiyo-take 月夜茸 (Moonlit Cap) (極上 Gokujō)

description.value:
Tsukiyo-take 月夜茸 (Moonlit Cap)

Category: Kinoko
Rarity: Rare
Source: Foraged (Saishū)
Preservation: Fresh 1 day only — silver light fades within hours; dried retains only faint effect
Tools: Herbalism kit (advantage); **full Kagetsu moon required**
Restrictions: Can only be gathered on nights when Kagetsu is full
Grade: 極上 Gokujō (craft modifier: +5)

A pale, luminescent mushroom found on deadwood in high-altitude forests during nights when Kagetsu is full. The cap glows with a soft silver light that fades within hours of picking. The flavor is elusive — dreamlike is the word most often used, though no one can articulate what that means. Some who eat them report unusually vivid dreams during the following rest.

DM Notes

Lunar gating — tie to Kagetsu full phases on the calendar. Consumption during long rest may grant prophecy/dream hooks at DM discretion.

unidentified.name: Unidentified Moonlit Cap
unidentified.description: A pale cap on deadwood emitting a soft silver glow under the full moon. The light begins to fade the moment it is picked.

items.name: Udon & Soba うどん・蕎麦 (Wheat & Buckwheat Noodles) (極上 Gokujō)

description.value:
Udon & Soba うどん・蕎麦 (Wheat & Buckwheat Noodles)

Category: Shushoku
Rarity: Common
Source: Traded (milled & cut)
Preservation: Dried weeks to months
Tools: None
Grade: 極上 Gokujō (craft modifier: +5)

Dried wheat noodles (udon) and buckwheat noodles (soba), sold in paper-wrapped bundles. Keep for weeks, cook in minutes. Soba is the mountain food — buckwheat grows where wheat cannot — while udon is the lowland staple, favoured for its softness and the way it holds a rich broth. A traveller of any province recognises both and knows when to carry which.

DM Notes

Two regional subvariants — DM chooses which by province.

unidentified.name: Unidentified Wheat & Buckwheat Noodles
unidentified.description: A paper-wrapped bundle of long, dried noodle strands — some thick and pale (udon), some thin and grey-brown (soba).

items.name: Umeboshi 梅干し (Pickled Plum) (極上 Gokujō)

description.value:
Umeboshi 梅干し (Pickled Plum)

Category: Shushoku
Rarity: Common
Source: Traded (home-cured)
Preservation: Years in sealed jar; often generations
Tools: None
Grade: 極上 Gokujō (craft modifier: +5)

Small, intensely salty-sour plums pickled in salt and red shiso leaves, wrapped individually in leaf or stored in small jars. A single umeboshi sharpens a bowl of plain rice, and travellers swear the fruit wards off road sickness, fevers, and ill intentions. Keeps for years — many households preserve the same crock across generations.

DM Notes

Folk-remedy for fever, road-sickness, ill intentions. Good to hand to players at long rests.

unidentified.name: Unidentified Pickled Plum
unidentified.description: A small shriveled red plum wrapped in shiso leaf, intensely salty-sour to taste.

items.name: Umi-shio 海塩 (Deep Sea Salt) (極上 Gokujō)

description.value:
Umi-shio 海塩 (Deep Sea Salt)

Category: Chomiryo
Rarity: Uncommon
Source: Harvested (Saishū, coastal)
Preservation: Indefinite; mineral-stable
Tools: Knife or small pick; tide knowledge
Grade: 極上 Gokujō (craft modifier: +5)

Coarse, grey-blue salt crystals harvested from deep tidal caves along Nami's coastline, where centuries of seawater evaporation have left mineral-rich deposits on cave walls. The flavor is more complex than ordinary sea salt — briny, faintly bitter, with a mineral depth that ordinary salt lacks. Nami fishermen consider it essential for proper fish curing.

DM Notes

Tide-dependent harvest.

unidentified.name: Unidentified Deep Sea Salt
unidentified.description: Coarse, grey-blue crystalline deposits scraped from the wet walls of a deep sea cave.

Category: Yakuso
Rarity: Uncommon
Source: Foraged
Preservation: 3 days fresh; indefinitely salt-pickled
Tools: Herbalism kit; climbing gear sometimes required
Grade: 極上 Gokujō (craft modifier: +5)

A thick-leafed coastal plant that grows on cliff faces and rocky shorelines where the salt spray is constant. The leaves are succulent, salty, and faintly bitter — eaten raw they taste of the sea. Nami fishermen chew them during long watches. Used in cooking to add a briny depth without additional salt.

DM Notes

A reliable source of salt-flavour for travelers without access to purchased seasonings.

A reliable source of salt-flavour for travelers without access to purchased seasonings.

items.name: Unagi 鰻 (Freshwater Eel) (極上 Gokujō)

description.value:
Unagi 鰻 (Freshwater Eel)

Category: Niku
Rarity: Uncommon
Source: Hunted
Preservation: 1 day fresh; cooked eel keeps 2 days
Tools: Traps, fishing tackle with specialized hooks; cook's utensils essential for butchering
Grade: 極上 Gokujō (craft modifier: +5)

Long, dark eels pulled from slow rivers and river-mouth estuaries. The flesh is rich with fat, almost buttery, and requires expert butchery to prepare properly — the spine must be pinned and the fillets drawn in long clean cuts. Grilled over coals and basted with a sweet soy glaze, it is one of the great summer indulgences in Kagekuni.

DM Notes

Traditional hashing — pinning the spine, drawing the fillets, removing the skin — requires trained hands. A cook without cook's utensils proficiency gets a rough, partially-ruined yield. Summer eel is strongest in flavour; autumn eel is fatter.

unidentified.name: Unidentified Freshwater Eel
unidentified.description: A long, dark, snake-like fish the length of an arm, slick and strong even after killing. A faint river-bottom scent.

items.name: Uzura 鶉 (Quail) (極上 Gokujō)

description.value:
Uzura 鶉 (Quail)

Category: Niku
Rarity: Common
Source: Hunted
Preservation: 2 days fresh; 10 days smoked
Tools: Bow, sling, or snares; cook's utensils for dressing
Grade: 極上 Gokujō (craft modifier: +5)

Small ground-dwelling birds hunted in grasslands, scrub, and the margins of cultivated fields. The meat is darker than chicken and carries a slightly mineral sweetness — perfect for a single-skewer meal over a cooking fire.

DM Notes

Abundant in grasslands and scrub. Often driven into nets by beaters; rural households maintain standing snare lines near paddy margins during harvest season.

unidentified.name: Unidentified Quail
unidentified.description: Small plucked game birds, each no larger than a fist, with pale-to-rose flesh and tiny bones. Faint scent of grass and warm feathers.

items.name: Warabi 蕨 (Bracken Fern) (極上 Gokujō)

description.value:
Warabi 蕨 (Bracken Fern)

Category: Yakuso
Rarity: Common
Source: Foraged
Preservation: 2 days fresh; indefinitely dried after ash-water treatment
Tools: Herbalism kit; cook's utensils for preparation
Grade: 極上 Gokujō (craft modifier: +5)

Young fiddlehead ferns harvested in early spring from forest floors and shaded hillsides. Must be soaked overnight in wood ash water to remove bitterness before eating — raw warabi is genuinely unpleasant. A staple wild green across the archipelago; gathering warabi is one of the first foraging skills every village child learns.

DM Notes

Ash-water treatment is non-optional — eaten raw, it causes digestive discomfort. A character with herbalism proficiency knows this automatically.

unidentified.name: Unidentified Bracken Fern
unidentified.description: Tightly coiled fern heads no larger than a fist, pale green and downy, still cool from the forest floor.

items.name: Wasabi 山葵 (Mountain Horseradish) (極上 Gokujō)

description.value:
Wasabi 山葵 (Mountain Horseradish)

Category: Chomiryo
Rarity: Common
Source: Foraged (Saishū)
Preservation: Fresh root 1–2 weeks in cold water; grated paste must be used same day
Tools: Herbalism kit (advantage); small digging knife
Grade: 極上 Gokujō (craft modifier: +5)

Found wild along cool, shaded streams in the mountains. The root is grated fresh for a sharp, sinus-clearing heat. Cultivated near Ayame and in Kaze's valleys, but the wild specimens are said to carry a cleaner, brighter bite.

DM Notes

Prime wasabi is an Ayame economic lever.

unidentified.name: Unidentified Mountain Horseradish
unidentified.description: A knobbly green root pulled from a cold, clear mountain stream bed, fibrous and firm.

items.name: Wasanbon 和三盆 (Refined Sugar) (極上 Gokujō)

description.value:
Wasanbon 和三盆 (Refined Sugar)

Category: Shushoku
Rarity: Uncommon
Source: Traded (hand-refined)
Preservation: Years in sealed paper packet; humidity destroys it
Tools: None
Grade: 極上 Gokujō (craft modifier: +5)

Pale, extraordinarily fine sugar refined in small village cooperatives of southern Hana and Kusa, where the specific microclimate allows for the slow, patient crystallisation the product demands. Used sparingly in sweets, ceremonial confections, and the glaze of refined dishes. A luxury to most peasant households — a small paper packet of wasanbon is considered a generous gift to a host.

DM Notes

Gift-worthy item for noble social encounters.

unidentified.name: Unidentified Refined Sugar
unidentified.description: A fine pale powder-like sugar in a paper packet, almost floury to touch.

items.name: Yama no Kimo 山の肝 (Mountain Liver)

description.value:
Yama no Kimo 山の肝 (Mountain Liver)

Category: Niku
Rarity: Rare
Source: One-Time (Yama-no-Ōkami harvest)
Preservation: 1 day fresh; 7 days salted or smoked
Tools: Cook's utensils (precise preparation)
Restrictions: One-time only

A dark, fist-sized organ still faintly warm when pulled from the body cavity. Traditional mountain cooks consider this the single finest organ meat in Hokori — it carries a trace of the creature's essence, and eating it is said to sharpen the nerve and steady the breath. Suitable for a Refined dish.

DM Notes

Eating the liver grants Refined-tier buffs in the cooking system. Mountain hunters hold a loose tradition of offering the first cut of such a liver to a senior hunter or village elder.

unidentified.name: Unidentified Mountain Liver
unidentified.description: A heavy dark-red organ the size of a clenched fist, still warm to the touch and faintly pulsing when first handled.

items.name: Yama-usagi 山兎 (Mountain Hare) (極上 Gokujō)

description.value:
Yama-usagi 山兎 (Mountain Hare)

Category: Niku
Rarity: Common
Source: Hunted
Preservation: 2 days fresh; 14 days smoked or salted
Tools: Simple weapons or snares; cook's utensils for butchering
Grade: 極上 Gokujō (craft modifier: +5)

Lean, dark-rose meat from the wild hares that populate Hokori's lower forests and upland meadows. The flavour is clean and faintly grassy — not gamey, not strong, but distinctly wild. A single hare feeds two travellers well with rice.

DM Notes

Common throughout Hokori's forested provinces. Hunters set snares along known game trails in lower Fumoto and within any Satoyama. A Wisdom (Survival) check with trapper's tools yields the best results; bow hunting works at higher cost in time.

unidentified.name: Unidentified Mountain Hare
unidentified.description: A field-dressed small mammal, perhaps four to six pounds, pale rose flesh with darker muscle striping along the haunches. The smell is faint — clean meat, a trace of woodland soil.

Category: Niku
Rarity: Common
Source: Hunted
Preservation: 2 days fresh; 14 days hung and salted
Tools: Bow or snares; cook's utensils for dressing
Grade: 極上 Gokujō (craft modifier: +5)

The copper-barred pheasants of Hokori's forested hills. Larger and richer than quail, with a deep-red breast meat that benefits from slow cooking or the sharp bright heat of the grill. A proud bird, hunted by lords as often as peasants.

A favoured game bird of samurai hunters and a good meal for a road-weary party. Best taken at dawn along forest edges.

unidentified.description: A dressed game bird perhaps two feet long from neck stump to rump, dark meat under pale skin, a few copper-coloured feathers still clinging where the plucker missed.

The copper-barred pheasants of Hokori's forested hills. Larger and richer than quail, with a deep-red breast meat that benefits from slow cooking or the sharp bright heat of the grill. A proud bird, hunted by lords as often as peasants.

A favoured game bird of samurai hunters and a good meal for a road-weary party. Best taken at dawn along forest edges.

items.name: Yomi-take 黄泉茸 (Underworld Cap) (極上 Gokujō)

description.value:
Yomi-take 黄泉茸 (Underworld Cap)

Category: Kinoko
Rarity: VeryRare
Source: Foraged (Saishū)
Preservation: Stable in absolute darkness; decays rapidly in any light
Tools: Herbalism kit (advantage); Arcana (Int) DC 15 to handle safely
Restrictions: Found only in places that have not seen light in geological time
Grade: 極上 Gokujō (craft modifier: +5)

A pitch-black mushroom found in the deepest accessible caverns of Kagekuni — places where no light has reached in geological time. The cap absorbs light rather than reflecting it, creating a visual absence that is disorienting to look at directly. The flavor is the densest umami imaginable — concentrated essence of earth and darkness. Herbalists and seimasters debate whether it should be classified as a fungus at all.

DM Notes

**Classification unresolved.** Consumption is a DM-discretion event — may have sei effects, may simply be the purest umami in Kagekuni. Often tied to deep-dungeon reward.

unidentified.name: Unidentified Underworld Cap
unidentified.description: A cap so black that it seems to be a hole in the world; the eye slides off it and cannot focus on its edge.

description.value:
Yomogi 蓬 (Mugwort)

Category: Yakuso
Rarity: Common
Source: Foraged
Preservation: 5 days fresh; indefinitely dried
Tools: Herbalism kit
Grade: 極上 Gokujō (craft modifier: +5)

A tough, aromatic herb with silvery-green leaves found along roadsides and disturbed ground throughout Hokori. Bitter when raw, but blanched and pounded into rice cakes it produces the distinctive green kusamochi sold at every festival. Also burned as a smudge to repel insects at camp.

DM Notes

Kusamochi is a festival ubiquity — any roadside stall during spring festivals will be selling it. A traveller with yomogi can also make a reasonable mosquito smudge with a small fire.

items.name: Yūgure-su 夕暮れ酢 (Twilight Vinegar) (極上 Gokujō)

description.value:
Yūgure-su 夕暮れ酢 (Twilight Vinegar)

Category: Chomiryo
Rarity: Rare
Source: Foraged (Saishū)
Preservation: Stable for years
Tools: Herbalism kit (advantage); patience — trees are uncooperative
Grade: 極上 Gokujō (craft modifier: +5)

A deep amber liquid that collects in hollows of ancient hardwood trees in the Yōsei Mori, where sei activity and slow fermentation of tree sap produce a vinegar of remarkable complexity. The flavor carries notes of autumn leaves, honey, and something that suggests distance — like a memory of a taste rather than the taste itself. The trees that produce it are centuries old and cannot be cultivated.

DM Notes

Sei-active byproduct. Tied to Yōsei Mori respect rituals. --- **極上 Gokujō — Very Rare**

unidentified.name: Unidentified Twilight Vinegar

items.name: Yuki-kiji 雪雉 (Snow Pheasant) (極上 Gokujō)

description.value:
Yuki-kiji 雪雉 (Snow Pheasant)

Category: Niku
Rarity: Uncommon
Source: Hunted
Preservation: 2 days fresh; 14 days hung
Tools: Bow; traps suffer in deep snow
Grade: 極上 Gokujō (craft modifier: +5)

The white-winter pheasant of the high peaks, nearly invisible against fresh snow. The breast meat is pale and dense, with a subtle herbal aftertaste from the alpine browse of berries and conifer shoots. Mountain villages consider a snow-pheasant kill a mark of hunting skill.

DM Notes

Hunted in winter above the tree line. A successful kill is a village story. Best taken with bow — the bird's white camouflage makes snare work unreliable.

unidentified.name: Unidentified Snow Pheasant
unidentified.description: A plucked white-skinned game bird with pale, almost ivory flesh. Cold to the touch even hours after killing.

items.name: Yūrei-kusa 幽霊草 (Ghost Grass) (極上 Gokujō)

description.value:
Yūrei-kusa 幽霊草 (Ghost Grass)

Category: Yakuso
Rarity: Rare
Source: Foraged
Preservation: 14 days fresh; indefinitely dried
Tools: Herbalism kit
Grade: 極上 Gokujō (craft modifier: +5)

A pale, almost transparent grass that grows in the shadow of ancient ruins and abandoned settlements — particularly around Tsukikage in Kaze province. It sways without wind and is cold to the touch even in summer. When brewed as a tea, it produces a heightened awareness of one's surroundings that borders on unsettling. Some drinkers report hearing whispers.

DM Notes

A particularly good candidate for Tenku-ji Temple foraging. Tea from yūrei-kusa grants perception advantages but causes unsettling sensations — DM may choose to impose minor morale checks for prolonged use.

unidentified.name: Unidentified Ghost Grass
unidentified.description: Pale translucent grass that moves slightly without any apparent breeze, cool to the touch in any weather.

Type
settlement

"The village that keeps secrets the way stone keeps cold -- completely and without effort."

Overview

Akatsuki -- Dawn -- is a village whose name contradicts its character. It sits in perpetual shadow from the peaks above it, reached by a winding stone path gaining significant altitude. The air is cold even in summer. Mist collects in the surrounding terrain and rarely lifts before midday, often not at all.

The village is modest -- terraced farming on steep slopes, stone-built houses with heavy roofs designed for snow load, a central well, a small shrine. Residents are not hostile but are compact -- words measured carefully, questions answered with just enough to satisfy without offering more. They have maintained this posture for generations because they live below the Monastery of the Black Lily.

Above the village, higher on the mountainside and accessed by a stone staircase cut into the rock face, stands the Monastery of the Black Lily.

Districts / Landmarks

The Monastery of the Black Lily -- Dark stone and iron construction; austere; functional rather than beautiful. The Order of the Black Lily operates here -- Kagekuni's premier training facility for infiltration specialists, covert intelligence operatives, and precision agents.

The Order's relationship with Clan Gekko was long and close. The disappearance of Clan Gekko has severed the primary institutional support structure. They are reassessing.

The monks and initiates know the truth about the Nagaji transformation. They have made a calculated decision to not release this information without a reversal plan. They will share the complete truth with parties who demonstrate they are positioned to actually address the situation.

Key Figures

None publicly documented. The village maintains deliberate anonymity.

• The Order of the Black Lily knows what happened to Clan Gekko and will share the truth with those who can demonstrate they are positioned to act.
  • The village is not simply a bystander community -- it functions as a support system for the monastery.

DM Secrets

The Order's Full Knowledge The Order knows: what ritual was used, who performed it first, approximately how many Gekko clan members were transformed, and that Masota no Gekko himself underwent the ritual. They do not know where Masota currently is. The transformed Gekko move in patterns that even their surveillance cannot consistently track.

The Reversal The Order has determined a reversal exists -- theoretical, not practical. It requires three elements: the original ritual documentation (in Kinkokyo, in the Golden Dragon Clan's records); a specific sei configuration present only during a particular celestial alignment (upcoming, within the next few sessions); and a practitioner capable of performing sei-based restoration at significant scale.

What the Order Wants from the Party The Order will propose a partnership: the party retrieves the reversal documentation from the Temple of Kinryu; the Order handles logistics of gathering the transformed Gekko; together they manage the political revelation on a controlled timeline. In exchange, the Order provides intelligence, resources, and full knowledge of the Gekko situation.

The Village's Role Several former Order members have retired to the village. Two of the village's farmers are active deep-cover agents between assignments. Visitors who threaten this arrangement will encounter more than agricultural resistance.

Plot Hooks

  • A message from the Order reaches the party: "Come to Akatsuki. Complete information will be provided. Bring nothing official."
  • The Order has been watching the party since the mountain pass and wants to know what was found beyond the gold doors
  • An Order initiate has broken protocol and is heading toward Heian with partial information -- needs intercepting before triggering political consequences

Type
settlement

"Everyone coming or going through the mountains passes through Ayame. Everyone."

Overview

Ayame occupies the valley at the base of the Tenchusan Ren pass -- the primary land route between Hana's southern lowlands and the northern provinces. Everything that travels overland between these regions passes through Ayame. This geographic chokepoint function defines the town's character: it is less a community than a transit organism.

The town is organized around the pass road. The main thoroughfare runs straight through parallel to the Kinryugawa, broadening into a market square at the center. Secondary streets branch off at intervals -- accommodation, services, and residential areas spreading outward in concentric zones of decreasing formality.

The military overseer structure means Ayame is administered by appointed officials with military backgrounds. This produces efficient governance but can feel impersonal; permanent residents are pragmatic people who work with whoever is in charge.

Districts / Landmarks

Chuo-ku (Central District) -- Main thoroughfare and market square. Most commercial activity. The Marketplace operates daily.

Tenchusan Chiku (Mountain District) -- The approach zone toward the pass. Stables, equipment rental, guide services, outfitter shops. Increasingly sparse toward the pass entrance.

Notable Establishments

The Marketplace -- Permanent covered market stalls along the main street. Serves local needs and traveler provisioning. Prices reflect the captive market.

Blacksmith's Forge -- Military-grade equipment maintenance and standard smithing. Works in cooperation with the garrison.

Weaver's Shop -- Mountain-weight textiles and cold-weather clothing. Genuinely excellent; mountain gear quality is a survival matter.

Kawabe no Tengaku (Riverside Haven) -- Inn along the river approach. Quieter; favored by travelers wanting rest over socialization.

Kin no Chochin Ryokan (Golden Lantern Inn) -- Main waypoint inn on the central street. Busy, efficient, well-run. The party stayed here during their Ayame transit.

Ryu no Yasuragi Yado (Dragon's Rest Lodge) -- Secondary inn; the party stayed here after the wagon impoundment situation. Slightly more modest.

Ayame Temple -- Small temple in the residential quarter. Patron deity is a traveling spirit protector. Resident monk maintains the shrine to the pass spirits.

Key Figures

  • Takeda Yoshinobu -- Town leader; competent administrator -> npcs/takeda-yoshinobu.md
  • Chief Inspector Oshiro Masahiro -- Teikoku Keisatsu; confirmed party ally -> npcs/oshiro-masahiro.md

• Oshiro Masahiro's intelligence network extends far beyond what his official position suggests.
  • The Tenchusan Ren pass approach is under more surveillance than it appears.
  • Mountain guides have been returning from upper-route jobs shaken and unwilling to specify what they saw.

DM Secrets

Oshiro Masahiro -- Intelligence Asset Oshiro's decision to assist the party was not simply a judgment about innocence. He had received information suggesting their mission was legitimate and the impoundment was creating an obstacle. He knows more about the Gekko situation than he has shared. He is a potential ongoing intelligence ally.

The Pass Road -- Surveillance The pass approach is watched more carefully than it appears. Oshiro has informants at both the waypoint inn and the outfitter district who log significant travelers and goods movements. The network also detected a group with no identifiable clan affiliation, moving fast and carrying unusual cargo, approximately three weeks before the party's transit.

Takeda Yoshinobu's Concerns Yoshinobu has been receiving reports from mountain guides about unusual activity in the upper pass -- disrupted trail markers, signs of large encampment at non-standard locations, and two guides who came back shaken and unwilling to specify what they saw. He has not reported upward because he has no official channels he trusts.

Plot Hooks

  • Oshiro sends a discrete message: he has information relevant to the party's mission that he couldn't share safely in Ayame; proposes a meeting at the next Michibata up the pass
  • One of the mountain guides who returned early is drinking heavily at the Dragon's Rest and muttering fragments of what they saw
