The structural spine of the first floor — a N-S corridor from the South Entrance meeting an E-W corridor that connects all wings.

Physical Description:

N-S Corridor: 20 ft wide, connecting the South Entrance's tapered northern end to the Grand Hall's double double-doors. Stone walls, unadorned — functional architecture, not ceremonial. The transition from the South Entrance's vaulted height to this corridor's lower ceiling is abrupt. The Grand Hall doors are visible from the corridor's southern end.

Center Intersection (20 ft × 20 ft): Where the N-S and E-W corridors meet. A squared junction with sight lines extending in all four cardinal directions. The floor here is worn smooth — more traffic passed through this point than any other in the temple. Faint grooves in the stone suggest centuries of foot traffic, carts, and ritual procession.

E-W Corridor: 20 ft wide, extending approximately 120 ft in each direction from the center intersection.

  • West wing: Star Shrine hallway branches north at the far end (10 ft wide, 60 ft long). Mess Hall L-shaped hallway branches south at the far end. Stairs upward to the second floor at 45 ft west of center (north side). Stairs downward to the lower level at 45 ft west of center (south side).

  • East wing: Dormitory entrances on both sides at the far end — north side accessible, south side entrance collapsed (rubble blocks passage; dormitory beyond intact). Stairs upward to the second floor at 45 ft east of center.

Lighting: Dark. No sconces in the corridors — the South Entrance's magical torches end at the taper. Whatever light reaches the hallways comes from adjacent rooms or what the party carries.

Atmosphere: The corridors carry sound efficiently. Footsteps echo along the long axes. The center intersection amplifies this — sound from any wing reaches the center. A party moving without care can be heard from 60+ feet away.

Discoveries

  • Traffic patterns in the stone (DC 12 Investigation or Survival)
  • Stair conditions — up and down

Traffic Patterns: The wear in the stone tells a story. The heaviest traffic ran N-S (South Entrance to Grand Hall) — the primary processional route. The E-W corridor shows lighter but consistent wear toward both wings. Near the stairs, the stone is more worn on the western side than the eastern, suggesting the order's daily life centered more on the Star Shrine and Mess Hall side than the dormitory side. DC 12 Investigation or Survival to read the pattern.

The Stairs:

Stairs down (45 ft west of center, south side of E-W hallway): Stone steps descending into darkness. Air from below is warmer and carries a faint mineral dampness — different from the dry cold of the first floor. The steps are intact but dust-covered. Recent tracks in the dust: Nagaji. This is their route to and from the lower levels.

Stairs up — west (45 ft west of center, north side of E-W hallway): Stone steps ascending. Dust undisturbed — the Nagaji have not gone up. Whatever is on the second floor, they either cannot reach it or have not tried.

Stairs up — east (45 ft east of center): Stone steps ascending. Also undisturbed. A second route to the upper level, positioned near the dormitory wing.

Encounters

(No dedicated encounters in the hallway. Patrol Nagaji from the Grand Hall use this space as a transit route. The center intersection is a likely meeting point if the party moves noisily.)

DM Notes

Tactical Significance: The center intersection is the single most important control point on the first floor. A party that holds the intersection controls access to every wing. Conversely, enemies at the intersection can cut the party off from rooms they've already cleared. The 20 ft width allows two-abreast combat but not flanking without entering a side corridor.

The Nagaji Route: The stairs down (west, south side) are the Nagaji's primary transit path. Their tracks are visible in the dust. The stairs up show no such traffic — the second floor appears to be outside their patrol pattern. This is a meaningful detail: whatever drove the Nagaji to occupy the first floor and the levels below, the upper floor was either inaccessible to them or not worth their attention.

Sound Propagation: The corridors amplify sound. A fight at the center intersection can be heard from the South Entrance, the Grand Hall doors, and partway down both wings. This matters for encounter pacing — combat here draws attention from adjacent areas.

Type
location
Status
active

East wing — a long corridor with cells branching left and right, plus larger shared quarters at the north and south ends.

Read-aloud text: ../supplements/read-aloud-floor-1.md § Dormitories

Physical Description:

East wing, 120 ft from center intersection. Dormitory complex connects to both the north and south sides of the E-W hallway. Colder than the Grand Hall — an unnatural cold associated with accumulated violence, not mountain temperature.

North-side dormitory (accessible): Long corridor, two-person width, with eight individual cells — four west (Cells 1, 3, 5, 7), four east (Cells 2, 4, 6, 8). Most doors forced open — frames splintered inward or outward, some bearing edged-weapon scoring at shoulder height.

South-side dormitory (entrance collapsed): The entrance from the E-W hallway was deliberately collapsed by the priests during the fall. Rubble blocks the passage. The dormitory beyond is intact but inaccessible from this side. Access requires clearing rubble (hours; loud) or an alternate route via second floor or cavern system below.

Sealed room (Senior Priests' Quarters): Heavy wooden door, barred from inside; bar visible through gap at base. Beyond: 20 ft × 20 ft; four sleeping platforms, each occupied by skeletal remains. Remains are deliberate — hands folded, bodies oriented toward room's center. They chose this. On the writing desk: scroll case (Last Record of Priest Tomohiro) + bronze disc — left in plain sight, meant to be found.

Cell Layout

Cell Side Notable Feature Onryō
1 West Faded star chart drawings on wall Yes
2 East Single intact ceramic cup, upright, perfectly centered on shelf Yes
3 West Starburst damage — scorched walls, cracked floor, platform obliterated Yes — most volatile
4 East Personal effects scattered; sandal near doorway as if left mid-step Yes
5 West Swept clean — deliberately tidied after the fall; platform scrape marks No
6 East Nagaji-searched — contents pulled, platform overturned No
7 West Small devotional Kinryū carving still upright on shelf No
8 East Door frame scorched — caught edge of Cell 3 discharge No

Discoveries

  • Cell 3 — Starburst Damage (DC 14 Arcana; DC 17 Arcana for reconstruction)
  • Cell 5 — Swept Clean (intentionally unresolved)
  • Cell 6 — Planetary Gear Assembly (DC 13 Investigation) (Observatory component #2)
  • The Sealed Room — Priest Tomohiro's remains (DC 12 Thieves' Tools to open scroll case) (Handout: Last Record of Priest Tomohiro)
  • The Bronze Disc — orbital engravings (DC 13 Investigation) (Observatory component: calibration disc)
  • Evidence of the Nagaji — searched cells

Cell 3 — Starburst Damage

  • DC 14 Arcana: identifies sei discharge as cause — magical energy released suddenly without control
  • DC 17 Arcana: reconstructs the attempt — a priest tried to weaponize their own sei reserves in a single concentrated release against something already in the corridor; discharge was too large and uncontrolled; killed the priest and damaged Cell 8 through the shared wall

Cell 5 — Swept Clean

Someone tidied this cell after the fall — older than the Nagaji's arrival. Platform moved deliberately, replaced; nothing beneath it now. Intentionally unresolved — possible connection to Tomohiro.

Cell 6 — Nagaji-Searched / Planetary Gear Assembly

DC 13 Investigation locates the planetary gear assembly — seven interlocking bronze rings of graduated size, partially disassembled, discarded in debris under overturned platform. The rings are nested concentrically, each engraved with tiny orbital notations in Old Imperial. The outermost ring is bent but not broken. A character proficient in Tinker's Tools, Smith's Tools, or Navigator's Tools recognizes this as a precision gear mechanism — a planetary drive designed to model multiple simultaneous orbital periods through a single input rotation. DC 14 History (DC 11 for Ko'jiri) connects the orbital notations to the seven known planets of the Miyosai system. (Observatory component: planetary gear assembly. The Nagaji found it, examined it, could not understand it, and discarded it.)

The Sealed Room — Senior Priests' Quarters

The priests who sealed themselves in were not hiding — they were staying. They had made their peace and chose not to participate in the violence. Four sleeping platforms, each occupied by skeletal remains — hands folded, bodies oriented toward the room's center. The sealed room has been untouched since their death.

Breaking the door: AC 15, 40 HP. Alternatively, the bar can be lifted through the gap at the base (DC 12 Thieves' Tools or Dexterity check).

On the writing desk: The scroll case (DC 12 Thieves' Tools or carefully broken open) contains a last account — a personal record of the final days, from Priest Tomohiro's perspective. This is a major handout (see Handout: The Last Record of Priest Tomohiro) detailing how the infiltrators were discovered too late, who gave the order to seal the inner sanctum, and the name of the head infiltrator — a detail that, with a DC 17 History check, connects to a lineage that still exists in present-day Kagekuni.

The bronze disc is a formal order seal, granting the bearer recognition as a member of the Golden Dragon order — useful as a key within the temple for certain sealed areas (specifically the Jushoku no Ma hidden door).

The Bronze Disc — Additional Detail: The reverse face of the disc bears fine engravings invisible without close examination (DC 13 Investigation or automatic if studying the disc under good light). Concentric rings scored into the bronze correspond to orbital tracks, with seven small notches along the outer edge and four along an inner ring. A character who has found the planetary gear assembly recognizes the match immediately — the disc is designed to seat into a mechanical device as a positional reference. (Observatory component: calibration disc. When seated in the orrery's control interface, it establishes the reference date from which the mechanism can advance or rewind. The order seal and calibration key were the same object — the person authorized to operate the observatory was, by definition, a member of the order.)

Evidence of the Nagaji

Two of the individual cells (including Cell 6) show recent disturbance — the dust displaced, a pallet dragged aside to reveal the floor. The Nagaji have been searching these rooms. What they were looking for is unclear, but the cells they searched belonged (per the scroll case record) to the two most senior non-priest scholars of the order. Whatever those scholars possessed or knew, something is looking for it.

Encounters

  • 4 Uragiri no Onryō (裏切りの怨霊 — "Vengeful Spirits of Betrayal"; Specters, MM p.279 — Cells 1, 2, 3, 4)

Uragiri no Onryō — Trigger and Escalation

Corrupted priests who were the infiltrating force that destroyed the order from within. Named to reflect the specific sin that defines them — not just evil, but betrayers of the order they swore to serve. Each haunts a specific cell — emerge when the corridor is disturbed.

Trigger: Corridor disturbed (loud noise, running, light brought close to an occupied cell, combat vibration from elsewhere in the temple)

Initial state: Confused and territorial — emerge from cells, move erratically, cannot fully perceive the party. Window of non-hostility.

Escalation to hostility: Party attacks any of the four, OR the sealed room is interfered with disrespectfully (forcing door loudly, attempting to break it).

Respectful entry (picking the bar, asking permission aloud, moving quietly) does not trigger escalation.

Cell 3 spirit: Manifests first if party lingers near Cell 3 without triggering combat. Most volatile. Use Specter (MM p.279) with maximum HP and one additional action option.

De-escalation: A character who speaks to them calmly in any language (the intent reads through, even across the language barrier) and succeeds on a DC 14 Persuasion check can quiet one Onryō; it dissipates with a sound like a long exhale.

DM Notes

Atmosphere: The dormitory wing is colder than the Grand Hall. The cold is not mountain cold — it is the specific cold of places where violence has accumulated. Even mundane characters should feel uneasy here without knowing why.

The South Dormitory

Entrance deliberately collapsed by the priests during the fall. Dormitory beyond is intact but inaccessible from this side. Access requires clearing rubble (hours; loud) or alternate route via second floor or cavern system below. Contents: TBD — establish before party gains access.

Open Items

  • Tomohiro's scroll — contents to be drafted (significant handout; bridges dormitory and Jushoku no Ma)
  • South dormitory contents — establish before party gains access
  • Cell 5 swept clean — decide whether to connect to Tomohiro or leave unresolved

Type
location
Status
active

"Great Dragon Mountain — Temple of the Celestial Sky"

The temple has slept for thousands of years. Something in it has not.

In-game narration for all rooms on this floor is in supplements/read-aloud-floor-1.md. This file contains the floor overview, spatial layout, and DM reference material. Individual room details are in the floor-1/ folder.

DM Architecture Notes — First Floor

The Temple's Two States The central dramatic tension of the first floor is the contrast between what has decayed and what has not. The statue and pools are perfect. Everything else is dying. This should never be explained — just felt. Players will draw their own conclusions. The correct conclusion (that Kinryu's lingering presence, however attenuated, maintains what is closest to their effigy) is available to a DC 16 Arcana or Religion check, but it should not be handed out.

The Nagaji as Former People The party does not yet know the Nagaji are transformed Gekko clan members. Everything in this floor should add weight to that eventual revelation without revealing it. The intact bowl placed in the kitchen. The Nagaji drawn to the meditation space. The chief seimaster who has made a nest in the sanctum and sorted the debris with scholarly instinct. When the truth lands — they will look back at all of this differently.

The Nagaji Zasu — Playing the Encounter The chief seimaster is not a simple monster. If the party manages to communicate — through magic, through gesture, through patience — fragments of the original person respond. They remember the ritual. They remember it going wrong. They cannot fully articulate what they know, but a character who succeeds on a DC 15 Insight check during any interaction realizes: this thing is trying to tell them something. A DC 18 Persuasion check (with appropriate magical translation) can open a halting exchange. The abomination knows the temple's layout, including the scriptorium above. They cannot reverse what happened to themselves. But they might help someone else try.

Connecting to the Floors Above The scriptorium — where the Gekko reversal documentation lives — is on an upper floor. The first floor exists to prepare the party for that discovery: the sei-lacquer pointer from the surviving scroll, the celestial-timing insight from the star shrine, the bronze disc as a key, the Kinryu no Chikara mandate as a credential. Everything here is a tool for what comes next.

The Observatory Thread: Five observatory components are distributed across the first floor (Susanoo lens in the Grand Hall, planetary gear assembly in the dormitories, calibration disc on the bronze order seal, Tsukuyomi lens in the Star Shrine relic collection, sei conduit filament in the sanctum scroll). Additional components exist on the second floor. A party that explores thoroughly will accumulate components without necessarily understanding what they're for — the observatory itself, when they reach it, provides the context. The first component a player identifies (likely the planetary gear assembly, lowest Investigation DC) should prompt a "what is this part of?" question. Do not answer it directly. Let them carry the mystery upward. The orrery, when they find it, is the answer.

The Pools — Spending Wisely With approximately 48 charges of healing, condition removal, curse cleansing, and blessings available, the pools are a meaningful mid-dungeon resource. The party should understand they are finite. A character who examines the pools carefully (DC 13 Arcana) senses that the supply is not replenishing — each use is a permanent expenditure of something the temple has been holding in reserve for a very long time. Note: Kegare no Yamai (from Yaminezumi bites) auto-cleanses on pool entry at 1 charge per stack — the party may spend charges without realizing it.

  • 1. South Entrance — Kinko no Mon [hall: 70W × 75L, 60 ft ceiling] → south-entrance.md

    • dimensions: 70 ft wide at the south doors, 75 ft long; tapers to 20 ft wide at approximately 50 ft in, connecting to the N-S hallway
    • light: dim (blue-white magical torches, ~half functioning, ~two-thirds of those still burning; NE corner is dark)
    • cover: 8 freestanding pillars in two rows of 4 (half cover); shadow side-aisles between pillars and walls (three-quarters cover from center path); fallen pillar rubble in NE corner (full cover)
    • sight_lines: center path has clear line to N-S hallway (north); side-aisles obscured by pillar rows and dim light; taper narrows field of view approaching the hallway
    • occupants: none (standard)
    • atmosphere: cold, dry, still; bronze mineral scent; sound echoes with half-beat delay from vault; silence near tapestried walls
    • tactical: shadow corridors are the key feature — Nagaji use the side-aisles; DC 12 Perception to notice the depth before committing to center path; scraped center path telegraphs recent large-creature movement; taper creates a natural funnel toward the hallway

  • Central Hallway Cross [hallway system] → central-hallway.md

    • dimensions: 20 ft wide throughout; N-S hallway connects South Entrance (south) to Grand Hall double doors (north); E-W hallway intersects at a 20 ft × 20 ft center square; E-W wings extend approximately 120 ft in each direction from center
    • light: dark (no magical lighting in hallways)
    • cover: minimal in hallways (flat walls, no alcoves described)
    • sight_lines: long sight lines down each hallway axis; corners at the center intersection block cross-axis views

  • 2. Grand Hall — Hiroba [chamber: oval, 125W × 100 N-S] → grand-hall.md

    • dimensions: oval room, 125 ft east-to-west, 100 ft north-to-south; ceiling not visible (well beyond standard darkvision range — statue is 250 ft, so ceiling must be at least that)
    • access: double set of double doors on south wall (from N-S hallway, ~10 ft vestibule between door sets); double set of double doors on north wall (directly into Inner Sanctum)

    • cover: central statue and plinth (full cover); collapsed offering tables and debris (half cover at edges)

    • atmosphere: the statue's warmth zone (30 ft radius) contrasts with the cold decay beyond it; cold-based effects within 30 ft of statue have damage reduced by 1d4
    • tactical: the statue is the only spatial anchor; the pools create a safe zone the Shadows and Nagaji avoid; upper darkness is effectively infinite vertical space for the Shadows; the double-double-door arrangement on both ends creates two vestibule chokepoints

  • Jushoku no Ma, at remains — Head Priest Kinjiro's Bōrei (manifests when remains/box touched)

Tactical / Environmental Features

  • South Entrance, between pillars and walls — Shadow side-aisles (3/4 cover from center path)
  • South Entrance, NE corner — Fallen pillar rubble (full cover)
  • Star Shrine, entrance — Sound suppression boundary at shrine threshold
  • Grand Hall, centered on statue — 30 ft warm zone (cold damage reduced 1d4)
  • Hiroba, pool radius — Pool safe zone (Shadows and Nagaji avoid)
  • Grand Hall, south double-double-doors — Vestibule chokepoint (south)

Type
location
Status

Read-aloud text: ../supplements/read-aloud-floor-1.md § Grand Hall

Physical Description:

Oval chamber, 125 ft east-to-west × 100 ft north-to-south. Ceiling not visible (statue is 250 ft — ceiling is at least that high). Accessed via double set of double doors on south wall (from N-S hallway, ~10 ft vestibule between door sets); second double set of double doors on north wall leads directly into the Inner Sanctum. Scale is disorienting; the statue at center is the only fixed reference point.

Kinryu Statue (center): 250 feet of gold, coiled around a central plinth. Resting posture, head slightly lowered. Inlaid amber eyes oriented forward. Surface untarnished — no degradation whatsoever. Radiates perceptible warmth within 30 feet (afternoon-sun quality, not body heat).

Pools: Four shallow pools at the statue's base (south and east faces). Water perfectly clear with faint blue-white self-luminescence. Not dried, not stagnant — preserved by the same magic sustaining the statue.

Surrounding space: In sharp contrast to the statue and pools, everything else has decayed. Banners on wall brackets reduced to ribbons. Offering tables collapsed. Debris of food, incense vessels, and ceramics scattered. Floor beyond the pools buried under dust and debris.

Discoveries

  • The Statue's Magic — Passive (within 30 ft)
  • The Pools — Mechanics (DC 13 Arcana for finite nature; DC 14 Religion for ritual existence; DC 18 Religion for full ritual details)
  • The Fallen Offerings (DC 15 Investigation)
  • The Blue-White Crystal / Susanoo Projection Lens (DC 14 Investigation; DC 13 Arcana to identify) (Observatory component #1)

The Statue's Magic — Passive: The statue radiates warmth perceptible within 30 feet — not body heat, but the warmth of afternoon sun on stone, present even in the cold of the mountain interior. This warmth is real; cold-based effects within 30 feet of the statue have their damage reduced by 1d4. This property has no daily limit.

The Pools — Mechanics: The four pools are a single magical resource — approximately 48 total charges across all four pools (~12 per pool). Charge state is visually communicated: water dims and gold inlay loses glow as charges deplete. The Nagaji instinctively avoid the pools — a clue that the Golden Dragon's lingering presence repels their corruption. The pools do not regenerate. Once exhausted, the water becomes ordinary — clean, cold, but inert.

Skill Checks:

Check DC Result
Arcana 13 Identifies magical nature; reveals finite charge mechanic; charge state estimable on success
Religion 14 Identifies that holy pools of this tradition have multiple associated rituals; generic knowledge that blessings and rites exist — not their specifics
Religion 18 Reveals full ritual details — healing ritual, condition ritual, blessing ritual

The DC 18 Religion result can also be obtained from the hidden archive on the second floor.

Automatic Effects (Entry — no action required):

Effect Cost
Kegare no Yamai cleansed 1 charge per stack
Disease cleansed 1 charge per disease

Ritual 1 — Healing:

  • Trigger: Simple prayer (discoverable via DC 18 Religion check or second floor hidden archive)
  • Effect: 2d8+5 hit points restored
  • Cost: 1 charge per use

Ritual 2 — Condition Removal:

  • Trigger: Ritual activation (discoverable via DC 18 Religion check or second floor hidden archive)
  • Conditions removed: Poisoned, Blinded, Deafened, Paralyzed
  • Cost: 1 charge per condition removed

Ritual 3 — Blessing of Kinryū:

  • Trigger: Prayer to Kinryū (discoverable via DC 18 Religion check)
  • Cost: 2 charges per blessing
  • Effect: Random blessing from the Kinryū no Megumi table (see floor-1/kinryu-no-megumi.md)
  • Duration: 8 hours

The Fallen Offerings: Among the debris of collapsed offering tables, a DC 15 Investigation check finds: three bronze coins minted during the First Golden Age (worth 50gp each as antiques), a ceramic incense vessel cracked but intact with a faded clan sigil, and a fragment of silk embroidered with Old Imperial text. This fragment is a handout opportunity.

The Blue-White Crystal: Near the southernmost pool — close enough that the Nagaji would not approach — a faceted crystal the size of a fist lies half-buried in offering debris. DC 14 Investigation to notice (automatic if actively searching near the pools). The crystal is blue-white, cold to the touch, and faintly translucent with what appears to be a frozen light source at its center. DC 13 Arcana identifies it as a projection lens designed to channel sei into structured illusory output — a component of a larger device, not a standalone object. The craftsmanship matches the temple's foundational enchantment style. (Observatory component: Susanoo projection lens. Rolled near the pools during the final conflict; avoided by the Nagaji due to the pools' proximity.)

Encounters

  • 2 Kageban (影番 — "Shadow Watch"; upper darkness — descend when disturbed; avoid pools)
  • Nagaji Bushi ×1 (squad leader, rotation from Naijin)
  • Nagaji Hohei ×2 (rotation from Naijin)
  • Nagaji Ashigaru ×6 (rotation from Naijin)

DM Notes

The Statue's Magic — Active (Ko'jiri): If Ko'jiri approaches within 15 feet, the amber eyes shift. Not dramatically — no glowing, no sound, no proclamation. They simply orient. Anyone watching (DC 14 Perception to notice) sees the carved irises move in their settings to face him directly. If Ko'jiri speaks aloud in the statue's presence, he hears a single sound in response — not words, not language, but a low resonant hum from the stone itself, felt more in the chest than heard with the ears. It is acknowledgment. The con artist who built a career performing Golden Dragon authority is being recognized by the thing itself. What that means is for Ko'jiri to reckon with.

Scale of the Space: Emphasize the disorientation of the scale. The ceiling is not visible. The far walls require a light source or darkvision to confirm. The statue at the center is the only fixed reference point — everything orients toward it.

Undead Presence: Two Kageban (影番 — "Shadow Watch"; Shadows, MM p.269) inhabit the upper darkness of the Grand Hall — former temple guards of the loyal order, still at their post after millennia. They are not hostile by default — they are the loyalists, still watching their post. They do not descend into the light near the statue. They watch from above. If the party makes noise, desecrates offerings, or moves toward the dormitories, they descend. They do not pursue into the pools' radius of warmth.

Geography & Terrain

Hana occupies the eastern coast of Hokori and is the seat of imperial history. It stretches along the island's eastern seaboard, bounded to the northwest by the mountainous interior of Sora province for the majority of its inland border, with Tsuchi and Hi to the west, and Kaze to the north.

The province's defining feature is the Serenia-kai (Selenia Sea), a vast inland sea covering more than a thousand square miles, fed by twenty-five rivers and thirteen waterfalls cascading from the Tenchusan Ren and the central highlands of Hokori. Its surface shifts color with the seasons. The tidal rhythms driven by Kagekuni's four moons make its edges unpredictable; the shoreline can retreat several hundred meters during low compound tides.

To the west, the Seidorin Mori (Bronze Wood Forest) stretches for miles -- an ancient woodland where the trees grow with bark of burnished copper-bronze that catches sunlight like armor. Their leaves shed entirely in one night when the temperature drops below a certain threshold. The wood itself is extraordinarily hard and is harvested under strict clan license for weapons and structural reinforcement.

To the northeast, the land rises sharply toward the Tenchusan Ren. The pass through this range is the primary land route north. The mountains are sacred in Hana's religious tradition; several peak-top shrines are maintained by hermit monks.

Shirogane Yama (Silver Mountain), the highest peak on Hokori, dominates the northern skyline -- a pale peak streaked with natural mineral deposits that catch moonlight. At its summit sits the Hoshino To (Tower of Stars), an ancient astronomical observatory built during the Golden Age. The city of Kumoji sits at its base.

Key Waterways: Kinryugawa (Gold Dragon River), Midorikawa (Green River), Sutariba (Star River)

Points of Interest:

  • Seidorin Mori (Bronze Wood Forest) -- Ancient woodland with metallic-barked trees. Harvested under strict Clan Kaminari license. The interior is unnervingly quiet -- sound behaves strangely under the canopy. Unlicensed logging is a capital offense.
  • Serenia-kai (Selenia Sea) -- The great inland sea. Major artery for trade and travel. The most dangerous tidal event is Ryugetsu's Embrace, when three moons align over the sea simultaneously.
  • Hoshino To (Tower of Stars) -- Ancient observatory on Shirogane Yama summit. Still operational; maintained by a small order of seimasters. Instruments calibrated to all three stars and four moons simultaneously.
  • Kodan no Jinja -- Ancient roadside shrine. Grants divine boons to supplicants for a period of days equal to three times the recipient's experience level (maximum sixty days). Only one boon at a time.
  • Shadowfen Bridge -- Stone bridge near Sakura Mura crossing into marsh forest. Legend claims a river spirit demands one honest secret spoken aloud; liars find the far bank leads somewhere unintended.
  • Tenchusan Ren (Heavenly Pillar Mountains) -- The mountain range forming Hana's northwestern boundary. The pass is treacherous in autumn and impassable during winter storms. Significant ruins exist within the range.

Settlements

Settlement Type Population Notes
Heian City Large Imperial capital; major port; seat of clan governance
Fujisato City Medium Northeastern coastal port; fishing and trade
Kikyo City Medium Eastern edge of Bronze Wood; lumber trade; Clan Seishin subject
Ayame Town 638 Military waypoint; base of Tenchusan Ren pass
Kumoji Town Medium Base of Shirogane Yama; near Hoshino To observatory
Momiji Town Small Peaceful western lakeside town on Serenia-kai
Sakurano Town Small On Lake Midoriko; Heian ferry connection
Natsumura Village 161 Fishing village at mouth of Sutariba
Nishihara Village 180 Rolling hills; weekly market; Temple of Ancestors
Sakura Mura Village 150 Grew from highway inn; Shadowfen Bridge
Kawaguchi Village Small River crossing settlement
Takamine Village 97 Poor iron mining village; shadow of Kinryuzan

Culture & Trade

Hana's culture is the closest to the old imperial ideal -- formal, ceremonially rich, and deeply aware of its historical weight. The proximity to Heian means merchants, scholars, monks, and diplomats pass through constantly, and even small villages carry themselves with a certain civic dignity uncommon in frontier provinces.

The Bronze Wood trade defines the province's economy. Seidorin timber commands extraordinary prices across the archipelago -- weapons and armor crafted from it are status symbols as much as tools. The licensing system for harvesting creates significant corruption opportunities at every level of local administration.

Fishing on the Serenia-kai and the Kinryugawa sustains much of the rural population. The Gold Dragon River runs fat with a fish called kinuo (gold-tail) that is considered a delicacy in Heian and commands premium prices at market.

History

Hana is the oldest continuously inhabited province in the archipelago. The Golden Dragon Clan held dominion over these southern highlands long before human settlement -- their capital Kinkokyo is believed to have stood somewhere in or beneath the Tenchusan Ren, buried by the avalanche triggered during the Onyx Rebellion. The province's rivers still run faintly gold at dawn -- a phenomenon locals call Kinryu no Namida (the Golden Dragon's Tears).

Heian was chosen as the imperial capital by the First Emperor Tenryu no Mikado for strategic and spiritual reasons -- it stood at the convergence of three rivers, on a defensible peninsula, and was reportedly the site of a vision in which Kinryu declared the land under divine protection.

The province suffered heavily during the Dark Ages -- Heian was sacked twice -- but its infrastructure proved resilient. The Emperor's Highway remains largely intact through Hana.

Clan Kaminari has governed Hana for the past several centuries. The clan rose to prominence when Raijin no Kazuhiko unified the province under a single authority following a period of fractious minor-clan governance.

• The Bronze Wood Forest's metallic quality has a deeper origin than simple mineral runoff -- connected to the buried city of Kinkokyo beneath the Tenchusan Ren.
  • The Shadowfen Bridge exhibits genuine sei resonance that produces mild disorientation in those who speak falsehoods while crossing.
  • A seimaster from Hoshino To has gone missing after reporting an unusual celestial alignment that matches nothing in the records.

The Buried City of Kinkokyo

The Golden Dragon Clan's capital is not simply buried rubble. Significant portions survived structurally intact, sealed beneath hundreds of feet of rock and earth. The gold doors the party currently stands before are an outer entrance to this buried complex, exposed by a recent earthquake. The temple above is connected to Kinkokyo below. Ko'jiri's research is essentially correct.

Kinryu no Hikari

The artifact exists. It is held in a sealed vault deep within the temple, in the farthest underground section of Kinkokyo. It is not a weapon or a key. It is a communication device: a golden mirror that allows direct communion with Kinryu, the living Golden Dragon, wherever she is hidden. She will answer if called by someone she deems worthy.

The Bronze Wood Secret

The Seidorin Mori grows over a second branch of the buried Kinkokyo canal system. The metallic quality of the trees is caused by trace mineral content in the groundwater -- water flowing through golden veins in the buried city's infrastructure for thousands of years. Ren Nakamura (Shicho of Kikyo) knows this. The merchant guild he is allied with wants to find the source and exploit it directly.

Hiroshi Nakamura -- Traitor in Place

As Shugo of Heian, Hiroshi controls the administrative heart of the province. His access to Clan Kaminari intelligence is nearly total. He has been feeding information to an outside party (undeveloped) for at least three years. His warm, approachable public persona is his most effective weapon -- even his brother Hideo does not suspect how deep the betrayal runs.

Plot Hooks

  • Unlicensed Bronze Wood poaching tied to a merchant guild front operation in Kikyo -- Ren Nakamura's faction or a rival?
  • Strange behavior reported in Shadowfen Bridge area -- a traveler arrived at the wrong destination and has no memory of the crossing
  • A seimaster from Hoshino To has gone missing after reporting an unusual celestial alignment that matches nothing in the records

Type
settlement

"The city that outlasted every empire built within it."

Overview

Heian is the oldest continuously inhabited city in the archipelago and the seat of imperial authority for over eight thousand years. It stands on a peninsula where the Nagisa Sea meets Lake Midoriko -- a position offering both a defensible landward approach and open water access in two directions.

The city is beautiful in the way that things shaped by deep time become beautiful -- through the accumulation of craftsmanship, care, and purpose. Ancient trees line the main avenues, their roots lifting paving stones that are reset around them generation after generation. The Imperial Palace complex dominates the skyline. Shirogane Yama is visible on clear days forty miles to the north and northwest.

The Emperor's Highway extends from Heian in three directions -- north through Tenchusan Ren toward Kaze, east along the coast, and west by ferry connection to Sakurano and the interior. With no emperor, the city is a center without a purpose -- the streets are still busy, the markets still active, but there is a quality to civic life: the posture of a city holding itself together while waiting for resolution.

Districts / Landmarks

Hikari Zon -- Knowledge District Libraries, academies, schools, and scholarly institutions. Low, wide buildings with sliding walls. The central library holds the largest collection in Hana. Seimasters and scholars from across the archipelago spend time here.

Hinode-ku -- Eastern Residential Ward Mixed residential for artisans and merchants. Workshops opening onto narrow streets. A lively night market operates along the canal.

Ichiba Chiku -- Market District The economic heart. The largest open market in Hokori operates six days out of seven. The Market District never truly closes.

Inari Kyoku -- Religious District Temples, shrines, and spiritual institutions. Torii gates multiply inward from the boundary. A shrine to each of the seven dragon clans exists here.

Kaze-sho -- Wind District Open spaces, windmills, farming plots within the city boundary. The windmills power grain milling and workshop machinery.

Kinrin Chiku -- Palace Surrounding Quarter Residential and administrative district surrounding the Imperial Palace. Noble families and senior officials. Access is controlled. Streets are wider for ceremonial processions.

Kokyo Chiku -- Imperial Palace Complex Palace grounds surrounded by walls, gates, and a water moat. Centuries of accumulated construction. With no emperor, maintained by skeleton staff under the Kokushi Kyokai. Sections have been sealed.

Kurogane-sho -- Steel Precinct The forge district. Smiths, armorers, weapons specialists. Runs hot year-round. Home to Taro's Forge.

Mizu-gai -- Riverside Ward Along the water's edge. Water gardens, seafood restaurants, fish markets, fishing family residences. The morning catch market is a Heian institution.

Ryu Jikuchiku -- Dragon Borough Nightlife, theater, teahouses, entertainment. Operates on a shifted schedule -- fully alive after dark. Hosts noh theater, storytellers, gambling establishments, and renowned teahouses.

Sakura-ku -- Cherry Blossom Ward Parks, public gardens, festival infrastructure. Famous cherry tree avenues. Hosts major seasonal festivals.

Tabibito Gai -- Traveler's Street Eastern gate neighborhood for transient visitors. Inns, stables, money changers, translation services. Character shifts constantly.

Tenku Zon -- Hilltop Ward Highest elevation residential area. Reserved for nobility and senior officials. Finest architecture in Heian.

Tensho no Mon -- Military District Barracks, command infrastructure, training grounds. Home to Taisho Hideo Nakamura's command headquarters. Where the party received their mission briefing.

Notable Establishments

Taro's Forge (Kurogane-sho) -- Master blacksmith Taro Fukomoto's workshop. Renowned for quality and integrity. Produces exceptional weapons and armor. Taro teaches those who demonstrate genuine commitment.

The Moonlit Garden (Ryu Jikuchiku) -- Teahouse in the Dragon Borough with a garden famous for nighttime aesthetics -- white stone, silver-leaved trees, reflecting pool. The party first convened here. Renowned for discretion.

Hikari no Shizuku (Hikari Zon) -- Healing and light magic enclave in the Knowledge District. Provides medical services and trains healing-aligned sei practitioners.

Key Figures

  • Hiroshi Nakamura -- Shugo (Governor) of Heian -> npcs/hiroshi-nakamura.md
  • Hideo Nakamura -- Taisho (General); military commander -> npcs/hideo-nakamura.md
  • Taro Fukomoto -- Master blacksmith -> npcs/taro-fukomoto.md

• The Imperial Palace's sealed sections contain something found after the Emperor's death that the Kokushi Kyokai does not know how to handle.
  • The Moonlit Garden teahouse serves a deeper function as a neutral meeting ground for intelligence exchanges.
  • Multiple individuals have arrived in Heian with claims to imperial succession.

DM Secrets

Hiroshi Nakamura -- Traitor in Place As Shugo, Hiroshi has near-total access to Clan Kaminari's intelligence and administrative operations. He is feeding intelligence to an outside party and has been for at least three years. He is aware that Hideo is investigating and is actively monitoring that investigation. His public persona is a performance of exceptional consistency.

The Imperial Palace -- Sealed Sections Something was found in the imperial apartments after Ryujin no Mikado died that the Kokushi Kyokai administrators do not know how to handle. It is not evidence of murder -- it is evidence of something older and stranger.

The Moonlit Garden's True Function The owner is a retired intelligence operative who maintains it as a neutral meeting ground for the Elven Council, among other groups. Information exchanges here regularly under the social protection of tea ceremony neutrality. The staff are trained to notice and remember without appearing to.

Hideo Nakamura's Investigation Hideo is hunting a traitor he does not yet know is his brother. He has narrowed the leak to a small circle of senior staff. The question is whether he reaches the conclusion before Hiroshi learns how close Hideo is and takes action.

The Succession Crisis in Heian Multiple claimants with genealogical documents of varying plausibility. The Kokushi Kyokai handles them through administrative delay. Three serious claimants are being watched. Two are probably fraudulent. One may not be.

Plot Hooks

  • Hideo Nakamura asks the party to carry out intelligence work he cannot assign to his own staff -- suggests he suspects someone close
  • An unusual request arrives from the sealed section of the Imperial Palace: someone inside has sent a note requesting outside contact; the Kokushi Kyokai doesn't know how this happened
  • A succession claimant approaches the party specifically, wanting independent witnesses to a document verification

text.content:
Geography & Terrain

Hi is the most geologically violent province on Hokori -- a region of active volcanism, fumarole fields, obsidian plains, and mountains that periodically tear themselves apart. It encompasses the majority of the island's western side, surrounded by mountains and the sea. Tsuchi borders it to the southeast, Hana shares a small stretch of its eastern border, Sora encompasses its northern boundary, and Mizu sits along its western edge. Earthquakes are ambient. Residents learn to read tremors the way sailors read wind.

The province takes its name -- Hi, meaning fire -- from the volcanic peaks that define it. The largest, Enshiyama (Flame Peak Mountain), is the third highest peak on Hokori. It last erupted in full approximately two hundred years ago.

The terrain is dramatic and hostile. Black obsidian fields stretch for miles where ancient lava flows cooled and cracked. Fumarole vents release sulfurous steam. Soil, where it exists, is extraordinarily fertile -- volcanic ash enriches it beyond anything in the southern provinces. Terraced farming on the slopes between active zones produces crops of startling quality. This contradiction -- death and abundance in tight proximity -- defines Hi's cultural character.

Rivers here run fast and hot from thermal sources. The Honogawa (Flame River) originates from a thermal lake near Enshiyama's base and is warm to the touch for its entire upper reach.

Points of Interest:

  • Enshiyama (Flame Peak Mountain) -- Dominant volcano of Hokori's north. Currently active at low levels. Crater contains a mineral-rich lake that glows faintly orange at night.
  • Honogawa (Flame River) -- Warm thermal river. Upper reach near the source is hot enough to scald. Runs through a narrow volcanic gorge.
  • Obsidian Fields of Kuroso -- Vast plains of black volcanic glass. Obsidian of exceptional quality, ideal for blades and lenses. Seismically active and hazardous.
  • The Crimson Shrine -- Deep in the volcanic highlands, predating the empire. Torii of natural red stone. Local tradition holds Akaryu's presence can be felt during major eruptions. Never absorbed into the imperial religious system.
  • Onsen-machi Hot Springs -- The only genuinely comfortable location in Hi. Natural hot spring pools developed into a resort town maintaining political neutrality.

Settlements

Settlement Type Notes
Enshiro Town Provisional garrison capital; military administration; base of active clan competition
Kazan Mura Village Slopes of Enshiyama; volcano watchers; evacuation specialists
Kurokawa Village Black river settlement; obsidian crafting; trade in volcanic glass
Onsen-machi Town Hot spring resort town; wealthy visitors; nominal neutrality
Takibi Village Remote highland farming community; terraced volcanic fields

Culture & Trade

Hi's culture is defined by proximity to death. The people are laconic, practical, and possess a dark humor about their circumstances. They do not flee volcanic activity -- they have developed sophisticated systems for reading, mitigating, and living alongside it. Hi's volcano-guides, engineers, and evacuation specialists are prized across the archipelago.

Primary exports are obsidian, volcanic sulfur (used in alchemy and sei-related preparations), hot spring minerals, and surprisingly excellent agricultural products from volcanic terraces. The Onsen-machi resort draws wealthy visitors from across Hokori and beyond.

History

Hi was long considered a backwater -- too dangerous and too remote. The Crimson Dragon Clan had their true stronghold here before unification, and the western reaches refused submission to Tenryu no Mikado. That refusal left a cultural legacy: Hi's people are fiercely independent and deeply skeptical of imperial authority.

During the Dark Ages, Hi was almost entirely abandoned by formal authority. Small communities developed their own governance structures, spiritual practices, and martial traditions largely divorced from the broader empire.

The province is currently in contested administration. The previous governing clan was wiped out in the opening engagements of the Arashi-Genso war, and neither alliance has installed a replacement. Several smaller clans are vying for the position.

• The Crimson Shrine's keeper, Tsubaki, has served for sixty years and communicates with something through the shrine's ember-bowl.
  • The western territories of Hi are home to descendants of the Crimson Clan faction that refused unification, organized into loose tribal confederacies preserving forgotten traditions.
  • Seimasters debate whether Enshiyama's current activity signals a major eruption building.

The Crimson Dragon Clan's Hidden Presence

Akaryu, the Crimson Dragon, is still alive and hidden. She maintains a tenuous connection to Hi through the Crimson Shrine. The shrine's keeper Tsubaki is an Initiate of the Order of the Ancient Guard. She does not know Akaryu's location, but knows the dragon is alive. Offerings burned in the shrine's ember-bowl reach something that responds.

The Western Territories

The western reaches are effectively a separate entity. Descendants of the Crimson Clan faction that refused Tenryu's unification live there in loose tribal confederacies that have preserved traditions the rest of the empire forgot. They are fiercely territorial and know things about the volcanic highlands that no imperial map captures.

Enshiyama and the Coming Eruption

The current low-level activity is the precursor to a significant eruption -- within one to three years. The seimasters who know this are divided on whether to publicize it; the political vacuum means there is no coordinating authority capable of organizing evacuation. This is an unlit fuse.

The Contested Administration

The three clans competing for Hi's governance are being quietly manipulated by a fourth party -- a merchant consortium that wants provincial administration too weak to enforce trade regulations. The current chaos is, to some degree, manufactured.

Plot Hooks

  • A volcano-guide from Kazan Mura has seen something in the upper reaches of Enshiyama -- something that moved against the wind -- and is too frightened to go back alone
  • The Crimson Shrine's ember-bowl responded to an offering in a way it never has before; Tsubaki needs discreet help interpreting what it means
  • A seimaster studying the eruption precursors has disappeared; her notes suggest she found something in the obsidian fields that was not geological

North end of the temple — the most sacred space on the first floor. Includes the Jushoku no Ma (Abbot's Chamber, 6a) and Hoko (Storehouse, 6b).

Read-aloud text: ../supplements/read-aloud-floor-1.md § Inner Sanctum

Physical Description:

North end of the temple — most sacred space on the first floor. Octagonal chamber, 90 ft wide × 35 ft deep. Accessed via double set of double doors from the Grand Hall's north wall.

Doors: Black-lacquered wood banded with bronze. Frame carved with a frieze of the seven dragon clans in a ring. Standing open. Inlaid silver locking mechanism lines visible inside the frame — dark and dead. Wards broken from the outside (shadow-aspected magic, Kokuryu tradition).

Walls: Eight scroll positions. Six empty (mountings remain, scrolls gone). One holds only floor-level fragments with faded ink. One (far wall) holds an intact scroll — Kinryu in flight, gold and deep blue on black silk, colors perfectly preserved by active sei-lacquer. Contains hidden sei conduit filament in the decorative border.

Center: Floor cleared deliberately. Original furnishings (shattered pedestals, broken braziers) pushed to walls. Circular depression in swept floor — nest shape, formed by repeated use by something large. Edges built from broken furniture and torn fabric. Currently empty. Radiates warmth and a sense of presence.

Hidden door (east wall): Stone-framed, flush with surface, seam filled with centuries of grit. Accessed via a 5 ft wide, 20 ft long secret hallway. Opened by pressing the bronze disc against a specific carved scale in the dragon-frieze border. Leads to the head priest's private chamber (15 ft wide × 20 ft deep — never entered since the order fell).

Discoveries

  • The Surviving Scroll — sei-lacquer identification (DC 13 Arcana)
  • The Scroll's Hidden Thread / Sei Conduit Filament (DC 16 Arcana, or DC 14 if lens already found; DC 14 Sleight of Hand to extract) (Observatory component #5)
  • Breaking the Wards — analysis (DC 15 Arcana — shadow-aspected, Kokuryu)
  • The Hidden Door to Jushoku no Ma (DC 15 Perception, or automatic if searching walls; bronze disc opens)
  • Jushoku no Ma — Kinjiro's Journal (in bronze box, DC 16 Thieves' Tools or disc as key)
  • Jushoku no Ma — Kinryu no Chikara Mandate (in bronze box)
  • Jushoku no Ma — Operational Ledger (in bronze box)
  • Jushoku no Ma — Kinjiro's Remains
  • The Zasu's Ritual Scrolls — Hebi no Hensen (found on Zasu's body after encounter; see zasu-ritual-scrolls.md)
  • Hoko (secret door S wall behind dresser — contents TBD)

The Surviving Scroll: The preserved scroll of Kinryu in flight is worth 800gp as an antique, more to the right buyer. More importantly, the sei-lacquer preserving it is still active — a character who examines it closely (DC 13 Arcana) identifies the preservation technique as Golden Dragon order craft, and notes that the same technique was almost certainly used on the most important records kept in this temple. Records preserved this way would survive in far better condition than anything else here. This is a subtle pointer toward the scriptorium on the floor above.

The Scroll's Hidden Thread: DC 16 Arcana (or DC 14 for a character who has already identified a projection lens elsewhere in the temple) reveals something additional: woven into the scroll's decorative border is an impossibly fine golden filament — not thread, not wire, something between the two. It carries a faint, steady sei charge, distinct from the preservation enchantment. This filament is a sei conduit — a transmission line designed to carry magical resonance between connected systems. Removing it without destroying the scroll requires DC 14 Sleight of Hand or Tinker's Tools; on failure, the scroll's preservation enchantment collapses and the image fades to nothing within minutes (the scroll is destroyed, but the filament is recovered). On success, both the scroll and filament are preserved intact. (Observatory component: sei conduit filament. Connects the orrery's mechanical output to the arcane projection system. The scroll was stored in the sanctum — closest room to the observatory's position on the floor above — because the conduit needed to remain within the temple's foundational magic field to retain its charge.)

Breaking the Wards: The magical seals on the door were broken from outside. The magic used to break them — DC 15 Arcana — is shadow-aspected. Kokuryu tradition. The infiltrators unsealed this room during the order's fall, gaining access to the sanctum's contents. Whatever was in here, they took it or destroyed it.

The Jushoku no Ma (Abbot's Chamber): Behind the rubble on the east side of the room, almost invisible unless the party is actively looking (DC 15 Perception, or automatic if they are searching the walls), is a section of wall that is actually a door — stone-framed, flush with the surface, its seam filled with centuries of grit. The locking mechanism is a pressure sequence on specific carved scales in the dragon-frieze border; the bronze disc from the sealed dormitory room, when pressed against a specific scale, triggers the release. The room beyond — the head priest's private chamber — has never been entered since the order fell.

What Is In The Jushoku no Ma: A small, very austere room (15 ft wide × 20 ft deep). A sleeping platform against the west wall with a dresser beside it. A writing desk with a locked bronze box (DC 16 Thieves' Tools or the disc again as a key). Inside the box: three documents, each sealed separately.

  1. The personal journal of Head Priest Kinjiro — final entries. The journal is personal, written in a direct hand that does not match the formality of the other documents. The final entries describe the order's disintegration — not the external pressures (those are in the ledger) but the internal experience of watching a community fracture. Kinjiro names no traitors. The journal's emotional weight is in what it does not accuse.

  2. The Kinryu no Chikara mandate — a sealed tube containing a formal document conferring specific authority within the temple to named individuals. The mandate is blank on the recipient line, left that way deliberately — Kinjiro did not know who would find it and chose to leave it open. A character who performs the short ritual described in the journal (10 minutes, spoken in any language, a genuine statement of intent to protect rather than exploit what lies within) can inscribe their name. The mandate grants its bearer advantage on all Charisma checks within the temple and allows passage through one magically sealed door elsewhere in the structure.

  3. The operational ledger of the hub — a formal record of network activity kept by the head priest. Each significant entry logs the full operational cycle: distress signal received, acknowledgement authorized and sent, dispatch ordered, field report on findings. The ledger records both inbound signals and outbound responses — a complete cycle document, not a record of actions alone.

Ledger physical condition: Sei-lacquered selectively in the same technique as the surviving sanctum scroll. Routine entries written in ordinary ink have faded to illegibility. Entries the head priest considered significant were lacquered and remain fully readable. Which entries were treated is itself information about what the head priest considered to matter.

Standard entry format: Prior entries from the order's functional period are complete. Signal received, response sent, investigator dispatched, findings returned and summarized. These entries establish the template clearly. The party understands what a finished cycle looks like before they reach the entries that are not finished.

The fall-period entries — what is absent: The distress signals sent by Kaze and Sora at the fall of 13088 are not recorded in the ledger. No entry exists for either signal — not the incoming alert, not an acknowledgement, not a dispatch, not a field report. The ledger's last entries are whatever completed operational cycles preceded the fall. Then the record ends. The absence is not by design — distress signals appear in prior entries. Kaze and Sora are simply not there because the collapse overtook the record-keeping.

Sora acknowledgement gap: The acknowledged state exists in the network (visible on Tapestry III). It does not exist in the ledger. Possible explanations: a monitor acting independently during the chaos; the head priest sent it but was interrupted before recording; someone who didn't survive sent it; or the entry was among those that faded. The document cannot close the gap.

Kaze in the ledger: Whether Kaze was ever acknowledged cannot be determined from the ledger. The signal is absent from the record entirely.

Placement note: The journal is personal. The mandate confers authority. The ledger is institutional memory. Together they represent what the order chose to preserve when everything else was falling.

The Remains: On the sleeping platform, partially covered by a threadbare blanket that has largely disintegrated, lie the skeletal remains of Head Priest Kinjiro. The posture is deliberate — hands folded across the chest, body aligned with the room's cardinal orientation, head turned slightly toward the writing desk. He went to his bed and did not rise. The bones are undisturbed. Nothing in this room has been touched since the door sealed.

Encounters

  • Nagaji Zasu (Inner Sanctum lair — currently patrolling; returns periodically)
  • Head Priest Kinjiro's Bōrei (Jushoku no Ma — manifests when bronze box or remains touched)

DM Notes

Kinjiro's Spirit: The head priest did not move on after death. His spirit persists in this chamber as a protector — bound not by curse or unfinished personal business, but by the weight of institutional obligation. He was the last keeper. No one relieved him of the duty. The spirit is dormant until the chamber is entered; it manifests when someone touches the bronze box or the remains.

Manifestation: Not aggressive by default. The spirit appears as a translucent figure seated at the writing desk — the posture of someone still working, still keeping records. Cold fills the room. The torchlight dims but does not go out. Kinjiro does not speak first. He watches. His expression carries exhaustion rather than menace.

Peaceful Resolution: A party that approaches with respect — speaks to the spirit, identifies themselves, or demonstrates they are not here to loot — can engage Kinjiro in limited communication. He cannot speak freely (the binding is too old, his connection too frayed), but he can answer direct questions with gestures, single words, or by directing attention to specific objects in the room. He knows the temple's layout, the purpose of the documents in the box, and the broad shape of what went wrong. He does not know the current state of the Nagaji — he died before the transformation. If the party undertakes to cleanse the temple (removing the corruption, restoring order to the sacred spaces), and succeeds, Kinjiro can finally release. His departure is quiet — the cold lifts, the translucence fades, the bones settle slightly as whatever held them together withdraws.

Combat Resolution: If the party acts aggressively — drawing weapons in the chamber, attempting to force the box open without care, or showing clear intent to desecrate — the spirit defends. Use Revenant (MM p.259) as a base, adjusted: Kinjiro is not pursuing vengeance but defending a post. He fights to drive intruders from the chamber, not to kill. If reduced to 0 HP, he reforms in 24 hours (as Revenant) unless the party has cleansed the temple, in which case he passes on regardless.

Reward: TBD — see dm/plot-threads.md for open decision. Consider: direct knowledge that shortcuts a discovery elsewhere in the temple, a blessing granting advantage on a specific check type within the temple, or a narrative reward connected to the Kinryu no Chikara mandate (the priest confirming the ritual, or adding weight to the inscription).

The Hoko (Storehouse): A secret door on the south wall of the Jushoku no Ma, west side — behind the dresser, west of the bed. Completely concealed. Contains the priest's and the temple's most sacred items. This room has been left entirely untouched since the order fell — sealed within a sealed room within a hidden chamber. The deepest-hidden space on the first floor. (Contents: TBD — see dm/plot-threads.md)

The Zasu's Scrolls: When the Zasu is defeated, the party finds a cracked leather scroll case lashed to its midsection with strips of torn formal silk bearing the Gekkō mon. Contains seven documents in varying states of preservation — the transformation ritual research the chief seimaster gathered before performing the ritual on himself. Full details: zasu-ritual-scrolls.md

The Occupant: A Nagaji Zasu (MM p.308) has made this space its lair — a Nagaji of particular power, one of the original senior members of Clan Gekko, transformed more completely than the others. This individual was once Gekko's chief seimaster — the architect of the failed ritual. The transformation has cost them nearly everything, but not quite. Deep within the abomination, fragments of the original person remain: a scholar, a leader, someone who made a catastrophic decision trying to protect their clan. They are not in the sanctum when the party first arrives (they patrol the temple), but they will return.

Atmosphere: The nest radiates residual warmth and something harder to name — a sense of presence, of being watched, even in an empty room. The cleared center of the room feels deliberately territorial. Players with high Passive Perception (14+) notice that the debris pushed to the walls has been sorted — materials of value (intact objects, sealed containers) are in one pile; pure refuse in another. Whatever lives here is not mindless.

Geography & Terrain

Kaze is a province of shadows and mist. It occupies the eastern side of Hokori's northeastern leg -- the X-shape's upper-right arm. Nami sits to the north, Kusa to the west, Hana to the south, and Sora shares a brief stretch of its southwestern border. Sheltered from direct coastal weather by mountain ranges, it has a microclimate of cool, damp air that never fully clears. The province averages fewer clear days per year than any other on the island. Its forests -- dense stands of dark cedar and ancient black pine -- grow so thickly that the canopy blocks most sunlight even in summer. Locals navigate by landmark and feel rather than by sun or stars.

The terrain is mountainous, cut by deep river valleys and narrow gorges. The Kazeyama Ren (Wind Mountain Range) runs along the province's southern border, channeling wind up the valleys in complex, disorienting patterns. Sounds carry strangely here, seeming to come from the wrong direction.

The Kagero River (Shimmer River) is the primary waterway -- named for the heat shimmer visible over its surface on rare warm days, caused by thermal differential between the water temperature and the cool air.

The town of Akatsuki (Dawn) occupies a peculiar position -- its name suggests emergence and new light, but it is one of the most shrouded settlements in the archipelago. The name predates the current settlement.

Points of Interest:

  • Tsukikage (Moonlit Shadow) -- Abandoned former capital of Clan Gekko. Not destroyed or obviously fled in panic -- it simply emptied gradually over several months. Personal belongings remain in homes. The daimyo's residence is locked from the outside.
  • Monastery of the Black Lily -- Above Akatsuki village, accessible by stone staircase cut into rock. Dark stone and iron construction; austere; forbidding. The Order of the Black Lily operates here -- Kagekuni's most skilled infiltrators and intelligence operatives.
  • The Kagero Gorge -- Narrow river gorge with complex, disorienting acoustics. The gorge wall contains numerous carved reliefs depicting serpentine figures that do not match any known iconographic tradition.
  • The Hollow Peaks -- Three mountains in the Kazeyama Ren that are demonstrably hollow. Cold air vents from fissures at their bases year-round. Sei-sensitive individuals report a powerful residual presence.

Settlements

Settlement Type Notes
Tsukikage Town Traditional Gekko capital; functionally abandoned; eerie and intact
Akatsuki Village De facto administrative center; above it: Monastery of the Black Lily
Kazetani Village Deep valley settlement; largely cut off; residents haven't left in months
Kirigakure Village Literally "hidden in mist"; the most isolated settlement; some suggest it moves
Mikazuki Village Crescent Moon Village; southern border; last outpost before Hana

Culture & Trade

Kaze's culture is inward-facing. Primary exports have historically been information -- Clan Gekko's intelligence networks and the Order of the Black Lily's trained specialists. In tangible terms, Kaze produces excellent black pine lumber, rare mountain herbs for medicine and alchemy, and distinctive lacquerware using naturally sourced pigments from mineral-rich soil.

The people of Kaze are not cold -- they are careful. A culture of watching and listening developed naturally in a province where visibility is limited and sound behaves unreliably. They form deep loyalties within small groups and extend trust to outsiders only after extended familiarity.

History

Kaze was historically the domain of Clan Gekko, an independent clan that maintained careful neutrality through successive political upheavals. The Gekko were notable for producing seimasters specializing in shadow and illusion magic -- linked to the province's physical character and lingering influence from the Onyx Dragon Clan.

The province was never fully subdued -- even Tenryu no Mikado secured Gekko cooperation through negotiation rather than conquest. This arrangement eventually crystallized into the Order of the Black Lily, Kagekuni's premier infiltration school.

Clan Gekko's recent disappearance has plunged the province into deep unease. Trade has slowed. The provincial administration has stopped communicating with Heian. Small communities have reported strange encounters -- serpentine figures glimpsed on mountain trails, abandoned buildings showing signs of violent disturbance, livestock found dead in unnatural ways.

• Clan Gekko's disappearance was not caused by an outside force -- the senior seimasters attempted something that went catastrophically wrong.
  • The Order of the Black Lily knows the truth about what happened and has made a calculated decision about when to reveal it.
  • The Hollow Peaks were structures of the Onyx Dragon Clan -- hollow mountains used as nesting and storage spaces.
  • The gorge carvings depict something connected to the transformation that befell Clan Gekko.

The Nagaji Truth -- Core Campaign Revelation

Clan Gekko's disappearance was not caused by an outside force. The clan's senior seimasters, searching for a way to elevate their shadow magic capability, discovered fragmentary texts describing an Onyx Dragon ritual -- a transformation rite tied to Kokuryu. It transformed those who underwent it into Nagaji -- serpentine humanoids driven by new instincts they cannot fully suppress. The transformation spread. Masota no Gekko himself underwent the ritual last, in a desperate attempt to maintain control. He is now Nagaji as well -- somewhere in the Kaze highlands.

The Order of the Black Lily -- What They Know

The Order knows the truth about the Nagaji transformation. Several operatives witnessed the early stages. The Order has made a calculated decision: the information is too dangerous to release without a reversal plan. They will share the complete truth with parties who reach them -- but only the complete truth, no partial admissions.

Is the Transformation Reversible?

Yes -- but the answer lies in the Temple of Kinryu, specifically in the clan's records about Kokuryu's original ritual and the countermeasure that the Golden Dragon Clan developed. This creates a direct link between the party's current location (the gold doors) and the Kaze storyline.

Masota no Gekko -- Current State

He is alive, in the Kaze highlands. He retains fragments of his original identity but the transformation suppresses rational thought during stress or combat. He is not a villain. He is a leader who made a terrible decision in desperation. A potential redemption arc exists if the party can find a reversal.

The Hollow Peaks

These were Onyx Dragon Clan structures. The interior of at least one is accessible from the gorge. What remains inside is ancient and significant: Onyx Clan cultural artifacts, including documentation of the transformation ritual.

Plot Hooks

  • The Order of the Black Lily sends a message via an intermediary: "Come to Akatsuki. Come alone. Come before the moon is full."
  • Masota no Gekko leaves something behind at a ransacked site -- something a transformed being could not have done deliberately unless part of him was still trying to communicate
  • A scholar in Mikazuki has been studying the gorge carvings for years and has just realized what they depict

Type: Curse (not disease)

Reflects kegare as spiritual pollution — a Shinto concept of ritual impurity — not physical illness. Removal requires Remove Curse (3rd level spell), not Lesser Restoration.

Transmission

Vector: Yaminezumi (闇鼠 — Darkness Rats) bite

On a successful hit, the target makes a DC 12 Constitution saving throw. Failure: gains one stack of Kegare no Yamai.

Effect

Each stack reduces Wisdom by 1.

  • Stacks accumulate — multiple failed saves = multiple stacks = increasing Wisdom reduction
  • Affects Insight, Perception, Wisdom saving throws, and spellcasting for Wisdom-based casters

Removal

  • Remove Curse spell removes all stacks
  • The restorative pools in the Grand Hall auto-cleanse on entry — 1 charge per stack removed

frontmatter.name: Kegare no Yamai — Disease of Defilement

text.content:
Type
settlement

"The city that built its fortune on something older than itself."

Overview

Kikyo sits at the eastern edge of the Seidorin Mori -- the Bronze Wood Forest -- organized entirely around harvesting and trading a resource it did not create. The Bronze Wood is to Kikyo what a great mine is to a mining town, except the resource is renewable (slowly), carefully managed, and far more politically complicated.

The city's architecture uses Bronze Wood extensively -- older buildings have developed a patina of aged copper giving streets a warm metallic glow at sunset. Newer construction uses it more sparingly due to licensing restrictions, creating visible stratification between old-money establishments and newer buildings.

Kikyo's economy runs on the licensing system. Every piece of Bronze Wood leaving the forest passes through a licensing transaction administered by Ren Nakamura's office. The paperwork is meticulous; the opportunities for licensed abuse are significant.

Districts / Landmarks

Commercial Quarter -- Trading heart. Merchant warehouses, guild offices, the commodity exchange for Bronze Wood contracts. Ko'jiri was caught performing here.

Administrative Quarter -- Ren Nakamura's offices and civic administration. The licensing offices are among the most visited buildings in Kikyo.

Residential Quarters -- Mixed; older areas near the forest edge contain original families; newer development pushed outward.

Kikyo Guard Compound -- Haruto Masashige's base of operations. Small but highly capable force focused on licensing enforcement and forest protection.

Notable Establishments

Notable establishments are primarily the licensing offices, merchant guild headquarters, and the Guard Compound -- all integral to the Bronze Wood trade that defines the city.

Key Figures

  • Ren Nakamura -- Shicho (Mayor) and Daimyo of Clan Minato -> npcs/ren-nakamura.md
  • Haruto Masashige -- Captain of the Guard; Gold Dragonborn -> npcs/haruto-masashige.md

• Ren Nakamura has discovered the true source of the Bronze Wood's metallic quality and is working with a merchant guild to exploit it.
  • Haruto Masashige is building an informant network and has noticed irregularities in the licensing records.
  • Ko'jiri carries both a legitimate letter from Ren Nakamura and a forged version -- a ticking clock.

DM Secrets

The Bronze Wood Secret The Seidorin Mori grows over an underground branch of Kinkokyo's ancient canal system. The metallic quality is caused by trace gold and copper in groundwater flowing through the buried city's infrastructure for thousands of years. Ren Nakamura has discovered this. His allied merchant guild wants to locate and exploit the source directly, bypassing tree-harvesting -- requiring excavation that would destroy the forest.

Haruto Masashige's True Purpose Masashige suspects something significant about the licensing system. He has noticed irregularities -- specific harvesting zones consistently licensed to a single merchant entity with documentation that obscures the pattern. He is three to four months from a coherent accusation.

Ren Nakamura's Alliance The merchant guild is based in Heian with operations across Hana and beyond. The alliance provides financial support for Clan Minato's elevation ambitions and exclusive export contracts. Nakamura is not villainous by nature but has made compromises requiring further compromises to sustain.

Ko'jiri's Forged Letter -- Ticking Clock Ko'jiri carries a legitimate letter and a forged version requesting additional materials. The real letter has already been sent to Heian through official channels. When the discrepancy is discovered, Ko'jiri's Conditional Pardon will be immediately at risk. Estimate: 2-4 sessions.

Ancient Dragonborn Ritual Knowledge Haruto Masashige's knowledge of ancient Dragonborn rituals includes a purification and restoration rite preserved in his family's oral tradition -- directly applicable to the Nagaji situation if someone connected the dots.

Plot Hooks

  • Haruto sends word to the party in Heian: he has found something in the licensing records connecting to their mission
  • A merchant guild representative in Kikyo attempts to discourage the party from returning there with unusual vehemence
  • Ren Nakamura contacts Ko'jiri separately with an additional, unwritten request
