text.content:
Type
core

A well-prepared meal before rest does more than fill the stomach. In Kagekuni, the art of trail cooking is respected — a traveler who can turn foraged ingredients into something worth eating earns standing at any campfire.

Cooking Rules

Who Can Cook

Any character with proficiency in cook's utensils can attempt to prepare a recipe they know. A character without proficiency can prepare Common recipes only, and does so at disadvantage.

When to Cook

Cooking occurs during a long rest. A meal takes 1 hour to prepare and must be consumed during that same rest to gain its benefits. A cook can prepare one recipe per long rest — enough to serve the entire party (up to 6 servings per preparation).

How It Works

The cook makes a Wisdom (Survival) check using cook's utensils. The DC depends on the recipe's tier.

Recipe Tier Cooking DC Ingredient Rarity Required
Simple 10 Common only
Hearty 13 At least one Uncommon
Refined 16 At least one Rare
Masterwork 20 At least one Very Rare

Success: The meal is prepared. All characters who eat it gain the listed buff after completing the long rest. The buff lasts 8 hours or until the next long rest, whichever comes first.

Failure: The ingredients are consumed but the meal is unremarkable — no buff is granted. The characters still eat (no penalty), but the special properties are lost.

Failure by 5+: The meal is actively unpleasant. Ingredients are wasted. Each character who eats it must succeed on a DC 10 Constitution saving throw or suffer disadvantage on their first ability check after the rest (the aftertaste lingers).

Buff Stacking

A character can benefit from only one meal buff at a time. A new meal replaces the previous buff. Meal buffs do not stack with the Kinryū no Megumi temple blessings — the more powerful effect takes precedence.

Ingredient Grade and Cooking

All gathered ingredients now carry a grade from the materials system: 並 Nami (rough/damaged), 上 Jō (standard market grade), 特上 Tokujō (exceptional), and 極上 Gokujō (peerless). Ingredient grade modifies the cooking check and, on high-grade inputs, can lift a recipe's outcome beyond its base tier.

Ingredient Grade Cooking Check Modifier Effect on Buff
並 Nami −2 to the check Buff duration halved (4 hours) on success
上 Jō +0 (baseline) Standard buff as written
特上 Tokujō +2 to the check Buff applies with advantage on any roll it modifies, or +1 to any flat numeric bonus it grants
極上 Gokujō +5 OR advantage on the check Recipe may be prepared as if one tier higher (Simple→Hearty, Hearty→Refined, etc.) for effect purposes; the cook still rolls against the original DC, and if they would clear the higher-tier DC the meal delivers the upgraded buff described in the recipe's "Gokujō Variant" note (or, absent that note, DM discretion applies an appropriately scaled effect)

When a recipe lists multiple ingredients at different grades, use the lowest grade present as the cooking modifier, but the highest-grade ingredient determines whether the meal is eligible for tier-up. A Gokujō centrepiece can still anchor a recipe built on Jō vegetables; the result is exceptional only if the cook clears the upgraded DC.

Ingredient Cross-Reference

Every recipe ingredient below corresponds to a Part I entry in core/materials.md. When a DM or player wants the full stat block — rarity, yield, weight, base value, grade variants, biomes, cultural notes — that file is the source of truth. Recipes cite ingredients by name only; materials.md carries the mechanical detail.

Recipe List

Simple Recipes (DC 10)

Yama-usagi no Nabemono — Mountain Hare Stew

A straightforward one-pot stew simmered with whatever is at hand. Every traveler in Kagekuni has eaten some version of this on a cold mountain road.

Ingredients: Yama-usagi (1 portion) + Seri or Nobiru (1 portion) + Kome (rice, carried) Buff: Warming Rest — Resistance to cold weather exhaustion checks for 8 hours. Characters ignore the effects of temperatures down to -10°F for the duration. Where Found: Common knowledge — any character proficient with cook's utensils knows this recipe.

Kawa-gani no Suimono — River Crab Clear Soup

Delicate broth made from freshwater crab, wild garlic, and a touch of rice vinegar. Light enough for a warm evening, restorative enough for a weary body.

Ingredients: Kawa-gani (1 portion) + Nobiru (1 portion) + Rice Vinegar (carried) Buff: Clear Head — +1 bonus to Wisdom (Perception) checks for 8 hours. Where Found: Common knowledge — any character proficient with cook's utensils knows this recipe.

Uzura no Yakitori — Grilled Quail Skewers

Quail speared on green sticks and turned over coals, basted with soy paste and sake. Simple, satisfying, and impossible to ruin completely.

Ingredients: Uzura (1 portion) + Shōyu (carried) + Sake (carried) Buff: Road Endurance — +5 feet to walking speed for 8 hours. Where Found: Common knowledge — any character proficient with cook's utensils knows this recipe.

Kinoko Miso-shiru — Mushroom Miso Soup

A traveler's best friend. Dried mushrooms reconstituted in miso broth with whatever greens are available. Warm, umami-rich, and deeply comforting after a day on the road.

Ingredients: Shiitake or Nameko (1 portion) + Miso (carried) + Seri (1 portion, optional) Buff: Settled Stomach — Advantage on Constitution saving throws against poison and disease for 8 hours. Where Found: Common knowledge — any character proficient with cook's utensils knows this recipe.

☆ Tabibito no Zōsui — Traveller's Rice Porridge (Wildcard)

The most forgiving recipe on the road. Whatever meat is at hand goes into the pot with rice and water, simmered until it thickens into something warm and filling. Every version tastes different. None of them taste bad.

Ingredients: Any 1 common meat/fish (1 portion) + Kome (carried) + Shio (carried) or any 1 common herb (1 portion, optional) Buff: Trail Stamina — Recover 1 additional Hit Die at the end of the long rest. Where Found: Common knowledge — any character proficient with cook's utensils knows this recipe.

☆ Nobi no Itamemono — Roadside Stir-Fry (Wildcard)

Hot oil, whatever greens are at hand, a splash of soy paste, and the sizzle that draws everyone around the fire. Speed is the art here — cook fast, eat hot.

Ingredients: Any 2 different common herbs/greens (1 portion each) + Shōyu (carried) + Goma (1 portion, optional) Buff: Light Step — Difficult terrain costs no extra movement for 8 hours. Where Found: Common knowledge — any character proficient with cook's utensils knows this recipe.

Ayu no Shioyaki — Salt-Grilled Sweetfish

Whole sweetfish skewered and grilled upright beside the fire, salted and nothing more. The simplest preparation, and one of the best — the clean, melon-sweet flesh needs no embellishment. Festival food, trail food, good food.

Ingredients: Ayu (1 portion) + Shio (carried) Buff: Refreshed — Advantage on the first ability check made after the long rest. Where Found: Common knowledge — any settlement near a river.

☆ Kinoko no Takikomi-gohan — Mixed Mushroom Rice (Wildcard)

Rice cooked with whatever fungi are available, the mushrooms cut small and stirred through so every bite carries their earthiness. The type of mushroom changes the character of the dish entirely — a different meal at every campsite.

Ingredients: Any 2 different common fungi (1 portion each) + Kome (carried) + Shōyu (carried) Buff: Rooted Rest — +1 bonus to Constitution checks (not saving throws) for 8 hours, including checks to maintain a forced march. Where Found: Common knowledge — any character proficient with cook's utensils knows this recipe.

Hearty Recipes (DC 13)

Kinuo no Sashimi — Gold-Tail Sashimi

Thinly sliced raw kinuo, arranged with care and served with wasabi and soy. The Heian elite pay handsomely for this in restaurants — preparing it fresh from a river catch is a rare pleasure.

Ingredients: Kinuo (1 portion) + Wasabi (1 portion) + Shōyu (carried) Buff: Golden Vigor — Gain temporary hit points equal to your proficiency bonus + your Constitution modifier (minimum 1) after the long rest. These last until depleted or 8 hours, whichever comes first. Where Found: Natsumura (any fisherman will share it for a good story); Heian's Mizu-gai (purchased from a seafood stall for 5 gp).

Inoshishi no Kakuni — Slow-Braised Boar Belly

Wild boar braised for hours in sake, soy, and mountain garlic until the fat renders and the meat falls apart. Rich, dense, and fortifying. A meal for the night before a hard day.

Ingredients: Inoshishi (2 portions) + Nobiru (1 portion) + Sake (carried) + Shōyu (carried) Buff: Boar's Fortitude — +1 bonus to Constitution saving throws for 8 hours. Where Found: Ayame — the inn there serves a version of this to soldiers before the mountain crossing. The innkeeper shares the recipe with anyone who buys a round for the garrison.

Kurokaze Cha-gayu — Black Wind Tea Porridge

Rice porridge steeped with the bitter kurokaze herb of Kaze province. Not delicious, precisely — but the alertness it brings is unmistakable. Gekkō sentries drank this before night watch.

Ingredients: Kurokaze-sō (1 portion) + Kome (carried) + Shio (carried) Buff: Watchful Mind — Cannot be surprised for 8 hours. Additionally, +2 bonus to passive Perception during the duration. Where Found: Kaze province — Akatsuki village elder, or discovered in the abandoned Tsukikage settlement (scroll in a guardhouse).

Enokidake no Takikomi-gohan — Bronze Wood Mushroom Rice

Rice steamed with the copper-noted enokidake mushrooms unique to the Seidōrin Mori, seasoned with Bronze Wood Salt. A dish with a faintly metallic sweetness that lingers.

Ingredients: Enokidake (1 portion) + Seidōrin no Shio (1 portion) + Kome (carried) Buff: Ironbark Resolve — +1 bonus to AC against the first attack that hits you each combat (the bonus is consumed on the first hit, reducing damage by your proficiency bonus; minimum 1). Where Found: Kikyo — lumber merchants share this recipe freely, considering it common regional knowledge.

Hi no Ha Rāmen — Fire Leaf Noodle Broth

A searing broth built on dried dashi, laced with the volcanic hi no ha, and served over thick wheat noodles. Sweat-inducing, breath-clearing, and beloved in Hi province where the locals consider anything less spicy to be "children's food."

Ingredients: Hi no Ha (1 portion) + Dried Dashi (carried) + Kome or noodles (carried) + Shōyu (carried) Buff: Inner Fire — Resistance to fire damage from environmental sources (not attacks) for 8 hours. Additionally, immune to the effects of extreme cold weather for the duration. Where Found: Hi province — any settlement. Enshiro's garrison cooks prepare it daily. Onsen-machi serves an upscale version.

Tsukimisō no Ochazuke — Moonflower Tea Rice

A calming dish of rice bathed in moonflower tea, served with pickled vegetables and a scatter of sesame. Traditionally eaten before diplomatic meetings, but equally useful before any encounter where a steady hand matters.

Ingredients: Tsukimisō (1 portion) + Kome (carried) + Tsukemono (carried) Buff: Serene Focus — +1 bonus to Charisma (Persuasion) and Wisdom (Insight) checks for 8 hours. Where Found: Heian — a tea house in the Ryū Jikuchiku sells this recipe for 10 gp. Alternatively, shrine monks at Kodan no Jinja share it with respectful visitors.

Unagi no Kabayaki — Grilled Eel with Sweet Glaze

Freshwater eel split, boned, and grilled repeatedly with a glaze of soy, sake, and a touch of sweetness. The fat renders between each pass over the coals until the skin crisps and the flesh melts. Regarded as a stamina food across all provinces — no coincidence that eel vendors do brisk business before military campaigns.

Ingredients: Unagi (1 portion) + Shōyu (carried) + Sake (carried) + Sanshō (1 portion) Buff: Eel's Endurance — Advantage on Constitution checks to maintain concentration and to avoid exhaustion from forced marches for 8 hours. Where Found: Natsumura — the eel-griller on the wharf teaches the technique to anyone patient enough to watch. Nishihara's river market also knows it.

☆ Yama no Nabe — Mountain Hot Pot (Wildcard)

The quintessential trail meal for a cold evening in high country. A communal pot over the fire, filled with whatever the day's foraging turned up — any game, any greens, any mushroom. The broth does the work.

Ingredients: Any 1 uncommon meat/fish (1 portion) + any 1 common or uncommon herb/green (1 portion) + any 1 common or uncommon fungi (1 portion) + Dried Dashi or Miso (carried) Buff: Shared Warmth — All characters who share the meal gain +2 to saving throws against cold weather effects and exhaustion from exposure for 8 hours. If at least 3 characters share the meal, each also gains 1d4 temporary hit points. Where Found: Ayame — soldiers share their version around the garrison fire. Takamine — the mountain guides know a dozen variations.

Kamo no Tsukune — Wild Duck Meatball Skewers

Wild duck minced with ginger and scallion, shaped into small balls and grilled over charcoal. The outside chars while the inside stays tender. Simple construction, but the richness of the duck meat carries a depth that domestic poultry cannot match.

Ingredients: Kamo (1 portion) + Myōga (1 portion) + Shōyu (carried) Buff: Sharpened Senses — +2 to passive Perception and +1 to initiative rolls for 8 hours. Where Found: Koriwara — a retired samurai who runs a yakitori stall in the market ward teaches the recipe to anyone who compliments his cooking with apparent sincerity.

Umikaze Chazuke — Sea Wind Rice

A coastal traveller's meal — hot dashi poured over rice, topped with the thick, salty umikaze greens and flaked fish. The briny greens cut the richness of the broth. Nami fishermen eat this before dawn watches when the storms are coming.

Ingredients: Umikaze-na (1 portion) + any 1 common fish (1 portion) + Kome (carried) + Dried Dashi (carried) Buff: Storm Ready — Advantage on Strength (Athletics) checks made to resist being knocked prone or pushed, and advantage on saving throws against effects caused by wind or lightning for 8 hours. Where Found: Nami coastline — any fishing village. The recipe travels with the tides.

Iwatake no Nimono — Simmered Rock Mushroom

Rock mushroom rehydrated in dashi, simmered slowly until the leathery texture softens into something rich and gelatinous. The mineral depth of the fungus fills the broth. Monk's food — austere, deliberate, and quietly satisfying.

Ingredients: Iwatake (1 portion) + Dried Dashi (carried) + Shōyu (carried) + Miso (carried) Buff: Mountaineer's Grip — +2 to Strength (Athletics) checks for climbing and advantage on saving throws against falling for 8 hours. Where Found: Takamine — a monastery cook shares this with pilgrims who help with kitchen duties. Also known at high-altitude shrines throughout Sora.

Refined Recipes (DC 16)

Seireiuo no Sunomono — Spirit Fish Vinegar Salad

Translucent spirit fish, briefly cured in rice vinegar, served over shredded daikon with a whisper of wasabi. The flesh still carries a faint luminescence on the plate. The taste is unlike anything from ordinary waters.

Ingredients: Seireiuo (1 portion) + Wasabi (1 portion) + Rice Vinegar (carried) Buff: Sei Attunement — +1 bonus to spell attack rolls and spell save DCs for 8 hours. Non-casters instead gain advantage on saving throws against magical effects. Where Found: Yōsei Mori — the Forest of Spirits faction shares this with allies who prove trustworthy. Alternatively, a scroll may be found in ruins with sei-active water sources.

Ryūjika no Sumibi-yaki — Charcoal-Grilled Dragon Deer

Dragon deer venison, seared over hardwood charcoal and finished with a glaze of sake and dragon salt. The meat's natural warmth intensifies over the flame. Those who eat it report a sensation of quiet strength settling into the bones.

Ingredients: Ryūjika (1 portion) + Ryūjio (1 portion) + Sake (carried) Buff: Draconic Fortitude — Gain advantage on death saving throws for 8 hours. Additionally, when you spend Hit Dice during a short rest within the duration, you may reroll any Hit Die that shows a 1 or 2 (keeping the new result). Where Found: Ancient Guard knowledge — Benkei knows this recipe and will share it with a party that has earned his trust. May also be inscribed on stone near Progenitor shrine sites.

Kageboushi no Ankake — Shadow Cap Mushroom in Thickened Broth

Shadow mushrooms simmered in a rich thickened dashi, their smoky depth intensified by slow reduction. The broth is dark as ink and just as staining. Eaten in near-darkness in Kaze, where they say the dish teaches you to see without light.

Ingredients: Kageboushi (1 portion) + Kuro-koshō (1 portion) + Dried Dashi (carried) + Shōyu (carried) Buff: Shadow Sight — Gain darkvision 30 feet for 8 hours. Characters who already have darkvision extend its range by 30 feet. Additionally, +2 to Dexterity (Stealth) checks in dim light or darkness. Where Found: Kaze province — the Black Lily monastery. The recipe is not secret, but the monastery shares it only with those who have done the Order a service.

Seikinoko no Chawanmushi — Sei Mushroom Custard

A savory egg custard steamed with luminescent sei mushrooms, their violet-blue glow dimming slowly as the custard sets. Served in ceramic cups and eaten with a small wooden spoon. The flavor is elusive — forest, rain, and something older.

Ingredients: Seikinoko (1 portion) + Seri (1 portion) + Dried Dashi (carried) Buff: Sei Reservoir — Recover one expended spell slot of 1st or 2nd level at the end of the long rest (in addition to normal recovery). Non-casters instead recover an additional Hit Die. Where Found: Mori no Sato village on the Yōsei Mori border — the village herbalist teaches it to those who bring her a fresh seikinoko specimen as proof of their foraging ability.

Hinotake no Dengaku — Fire Stalk Grilled with Miso Glaze

Fire stalk mushrooms, carefully peeled to avoid the caustic outer membrane, then glazed with sweetened miso and grilled until the edges char. The heat builds slowly — not unpleasant, but insistent. Hi province miners eat this before descending into volcanic shafts.

Ingredients: Hinotake (1 portion) + Miso (carried) + Sake (carried) Buff: Volcanic Resilience — Resistance to fire damage (all sources, including attacks) for 8 hours. Where Found: Hi province — Kurokawa village. The obsidian crafters share it with outsiders who help with a day's labor in the fields. Also found carved into a wall near the Crimson Shrine's outer approach.

Oniuo no Nitsuke — Demon Fish Braised in Soy

The demon fish's bony plates are pried apart to reveal dense white flesh, braised in a dark reduction of soy, sake, and ginger until the meat turns glossy and falls from the bone. The fishermen who hunt oniuo say the fight to land one is half the preparation — the braising is the easy part.

Ingredients: Oniuo (1 portion) + Tsuchi-shōga (1 portion) + Shōyu (carried) + Sake (carried) Buff: Predator's Tenacity — When you are reduced below half your hit point maximum, gain +1 to attack rolls until the end of your next turn. This triggers once per combat. Where Found: Kaze province — a ferryman on the Kagerō River who has fished its deep pools for forty years. He teaches the recipe as payment for help clearing debris from his crossing.

Kumokiji no Mushiyaki — Cloud Pheasant Steamed in Leaves

Cloud pheasant breast wrapped in murasaki-ha leaves and steamed over a low fire. The purple leaf imparts a faint sweetness and tints the meat a pale violet. A dish of high altitude and rare beauty — the kind of thing you eat once and remember for the rest of your life.

Ingredients: Kumokiji (1 portion) + Murasaki-ha (1 portion) + Yuzu (1 portion) Buff: Clarity of the Heights — Advantage on Wisdom saving throws for 8 hours. Where Found: Takamine — an elderly guide who leads parties above the cloud line. She cooks this at the summit camp and shares the recipe only with those who complete the ascent without complaint.

☆ Sansai no Sunomono — Wild Harvest Vinegar Salad (Wildcard)

A dish of raw preparation — whatever rare greens and herbs are at hand, sliced thin and dressed in vinegar with a scatter of sesame. No cooking, no broth, no fire. The ingredients must be exceptional, because nothing hides behind heat.

Ingredients: Any 2 different rare herbs/greens (1 portion each) + Rice Vinegar (carried) + Goma (1 portion) Buff: Sei Sensitivity — Gain the ability to detect sei-active objects and creatures within 10 feet for 8 hours (functions as detect magic, but limited to sei energy only). Where Found: Yōsei Mori border communities — shared among herbalists who trade in rare plants. A version of the recipe circulates among the Seishin Enclave's outer circle.

Kaseki-gani no Kani-miso — Stone Crab Tomalley Gratin

The dense claw meat of the stone crab, mixed with its own tomalley and broiled in the upturned shell until it sets into a rich, savoury custard. The mineral crust of the shell chars and seasons the dish from without. A cave-diver's reward — earned by anyone brave enough to wade into a tidal cavern.

Ingredients: Kaseki-gani (1 portion) + Umi-shio (1 portion) + Sake (carried) Buff: Ironhide — Gain +1 to AC for 8 hours (does not stack with shield or magical armor bonuses above +2). Where Found: Mizu coastline — the pearl-divers of Umigakure know it. Also traded among the sailors who shelter in Nami's cove villages during storm season.

Yūrei-kusa no Chakai — Ghost Grass Ceremony Tea

Not a meal in the traditional sense — a tea ceremony built around the pale, cold-to-the-touch ghost grass of Kaze's ruined settlements. The preparation is slow and deliberate: the grass is steeped three times, each steeping drawing out a different quality. The first is bitter. The second is smooth. The third carries something that makes the drinker acutely aware of nearby presences.

Ingredients: Yūrei-kusa (1 portion) + Kome (carried, for accompanying rice cakes) + Shio (carried) Buff: Spirit Sight — Gain the ability to see invisible creatures and objects within 15 feet for 8 hours. Additionally, you cannot be surprised by undead or spirit creatures. Where Found: Akatsuki — an elderly herbalist living on the edge of the settlement. The recipe is also referenced in fragmentary notes found in Tsukikage's abandoned guardhouse.

Masterwork Recipes (DC 20)

Ryūketsu Kaiseki — Dragon's Blood Banquet

A multi-course meal built around the impossibly rare dragon's blood flower. The petals are incorporated into every element — infused into the broth, pressed into the rice, scattered over seared venison. The meal takes two hours to prepare and demands the cook's complete attention. Those who eat it feel, for a time, as though something ancient is watching over them.

Ingredients: Ryūketsu-bana (1 portion) + Ryūjika (1 portion) + Kinuo (1 portion) + Ryūjio (1 portion) + Kome (carried) Buff: Progenitor's Blessing — +1 bonus to all saving throws for 8 hours. Once during the duration, when you are reduced to 0 hit points, you may immediately regain hit points equal to 1d10 + your character level. This consumes the blessing entirely. Where Found: Cannot be purchased or casually discovered. Possible sources: deep within Progenitor-associated ruins; a gift from a being of great age and wisdom; reward for completing a quest tied to dragon legacy.

Seiryoku Nabe — Sei-Vigor Hot Pot

A communal hot pot built around the luminous seiryoku grass, simmered with spirit fish, sei mushrooms, and whatever the wilderness provides. The pot glows faintly as it cooks. The ingredients must all be fresh — no dried or preserved components. Eating it is a communal act; the buff only functions if shared among at least two people.

Ingredients: Seiryoku-gusa (1 portion) + Seireiuo (1 portion) + Seikinoko (1 portion) + any 2 common herbs/greens Buff: Sei Communion — All characters who share the meal gain the following for 8 hours: advantage on concentration checks, +1 to all ability checks, and the ability to communicate telepathically with other characters who shared the meal (30 ft range). Requires at least 2 participants. Where Found: The Seishin Enclave on Unmeijima. Alternatively, fragments of this recipe appear across multiple locations — a hermit's cave in Sora, a shrine wall in the Yōsei Mori, a damaged scroll in the Temple of Kinryū. Assembling the complete recipe from fragments is itself a quest.

☆ Hoshizora Kaiseki — Starlight Banquet (Wildcard)

A multi-course meal that can only be prepared under open sky when Ryūgetsu is visible. The centrepiece is a dish built around any very rare ingredient — meat, herb, or fungus — supported by complementary rare and uncommon components. The specific courses change depending on what the cook has gathered. No two Starlight Banquets are alike. The meal takes two hours to prepare and demands the cook's full attention and a flawless performance.

Ingredients: Any 1 very rare ingredient (1 portion) + any 1 rare ingredient from a different category (1 portion) + any 1 uncommon seasoning (1 portion) + Kome (carried) Buff: Starlit Resolve — +1 to all ability scores (not modifiers) for 8 hours. Additionally, the first time during the duration that you would fail a saving throw, you may choose to succeed instead (consumes this portion of the blessing). Where Found: Cannot be purchased. The recipe exists as a philosophical framework rather than a fixed formula — learned from a master cook of extraordinary skill. Possible sources: a retired imperial chef living in seclusion, the kitchens of the Hoshimori observatory, or a spirit of the road who tests travellers with riddles before teaching the art.

Ryūkinoko Ryōri — Dragon Fungus Feast

A meal built around the impossible warmth of the dragon fungus, its golden glow casting slow amber light across the cook's hands as the flesh is sliced thin and layered with seasonal accompaniments. Those who eat it describe a feeling of being held — not restrained, but supported, as though the earth itself had placed a hand beneath them.

Ingredients: Ryūkinoko (1 portion) + Ryūjio (1 portion) + any 1 rare herb (1 portion) + Dried Dashi (carried) Buff: Progenitor's Calm — For 8 hours, you are immune to the frightened condition. Additionally, you gain advantage on death saving throws and may add your Wisdom modifier to death saving throws. Where Found: A Progenitor-associated cave system deep beneath the mountains. The recipe is understood instinctively by anyone who has been in the presence of a living Progenitor. It may also be discovered carved into stone near a dragon's resting chamber.

Named Beast Recipes — Yama-no-Ōkami

These recipes exist only because the party slew the Mountain God of the Tenchūsan Ren and harvested the beast with uncanny skill. Every component is single-grade-locked at 極上 Gokujō (see core/materials.md → Named Beast Harvests → Yama-no-Ōkami (Slain)), which means each dish below automatically clears the grade modifier for tier-up eligibility. A competent cook who can clear the upgraded DC delivers a peerless meal; a less skilled cook still produces an exceptional one. There is no "ordinary" preparation of these components — the beast will not permit it.

These recipes are not on the random loot table. They can only be learned by DM placement — a retired hunter's journal, a shrine-keeper who remembers the old rites, or a moment of insight at the campfire after a long day of travel. They are one-time rewards for a one-time harvest.

Ōkami no Kakuni — Mountain God's Braised Fang-Meat (Masterwork)

Ōkami-niku slow-braised for hours in sake, shōyu, and mountain garlic until the fat renders and the meat falls apart in sheets. The flesh is impossibly tender and carries a faint metallic brightness on the tongue — the taste of a beast that lived at the edge of the spirit world. Those who eat it describe dreams of high passes they have never walked.

Ingredients: Ōkami-niku (2 portions, Gokujō) + Nobiru (1 portion) + Sake (carried) + Shōyu (carried) Cooking DC: 20 (Masterwork) Buff: Mountain God's Fortitude — For 8 hours, gain +2 to Constitution saving throws and resistance to cold damage. The first time during the duration you would drop to 0 HP, you instead drop to 1 HP; this benefit is consumed on use. Gokujō Variant (tier-up): As above, plus the eater gains advantage on Strength checks and saving throws for the duration, and may add +1d4 to any single attack roll, ability check, or saving throw during the duration (consumed on use). Where Found: Not on the scroll tables. Learned only from direct instruction — a hunter who witnessed the harvest, or intuited by a character with proficiency in cook's utensils who spends downtime experimenting with the ingredients.

Reikokoro no Kaiseki — Spirit Heart Banquet (Masterwork, Legendary)

A single-sitting banquet built around the Reikokoro — the Spirit Heart — cooked in a sealed clay vessel with the marrow, liver, and storm-sinew of the same beast. The heart is cooked whole, and the vessel must not be opened until the moment of serving. The meal feeds six and cannot be preserved, split, or carried. It is eaten in silence, by the same fire that prepared it, within the same rest period. Those who share it describe sensing the wolf's final thoughts — the smell of snow, the weight of the mountain, the brief and perfect stillness before death.

Ingredients: Reikokoro (1 portion, Gokujō, feeds six) + Shirokiba no Zui (1 portion, Gokujō) + Yama no Kimo (1 portion, Gokujō) + Arashi-suji (1 portion, Gokujō) + Kome (carried) + Sake (carried) Cooking DC: 22 (Masterwork — single hardest check in the recipe list) Buff: Bond of the Mountain God — All characters who share the meal gain the following for 24 hours (not 8): +2 to all saving throws, advantage on Wisdom (Survival) checks made in mountain terrain, and the ability to sense the direction and approximate distance of any one willing participant at will. Additionally, the first time each character would drop to 0 HP during the duration, they instead drop to 1 HP. This benefit is consumed individually per character. Gokujō Variant (tier-up): As above, plus each participant gains 2d10 temporary hit points for the duration, and once during the 24 hours may choose to succeed on a single failed saving throw (each character, once, consumed on use). Where Found: Cannot be purchased, found, or stumbled upon. The recipe is knowledge carried by those who remember the old compacts between hunters and mountain kami. Possible sources: a retired hunter who served a daimyo of the Tenchūsan Ren; a shrine-keeper at a high-altitude shrine who senses the components the party carries; a dream-vision received by a character during a long rest in the mountains while carrying the Reikokoro. One-time meal: The ingredients for this recipe cannot be reassembled. Once the Reikokoro is consumed, this dish cannot be made again.

Arashi-suji no Dashi — Storm-Sinew Broth (Refined)

A broth rendered from the beast's sinew — stringy, slow to cook, and startlingly clear when it finishes. The first sip is unremarkable. The second carries the taste of wind over a high ridge. The drinker finds their step lighter and their lungs deeper.

Ingredients: Arashi-suji (1 portion, Gokujō) + Shio (carried) + any 1 uncommon herb (1 portion) Cooking DC: 16 (Refined) Buff: Storm-Lung — For 8 hours, walking speed increases by 10 ft, you can hold your breath for three times the usual duration, and you have advantage on Constitution saving throws made to resist exhaustion from forced march or harsh weather. Gokujō Variant (tier-up): As above, plus you gain the ability to take the Dash action as a bonus action (once per round) for the duration. Where Found: The simplest of the Yama-no-Ōkami recipes. A character with proficiency in cook's utensils can derive this from the sinew itself after spending an hour studying it at a campfire — the preparation is obvious to anyone who has worked with beast sinew before.

Design Notes (DM Only)

Wildcard Recipes (☆): Recipes marked with ☆ accept flexible ingredient substitutions — "any common meat," "any 2 rare herbs," etc. These are deliberately front-loaded in the system so players who engage with gathering early feel rewarded regardless of which specific ingredients they find. Wildcards also encourage experimentation and make the system feel less like a shopping list. The DM should let players describe what they're making with the specific ingredients they chose — this creates organic flavour and roleplay moments without requiring a unique recipe for every combination.

Power Calibration: Meal buffs are intentionally minor — comparable to a cantrip or a minor boon, not a spell effect. They reward engagement with the gathering and cooking system without creating a mandatory pre-combat checklist. The Masterwork recipes are deliberately harder to achieve and more impactful, serving as adventure rewards in their own right.

Encouraging the System: The best way to introduce this is organically — an NPC cooking at a campfire, a recipe scroll found as incidental loot, a grateful innkeeper sharing a family recipe. Let the players discover that the system exists rather than presenting it as a mechanic to optimize.

Sei Ingredients and Mystery: The sei-active ingredients (seireiuo, seikinoko, seiryoku-gusa, ryūketsu-bana) are deliberately tied to the world's deeper lore. Finding them should feel meaningful — these are ingredients that connect to the living magic of the world, not commodity goods. Their inability to be preserved reinforces this: they are gifts from the moment, not resources to stockpile.

Interaction with Kinryū no Megumi: The temple pool blessings are significantly more powerful than meal buffs and represent divine-tier effects. Meal buffs are mortal-tier — the difference should be felt. If both are active, the more powerful effect (always the temple blessing) takes precedence; the meal buff is suppressed but not consumed, resuming if the blessing expires first.

The Divine Structure

  • Single supreme divine entity — analogous to Christianity's monotheism
  • Historical deities venerated as saint-equivalents — subordinate to supreme being
  • Shrines and temples may be dedicated to specific divine figures without contradicting monotheistic faith
  • Different clans/regions have patron divine figures
  • Dragons occupy a unique revered position — between saints-equivalent and kami
  • Kami (nature spirits) exist as a separate category of minor spiritual beings

The Seven Dragon Clans — Founding Era

Clan Dragon Color Island Domain
Crimson Clan Akaryū Red Fushichō Fire, volcanic power, strength
Azure Clan Aoryū Blue Kawa Water, storms, coastal protection
Emerald Clan Midoryū Green Hokori Nature, earth, healing, balance
Onyx Clan Kokuryū Black Tatara Shadow, darkness, cunning, mystery
Golden Clan Kinryū Gold Hokori (central highlands) Honor, justice, nobility, mediation
Silver Clan Ginryū Silver Fuukajima Grace, purity, ice, cold, moon/stars
Amethyst Clan Murasakiryū Purple Shizukajima Arcane knowledge, divination, mystical arts

First Emperor

Tenryū no Mikado — descended from both Crimson and Golden bloodlines; united clans ~8000; established first imperial dynasty

Dragon Legacy in Society

  • Dragonborn within Kugai claim descent from dragon founders — legitimizes noble authority
  • Many daimyo trace lineage to founding dragons
  • Temples, shrines, festivals honor dragon ancestors annually
  • The arcadian (elf) imperial line descended from dragon-settler intermingling

Dragons Today — CRITICAL SECRET (DM Only)

  • All seven founding dragons are still alive — hidden, withdrawn
  • World considers them purely historical and mythological
  • Dragons are extremely rare in current era — occasional individuals exist
  • Dragon eggs believed to be fossils — viability unknown to world at large
  • Dragon eggs are highly collectible
  • The Order of the Ancient Guard exists specifically to protect the living dragons

text.content:
The Realm of Seizan

  • Magic energy called sei flows through all living things
  • Three stars, four seasons, four moons
  • Astrological events driven by stellar and lunar cycles overlay the standard seasons
  • The archipelago of Kagekuni ("Shrouded Isles") is the campaign setting
  • Located in the Raijin no Fukai sea
  • Shaped by competing influences of Susanoo and Tsukuyomi (celestial, not divine)
  • Temperate climate with north/south variation; monsoons and typhoons are regular
  • Frequent earthquakes, tsunamis, and volcanic activity shape culture and architecture
  • Four moons create complex tidal patterns that influence culture and magic

The Miyosai System — Astronomy

Three Stars (Taiyō)

Name Type Character Magical Influence
Amaterasu Primary golden-yellow Stable, foundational warmth Core life energy; baseline sei
Susanoo Smaller blue-white dwarf Complex orbit; closest during Nagorikaze Water magic, healing, purification; "ghost rainbows"
Tsukuyomi Larger deep-red dwarf Elongated orbit; furthest during Long Shadow; perihelion casts daytime shadows Transformation, energy manipulation

Note: These are purely celestial phenomena named after older divine concepts. Stars are not worshipped directly.

Four Moons — The Sisters' Tears (Tsuki)

Name Translation Character Notable Influence
Aokiba Blue Fang Crystalline, elliptical orbit; appears toothed Tidal surges during Tatsunami; navigation hazard
Kagetsu Shadow Moon Largest; absorbs light; halo effect at full Dreams under full face carry mystical significance
Nagikumo Gentle Cloud Smallest but appears large; soft inner glow Tranquil; perpetually luminous even in shadow
Ryūgetsu Dragon Moon Most complex orbit; color-shifting; linked to Shizukanami gravitationally Dragon's Rest — auspicious pauses for weather and spirit magic; auroras during Hikarishou

Lunar Sei Influence: Secondary sei signatures — subtler than stars. Three tracks: tidal (physical), omen (divinatory), sei amplification (mild magical resonance). Compounded stellar + lunar alignments produce meaningfully greater effects.

Seven Planets (Wakusi)

Name Translation Notes
Akahoshi — Innermost; molten; visible in daylight as crimson point
Akasa Red Sand Crimson desert world; influences weather during Tatsunami
Asahikawa River of Dawn Golden, reflective; brightest morning object; herald of celestial events
Seizan — Our world — the balance point
Shizukanami Silent Wave Frozen ocean; gravitationally linked to Ryūgetsu; blue glow under Susanoo
Kōrigami God of Ice Eternal winter; influences winter severity during Shinmyouji
Yamiyo Eternal Night Outermost; shadow magic potency; Shadow Resonance when aligned with Tsukuyomi

Seasons

Seizan experiences four standard seasons, identical to Earth's cycle:

Season Japanese Name Months
Spring Haru Yayoi (3), Uzuki (4), Satsuki (5)
Summer Natsu Minazuki (6), Fumizuki (7), Hazuki (8)
Fall Aki Nagatsuki (9), Kannazuki (10), Shimotsuki (11)
Winter Fuyu Shiwasu (12), Mutsuki (1), Kisaragi (2)

Current campaign date: Nagatsuki 1, 16744 (early Aki)

Calendar — Traditional Months

Month Name Meaning
1 Mutsuki (睦月) Month of Affection
2 Kisaragi (如月) Month of Changing Clothes
3 Yayoi (弥生) Month of New Life
4 Uzuki (卯月) Month of Deutzia
5 Satsuki (皐月) Month of Early Rice
6 Minazuki (水無月) Month of Water
7 Fumizuki (文月) Month of Letters
8 Hazuki (葉月) Month of Leaves
9 Nagatsuki (長月) Month of Long Nights
10 Kannazuki (神無月) Month of No Gods
11 Shimotsuki (霜月) Month of Frost
12 Shiwasu (師走) Month of Running Priests

Astrological Events

Seizan's complex stellar and lunar system produces named astrological phenomena that overlay the standard seasons. These are not seasons themselves but recurring celestial events with observable effects on weather, tides, sei, and the natural world.

Solar Events (driven by the three-star system):

Name Celestial Cause Effects
Nagorikaze Susanoo draws close to Seizan Blue-white atmospheric phenomena; ghost rainbows; water magic intensifies
Shinmyōji Kōrigami at peak influence Luminescent mists over Kagekuni; winter severity increases
Long Shadow Tsukuyomi at furthest point (aphelion) Transformation magic weakens; shadows behave strangely

Lunar Events (driven by the four-moon system):

Name Celestial Cause Effects
Tatsunami Four-moon alignment convergence Destructive tidal surges; coastal flooding; navigation hazards. Typically late Aki through mid-Haru.
Hikarishō Ryūgetsu full phase alignment Celestial dragon auroras; sei amplification; spirit activity increases

Additional solar and lunar events exist but are less commonly named or studied. Seimasters at Seishin maintain observational records of celestial alignments and their correlations to sei fluctuation.

Kannazuki — The Month of No Gods

The name Kannazuki predates recorded history. Common folk use it without thought — "the gods are away" is a saying during the tenth month, though no one remembers where the gods supposedly go. Ancient texts in the Great Library of Kawa reference a gathering of "the great ones" during this month, but the passages are fragmentary and often dismissed as allegory.

Discovery path: Research in the Great Library; conversations with Ancient Guard members; study of pre-Reckoning texts.

Kannazuki — The True Origin

The name is a historical fossil from the earliest age when the seven Progenitor dragons did physically gather during the tenth month. The tradition outlived the practice by millennia. The Ancient Guard recognizes the irony — the "Month of No Gods" was originally the month when all the gods were present in one place. Now, with the Progenitors slumbering, the name is accidentally accurate again for entirely different reasons.

The Great Aphelion and the Sei Drought

The sei drought began with the stellar decline of the War of Fractured Banners era (~12605). As Susanoo and Tsukuyomi entered their long retreat from the barycenter of the Miyosai trinary system, sei accessibility diminished gradually. The first secondary star crossed below naked-eye visibility around ~12806, marking the beginning of the dark ages. The Temple of Oryuzan Tenku-ji fell in 13088 — a consequence of the drought, not its cause.

The three stars of the Miyosai system orbit a common gravitational center (barycenter) on different orbital inclinations. Planets orbit Amaterasu and travel with it; moons orbit Seizan directly. Neither participated in the Great Aphelion — only the three stars reached maximum mutual distance. The Great Aphelion itself (~14344) was the absolute nadir: Amaterasu at one extreme of its barycentric arc carrying Seizan with it, while Susanoo and Tsukuyomi sat at opposing extremes on their own inclined planes. The geometry was not a uniform recession but a three-dimensional separation — the distances compounded geometrically.

Amaterasu never went dark. Its baseline sei sustained life, agriculture, and the physical world throughout the dark ages. The world retained normal day/night cycles. What was lost was the complex magical expression that depended on the full trinary system — Susanoo's contribution to water magic and healing, Tsukuyomi's contribution to transformation and energy manipulation. The dark ages were cultural and intellectual collapse rather than extinction.

The Progenitors entered their slumber during this same period. Whether the aphelion caused the slumber, the slumber caused the sei drought, or the aphelion caused both remains unknown — even to the Ancient Guard. The slow return of sei beginning 15962 (First Talents) correlates with Susanoo's partial orbital return after dawn (15883). The Great Awakening (~16693) marks the moment all three stars became clearly visible simultaneously — effectively the moment Tsukuyomi's return crossed the threshold of reliability. The orbital correction is still ongoing — the current celestial configuration has not yet fully returned to its pre-Aphelion state.

This connection is not understood by any living scholar. The data exists in fragmentary astronomical records across multiple institutions, but no one has assembled the complete picture. The Golden Dragon Clan's observatory at Ōryūzan Tenkū-ji contained the most complete model of the Miyosai system ever constructed — mechanical and arcane, capable of projecting celestial positions across millennia. It has not been operational since the temple fell.

See also: core/great-aphelion.md — full canonical timeline, orbital mechanics, and orrery projection sequence.

The Archipelago of Kagekuni

Five Major Islands

Island Character Key Feature
Hokori Largest; four tectonic plates; X-shaped Primary campaign island; capital Heian
Kawa Eastern; mostly submerged except winter Agricultural heartland; Great Library; Seirei Mizuumi
Fushichō Northern; volcanic Hi no Toride mountains; ancient secrets; Akaho Sanmyaku erupting
Yurei Haunted; barren; avoided Ancient curse; specters and monsters; Kuroshi Temple
Tatara Southern; mountainous Dwarven/gnomish heartland; Zirak vs Glimfyr conflict

Minor Islands

Fuukajima, Gyoshima, Kakujima, Shukajima, Unmeijima, Ryūhajima, Shizukajima, Takarajima, and others.

Unmeijima — Home of the city of Seishin (magical research); Order of the Tranquil Lotus monastery at Kazehama.

Tone, Aesthetic & Design Principles

Core Tone

  • Medieval Japan as cultural and historical backbone — not generic fantasy
  • High fantasy layered over authentic historical touchstones
  • Shifts fluidly: quiet beauty ↔ political intrigue ↔ brutal conflict
  • Honor, shame, duty, tension between order and chaos are recurring themes

The World Feels Otherworldly

Consistent cosmetic departures from reality — woven naturally, never called out as anomalies:

  • Trees with bark of burnished bronze or pale crystal
  • Grass in deep violet or indigo hues
  • Rivers faintly luminescent at night
  • Fog carrying incense scent without source
  • Constellations that don't match our sky
  • The bronze-leafed Seidōrin Mori — metallic trees harvested for weapons
  • Sei flowing visibly through natural phenomena

Historical Grounding (Second Priority After Continuity)

  • Feudal structure: Emperor, Shogun, Daimyo, Samurai, Peasantry — titles and land rights carry real weight
  • Bushido and social codes: honor, duty, sacrifice, and shame govern behavior
  • Religion and spirituality: Shinto animism, Buddhist philosophy, ancestor veneration
  • Arts and architecture: tatami, shoji, castle towns, torii gates, tea ceremony, noh theatre
  • Conflict and politics: clan rivalries, succession disputes, ronin, peasant uprisings

D&D 5e Compatibility

  • All mechanical content grounded in 5e rules
  • Homebrew clearly labeled
  • Seimasters map to wizards, sorcerers, monks
  • Honor mechanic: -2 on Honor ability checks for marginalized races in social situations

Foundry VTT Notes

  • Secret blocks used within journal entries for DM-only content
  • Player handouts prefixed with character name for easy sorting
  • Location journals pinned to maps
  • Active Objectives journal maintained as living document
  • One entry per subject; use journal links for wiki-style navigation

Preserve Mystery

  • Not everything needs to be explained
  • Leave room for improvisation and surprise
  • The living dragons secret is the campaign's deepest thread — never surface prematurely

Captain of the Guard — Kikyo

Appearance

Public Role

Captain of the Guard in Kikyo, operating from the Kikyo Guard Compound. Maintains a small but highly capable force; primary duties are licensing enforcement and forest protection for the Seidōrin Mori (Bronze Wood Forest). Building an informant network in Kikyo.

Personality

Stoic, disciplined; fierce loyalty; strong sense of justice.

Relationship to Party

Arrested Ko'jiri in Kikyo before the situation was resolved by Ren Nakamura's offer of the Summons and Conditional Pardon. Their initial interaction was adversarial but professional. Can become a staunch ally to those who prove their integrity.

True Nature

Building his informant network not simply for Kikyo's local security but because he suspects something significant is happening with the Bronze Wood licensing system. He has noticed irregularities in the licensing records — specific harvesting zones consistently licensed to a single merchant entity, with documentation that is technically correct but structured to obscure the pattern. He is three to four months away from having enough evidence to bring forward as a coherent accusation.

Connections

Knows ancient Dragonborn rituals potentially crucial to certain quests. His family's oral tradition preserves knowledge from the Golden Dragon Clan's Dragonborn lineages.

Quest Seeds

QUEST SEED Haruto sends word to the party in Heian: he has found something in the licensing records that connects to their mission and needs outside help to pursue it.

Campaign Secrets

Haruto Masashige's knowledge of ancient Dragonborn rituals is not merely historical curiosity. It includes a purification and restoration rite that the Golden Dragon Clan's Dragonborn lineages preserved — a rite that is part of the process for reversing certain magical transformations. He doesn't know its current relevance, but the ritual exists in his family's oral tradition and would be directly applicable to the Nagaji situation if someone connected the dots.

His licensing investigation is on a collision course with Ren Nakamura's secret alliance with the merchant guild. When these threads converge, Haruto will be in danger.

Plot Threads

  • Bronze Wood licensing investigation — will eventually expose Ren Nakamura's merchant guild alliance
  • Ancient Dragonborn restoration rite — directly applicable to reversing the Nagaji transformation
  • Ko'jiri connection — their adversarial first meeting could become a significant alliance
  • Potential danger when his investigation threatens the merchant guild's interests

Advised Relc to leave Kōriwara and journey outward. Blessed Relc's departure. Relc visited Elder Sato before departing. He has not told Relc everything he knows.

True Nature

More than a simple village elder. His decades of accumulated knowledge, his connection to the Order of the Sacred Grove, and his quiet role as a node in networks that extend far beyond a mountain foothills village give Kōriwara significance entirely disproportionate to its size.

Connections

Mid-rank member of the Order of the Sacred Grove. Has interacted with Order of the Ancient Guard agents on multiple occasions, including with Solas Evergreen directly. His community network in the Mizu foothills region could help establish Yasutake Mai in Sunsato if the party makes the connection.

Quest Seeds

QUEST SEED Sato sends word through a traveling merchant heading toward Heian: he needs to speak with Relc; something has happened near the sacred grove that he cannot explain and cannot address alone. [QUEST SEED] A stranger arrived in Kōriwara asking questions about Relc and where they had gone; Sato gave nothing away but is concerned about whether Relc is being watched. [QUEST SEED] If the party introduces Yasutake Mai to Sato's community network, they earn a favor with Sato and plant a contact in the north Mizu foothills.

Campaign Secrets

Sato knows Solas was Ancient Guard (not just Sacred Grove). He knows what the Ancient Guard is and, broadly, what it protects. He has not told Relc because he was following Solas's instruction to let Relc develop organically — and because he judged Relc was not yet ready for the weight of the full picture.

One of the three stones referenced in Solas's cipher poem is in Kōriwara — specifically, in the sacred grove above the village. It is a naturally occurring stone with unusual surface striations that, when viewed from a specific angle at dawn, produce a visual pattern. Sato knows this stone. He knows what the Warden's Wisdom is — not its specific content, but its general nature: protected knowledge about the living dragons held by the Order of the Sacred Grove for safekeeping.

Sato does not know who killed Solas, but he knows the category of entity capable of it. Solas was skilled, cautious, and not easily surprised. The killing required either significantly superior capability or intimate familiarity — someone Solas trusted and did not guard against. This points to either a very powerful practitioner or someone inside the Order of the Sacred Grove or the Ancient Guard itself.

Plot Threads

  • Relc's personal quest — the cipher poem's first stone is in Kōriwara's sacred grove
  • Solas's murder — knows the category of killer but not the identity
  • Order of the Ancient Guard knowledge — has not yet shared with Relc
  • Sacred grove disturbance — something has happened he cannot explain
  • Stranger asking about Relc — someone is tracking the party's druid
  • Yasutake Mai connection — can help establish her in the Sunsato/Kōriwara community

Public Role

Taisho (General) of Clan Kaminari and Commissioner of Special Operations. Commands from the Tensho no Mon (Military District) in Heian. Assigned the party their current mission to investigate the Gekkō Clan's silence. The party reports directly to him.

Exceptionally intelligent, strategic; values order and discipline; stern but fair; appreciates historical battles and traditional music.

Direct handler. Assigned the party their mission at the Tensho no Mon district in Heian. Sun Wukong's mandate from the Tranquil Lotus specifically names Hideo as the reporting authority. The party met him alongside Arinori Senzai during their mission briefing.

True Nature

Investigating a traitor within his own ranks. He has narrowed the leak to a small circle of senior staff. He may ask the party to carry out intelligence work he cannot assign to his own staff — the request would be framed neutrally but suggests he suspects someone close.

Connections

Commands the special operations apparatus of Clan Kaminari. His intelligence resources are significant but compromised by the presence of the traitor he is hunting.

The traitor Hideo is hunting is his own brother, Hiroshi Nakamura, the Shugo of Heian. Hideo does not yet know this. He will, in time, develop evidence pointing toward Hiroshi. The question is whether he reaches that conclusion before Hiroshi learns how close Hideo is and takes action.

Taisho — Shugo (Governor) of Heian

Appearance

Dark hair tied back; tanned; deep brown eyes; warm approachable expression.

Public Role

Taisho (General) of Clan Kaminari and Shugo (Governor) of Heian. As Shugo, he has near-total access to Clan Kaminari's intelligence and administrative operations. He is the civilian administrative authority over the imperial capital.

Personality

Calm, peace-loving, nature-appreciating, wise mediator. His warmth makes him trusted by nearly everyone — including his brother Hideo.

Relationship to Party

No direct contact established yet, but as Shugo of Heian he is a significant authority figure the party may interact with.

True Nature

His public persona — calm, peace-loving, wise — is a deliberate mask of exceptional consistency. His warmth is his most effective weapon.

Connections

Brother of Taisho Hideo Nakamura. Their sibling relationship gives him both access and cover.

Quest Seeds

QUEST SEED Hiroshi's true nature, once discovered, represents a massive intelligence find — the Shugo of the imperial capital is a traitor.

Campaign Secrets

Hiroshi Nakamura is an active traitor conspiring against Clan Kaminari. His primary driver is personal ambition — Nakamura family elevation. He is working with the Genso Alliance as his vehicle — Genso is the more overtly antagonist alliance in the broader story. His warmth and mediator persona is a deliberate mask over a calculated power play.

He is using his Shugo position to feed intelligence to enemies. He has been doing this for at least three years. He is aware that Hideo is investigating a traitor and is actively monitoring that investigation to stay ahead of it.

Who he is specifically working with within the Genso Alliance — his specific contact — is undeveloped and to be determined.

Plot Threads

  • Traitor within Kaminari — Hideo is hunting him without knowing it
  • Genso Alliance connection — his betrayal ties into the broader war
  • Nakamura family ambition — the driving motive
  • The eventual brother confrontation — devastating narrative moment
  • Succession crisis implications — the Shugo of the capital working against his own clan

Appearance

Unknown in current state. Formerly the Daimyo of Clan Gekkō, the third independent clan governing Kaze province from Hokori.

Public Role

Daimyo of Clan Gekkō. His disappearance and the silence of the entire Gekkō Clan is the central mystery driving the party's primary mission.

Personality

Unknown in current state.

Relationship to Party

No contact. The party has been assigned to investigate his disappearance and the silence of Clan Gekkō.

True Nature

Missing. The entire Gekkō Clan has gone silent. The party's primary mission is to investigate this disappearance.

Connections

Clan Gekkō had a long and close relationship with the Order of the Black Lily, who provided intelligence and covert capability in exchange for cover and protection. The clan's disappearance has severed the Order's primary institutional support structure.

Quest Seeds

QUEST SEED The full reveal of Masota's fate is intended to occur at the Monastery of the Black Lily in Akatsuki.

Campaign Secrets

Masota no Gekkō has been transformed into a Nagaji by a dark ritual gone wrong. He underwent the ritual in a final attempt to maintain leadership of his people after many clan members were transformed. His current state of mind is fragmented awareness — he retains a broken understanding of what happened and recognizes his mistake. Coherence degrades over time; the longer the party takes to reach him, the less of Masota is left to reach. This creates urgency without hard deadlines.

The Order of the Black Lily knows the full truth: what ritual was used, who performed it first, approximately how many Gekkō clan members were transformed, and that Masota himself underwent the ritual. They have been unable to locate him — the transformed Gekkō move in patterns that even their surveillance cannot consistently track.

A reversal exists — theoretical, not practical. It requires three elements: the original ritual documentation (which exists in Kinkōkyo, in the Golden Dragon Clan's records addressing Kokuryū's historical experimentation with transformation); a specific sei configuration present only during a particular celestial alignment (upcoming — within the next few sessions); and a practitioner capable of performing sei-based restoration at significant scale.

Plot Threads

  • Central mystery of the current campaign arc
  • Nagaji transformation — the party has killed multiple Nagaji without knowing they were transformed Gekkō clan members; moral weight of this revelation is pending
  • Temple of Kinryū may contain the reversal documentation
  • Order of the Black Lily at Akatsuki holds the full truth and will propose a partnership
  • Haruto Masashige's ancient Dragonborn purification/restoration rite is directly applicable to the Nagaji situation if someone connects the dots

Appearance

Public Role

Chief Inspector of the Imperial Police stationed in Ayame, the mountain waypoint town at the base of the Tenchūsan Ren pass. His authority and presence represent imperial law enforcement in this critical transit chokepoint.

Personality

Stern, meticulous, exudes authority.

Relationship to Party

Confirmed party ally. Returned the impounded wagon, horses, and treasures after assessing the situation. Provided a reward. Believed in the party's innocence or usefulness. His intelligence contacts are potentially useful going forward.

True Nature

His decision to assist the party was not simply a judgment about their innocence. He had received information from his intelligence network suggesting the party's mission was legitimate and the impoundment was creating an obstacle to something he wanted to see succeed. He knows more about the Gekkō situation than he has shared and has been watching for trustworthy parties to pass through.

Connections

Maintains an informant network in Ayame and the surrounding region. Has informants at both the waypoint inn (Kin no Chōchin Ryokan) and the outfitter district who log significant travelers and goods movements. This network detected the party's arrival and departure. It also detected other parties moving through the pass — including a group with no identifiable clan affiliation, moving fast and carrying unusual cargo, approximately three weeks before the party's transit.

Quest Seeds

QUEST SEED Oshiro sends a discrete message to the party: he has information relevant to their mission that he couldn't share safely in Ayame; he proposes a meeting at the next Michibata up the pass.

Campaign Secrets

Oshiro is a potential ongoing intelligence ally — someone who knows which questions to ask and where to find answers, even with the Teikoku Keisatsu operating at reduced capacity in the current political vacuum. His knowledge of the Gekkō situation extends beyond what he has shared.

The unidentified group that passed through the pass three weeks before the party — fast-moving, no clan affiliation, unusual cargo — is an unresolved intelligence thread.

Plot Threads

  • Intelligence ally for future information needs
  • Knowledge of the Gekkō situation he has not yet shared
  • Unidentified group in the pass — potential connection to Nagaji activity, Eikyū Yami, or other threats
  • Operating in a political vacuum — the Teikoku Keisatsu's reduced capacity affects what he can do officially

Shicho (Mayor) of Kikyo — Daimyo of Clan Minato

Appearance

Long black hair in topknot; fair skin; dark brown eyes; Clan Kaminari emblem tattoo on upper arm.

Public Role

Shicho (Mayor) of Kikyo and Daimyo of Clan Minato. Kikyo is a subject city of Clan Kaminari, but Ren Nakamura's dual role as both civic administrator and minor clan daimyo gives him unusual autonomy. He administers the Bronze Wood licensing system — every piece of Bronze Wood that leaves the Seidōrin Mori passes through a licensing transaction managed by his office.

Personality

Stern but fair; values loyalty; enjoys strategy (Go) and tea ceremonies; despises dishonesty — an irony, given his own secret alliances.

Relationship to Party

Issued the Summons and Conditional Pardon to Ko'jiri. Sent Ko'jiri as envoy to Heian. Ko'jiri's legal status depends on completing the mission assigned through Ren Nakamura's authority.

True Nature

Subtly working to elevate Clan Minato to equal standing with major clans. Has a secret alliance with a powerful merchant guild — exclusive Kikyo trading rights in exchange for financial and political support for Clan Minato's ambitions. Possesses ancient knowledge about Seidōrin Mori and Bronze Wood that he has not shared publicly.

Connections

The merchant guild he works with is not a Kikyo entity — it is based in Heian with operations across Hana and beyond. The alliance was struck in exchange for financial support for Clan Minato's elevation ambitions and exclusive export contracts.

Quest Seeds

QUEST SEED Ren Nakamura may contact Ko'jiri separately from the group with an additional, unwritten request — something the formal letter couldn't contain.

Campaign Secrets

Nakamura is not villainous by nature — he genuinely believes Clan Minato deserves greater standing — but he has made compromises that are beginning to require further compromises to sustain.

The Bronze Wood secret: the Seidōrin Mori grows over an underground branch of Kinkōkyo's ancient canal system. The metallic quality of the trees is caused by trace gold and copper content in the groundwater — water flowing through the buried city's infrastructure for thousands of years has mineralized the soil and is absorbed by the trees. Ren Nakamura has discovered this. The merchant guild he is allied with wants to locate and exploit the source directly, bypassing the tree-harvesting process entirely. This would require excavating the forest floor — destroying the grove to access what lies beneath.

Ko'jiri's forged letter ticking clock: Ko'jiri carries both a legitimate letter from Ren Nakamura and a forged version requesting additional materials. The real letter has already been sent to Heian through official channels — it will arrive before or very shortly after the party does. When the discrepancy is discovered, Ko'jiri's Conditional Pardon will be immediately at risk. Estimated timeline: 2-4 sessions from party arrival in Heian.

Plot Threads

  • Ko'jiri's legal jeopardy through the forged letter
  • Bronze Wood / Kinkōkyo underground connection
  • Clan Minato's elevation ambitions
  • Merchant guild exploitation of Seidōrin Mori
  • Connection to Haruto Masashige's licensing investigation

Guardian — Order of the Sacred Grove (Deceased)

Appearance

Long flowing silver hair; pale skin; emerald green eyes; intricate nature motif tattoos on arms.

Public Role

Former Guardian of the Order of the Sacred Grove. Dead under mysterious circumstances. Appears to Relc as a spirit — guiding visions that direct Relc's journey.

Personality

Unknown in life beyond what Relc and Sato Hideaki remember — a mentor, a protector, someone who prepared carefully for his own death.

Relationship to Party

Relc's mentor and predecessor as Guardian. Appointed Relc as next Guardian via a posthumous letter. Left a cipher poem pointing to hidden knowledge (Warden's Wisdom). His spirit appears to Relc at key moments — the next expected vision is at the gold doors or shortly after entering the Temple of Kinryū (Solas in the grove above Kōriwara, hand on a specific stone, dawn light from the east).

True Nature

His death was not natural or accidental. He was killed by someone with either significantly superior capability or intimate familiarity — someone he trusted and did not guard against. This points to either a very powerful practitioner or someone inside the Order of the Sacred Grove or the Ancient Guard itself.

Connections

Connected to Hideaki Sato (mid-rank Sacred Grove member) and Benkei (Ancient Guard). His death has compromised the Ancient Guard.

Quest Seeds

QUEST SEED The cipher poem (three stones, still water, rising sun, phoenix fern glade) leads to the Warden's Wisdom — protected knowledge about the living dragons. One of the three stones is in Kōriwara's sacred grove. [QUEST SEED] Investigating Solas's killer — the killer was motivated by hunting the locations of the Progenitors (the living founding dragons); they knew Solas was connected to protected knowledge about the dragons and targeted him for it.

Campaign Secrets

Member of the Order of the Ancient Guard. The Ancient Guard protects knowledge about the living dragons — the campaign's deepest secret.

Solas's killer was motivated by hunting the locations of the Progenitors (the living founding dragons). The killer knew Solas was connected to protected knowledge about the dragons and targeted him for it. Further identity and method TBD, but the motive is locked.

The Warden's Wisdom — the destination of the cipher poem — is protected knowledge about the living dragons held by the Order of the Sacred Grove for safekeeping. Its specific content and the destination location are yet to be determined but connect to the Ancient Guard or living dragons arc.

Sato Hideaki knows Solas was Ancient Guard (not just Sacred Grove). He knows the category of entity capable of killing Solas but not the specific identity.

Plot Threads

  • Relc's personal quest — the cipher poem and Warden's Wisdom
  • Solas's murder investigation — connected to the living dragons secret
  • Order of the Ancient Guard — his death has compromised the order
  • Spirit visions — ongoing guidance for Relc
  • The Progenitor hunt — whoever killed Solas is still looking for dragon locations

A young mother fleeing with her infant child. Encountered on the Emperor's Highway on the first day of travel north from Heian toward Ayame. She was out of breath, visibly distressed, claimed to be carrying a precious package, and asked the party to hold it — the package was her infant child. She spotted figures running toward her, tossed the child to the party, and bolted. The figures turned out to be boys out for a run, not a threat. Relc caught and returned her.

Personality

Capable of managing independently under normal conditions but was operating in a state of fear-driven poor decision making when the party found her. Behavior under stress and useful skills are undeveloped — flagged for development in the DM Notebook.

Relationship to Party

Traveling with the party. The party offered to take her north through the Tenchūsan Ren to Sunsato on the far side, where she might find safety and a new beginning near Relc's home region. She is currently inside the Temple of Kinryū with the party — a civilian in a dungeon. She cannot fight. She needs protection or a defensible position during encounters. Her presence affects the party's tactical decisions and roleplay.

True Nature

She has not fully explained her circumstances or what she was fleeing. Her fear on the highway was genuine — she is running from something real, even though the specific group she feared at that moment turned out to be harmless.

Connections

The people she is actually afraid of are real and have noticed she is gone. They are not currently actively searching — they are waiting to see if she surfaces somewhere that matters to their operations.

Quest Seeds

QUEST SEED Safely transport Yasutake Mai and her infant to Sunsato — quest objective active. [QUEST SEED] Optional extension: introduce Mai to Elder Sato's community network at Kōriwara, earning a favor with Sato and planting a contact in the north Mizu foothills.

Campaign Secrets

The merchant family she left was involved in Bronze Wood sourcing. She lived in that household for three years and heard conversations she didn't fully understand at the time. If the underground canal source beneath Seidōrin Mori ever becomes a significant plot point, Mai knows things she doesn't know she knows — a long-term seed, not immediately relevant.

The infant is a healthy baby boy with no apparent significance beyond being a mother's reason to flee.

Sunsato exists near Relc's home region and is a viable destination. The community near Kōriwara is historically accepting of people who arrive asking for honest work and quiet lives. Elder Sato Hideaki at Kōriwara knows the community network and could help establish her there.

If the quest is abandoned, Mai will eventually find her way to safety through other means — she is more capable than she appeared in crisis. She will survive. But she will remember whether the party kept their word.

Plot Threads

  • A Mother's Redemption quest — active; transport to Sunsato
  • Bronze Wood connection — she unknowingly carries information relevant to the Seidōrin Mori underground source
  • Civilian in a dungeon — her presence in the Temple of Kinryū creates tactical and roleplay considerations
  • Connection to Kōriwara/Sato community network
  • The people she fled — merchant family connected to Bronze Wood sourcing; watching for her to surface

"An independent clan does not simply go silent. Something happened. Finding out what may change everything."

Background

Clan Gekko — one of Hokori's three politically independent clans and historically a stabilizing force in Kagekuni's balance of power — has gone silent. No communication. No trade. No diplomatic contact. Provincial administration in Kaze has stopped responding. The clan's last confirmed external communication was several months ago and contained nothing unusual.

In the current political environment — no emperor, no shogun, two major alliances in open conflict — an independent clan going silent is not merely a diplomatic problem. It is a potential flashpoint. If Clan Gekko has been eliminated or absorbed, the balance of power shifts. If they are in crisis, the crisis could spill outward. If they are being suppressed by an outside force, that force has made a significant move that demands response.

Taisho Hideo Nakamura of Clan Kaminari's Special Operations division assigned the party to investigate — using Ko'jiri's conditional pardon as the formal mechanism, with the party as the operational unit. The Imperial Seal issued by Daimyo Akihiko Kurohana provides diplomatic weight: it calls on all factions to cooperate with the investigation as a matter of archipelago-wide concern.

Objectives

  • Determine what has happened to Daimyo Masota no Gekko and Clan Gekko
    • Travel to Kaze Province and Akatsuki
    • Investigate the Monastery of the Black Lily and the Order of the Black Lily
    • Locate and assess Clan Gekko's current status
    • Report findings to Taisho Hideo Nakamura

Known Information

The Nagaji Connection — The party has encountered Nagaji (serpentine humanoid creatures) multiple times in the Tenchusan Ren mountains. These creatures have been responsible for triggering the avalanche that endangered the party, operating what appeared to be an outpost in the mountain ruins, and guarding the approach to the gold doors. Their presence in the mountain pass between Hana and Kaze province is not coincidental. Their connection to the Clan Gekko investigation is not yet known to the party.

The Gold Doors — The party stands at the entrance to what appears to be the Lost Temple of Kinryu. This location is within the Tenchusan Ren, at the boundary of Hana and Kaze provinces. Whatever lies inside is connected to both the Golden Dragon Clan's history and — more immediately — to the Nagaji activity that has defined the party's mountain passage.

Imperial Seal of Clan Kurohana — Issued by Daimyo Akihiko Kurohana; carried by the party. A diplomatic instrument calling on the independent Kaminari Clan and all factions to cooperate with investigating Clan Gekko's unexplained silence. Its tone is carefully measured — no blame assigned, unity emphasized. Its weight is significant.

Known Parties with Interest:

Party Interest Stance
Taisho Hideo Nakamura (Clan Kaminari) Official mission authority Supportive; needs deniability
Daimyo Kazuhiko (Clan Kaminari) Political stability; alliance balance Invested; watching
Daimyo Akihiko Kurohana Balance of power; emperor assassination investigation Allied; issued the seal
Order of the Black Lily Know the truth; managing information Cautious; will engage right parties
Clan Gekko survivors Exist; transformed; situation desperate Location unknown

Hidden Truth

Clan Gekko's senior seimasters discovered fragmentary texts describing a transformation ritual tied to the Onyx Dragon Clan (Kokuryu). The ritual was meant to grant shadow-shifting capability. It transformed those who underwent it into Nagaji — serpentine humanoids — irreversibly and catastrophically. The transformation spread. Masota no Gekko himself performed the ritual last, in a final attempt to lead and protect his people in their transformed state. He is now Nagaji as well. The Nagaji the party has been fighting in the mountains are former Clan Gekko members.

NPC Knowledge

  • Order of the Black Lily — Knows the full truth about Gekko. Their stance when the party arrives at Akatsuki depends on how long they have known, whether they tried to stop it, and whether they are protecting, containing, or observing the transformed members.
  • Masota no Gekko — Alive, transformed, retains fragmented awareness. He recognizes his mistake. Coherence degrades over time — the longer the party takes to reach him, the less of Masota is left to reach.
  • The Nagaji Zasu in Tenkuji Temple — The chief seimaster of Clan Gekko, architect of the failed ritual. Fragments of the original person remain. Can potentially communicate if the party uses magic or patience.

Discovery Paths

  • A transformed Gekko member (Nagaji) who retains more of their original personality approaches the party non-aggressively — the first indication that these are people, not simply monsters
  • Inside the temple, Golden Dragon Clan records explicitly reference a "serpent corruption" and a "restoration of form" — the connection between the temple and their mission becomes undeniable
  • The Order of the Black Lily makes contact through Akatsuki and proposes a partnership contingent on the party having retrieved something from the Temple of Kinryu first

Full Truth

The party has already killed people. The Nagaji slain in the mountain pass were transformed Gekko clan members — people, not monsters. They did not know this. The moral weight of this revelation is pending and should land with appropriate gravity when the truth is revealed. Some of those killed may have been mid-ranking clan members with families. The party did not do anything wrong given what they knew; they had no way to know. But they will have to reckon with it.

A reversal for the transformation exists in documented form inside the Temple of Kinryu — specifically in the Golden Dragon Clan's historical records addressing Kokuryu's experimentation with transformation rituals centuries ago. The Golden Clan developed a countermeasure. That documentation is somewhere in the temple complex the party is about to enter.

Resolution Options

  1. Report the truth to Hideo and let the political process handle it — easiest; least satisfying. The party washes its hands.
  2. Pursue the reversal before reporting, changing the terms of the revelation entirely — hardest; most impactful. Requires finding and acting on the reversal documentation before anyone else learns the truth.
  3. Work with the Order of the Black Lily to manage the timeline and pursue the reversal collaboratively — middle path; most story-rich. Requires trust between the party and the Order.

The quest formally closes when a report reaches Hideo Nakamura. What happens after depends on what that report says.

Timing

  • Masota no Gekko's coherence degrades over time — creates urgency without hard deadlines
  • A celestial alignment approaching is required for the reversal to work on Masota specifically
  • The political explosion when the truth becomes public will reshape the alliance balance — every faction will have a position on what happens to the Nagaji

Connections

  • personal-kojiri-misunderstood — Ko'jiri's assignment IS this investigation; his pardon depends on reporting back
  • Temple of Kinryu — contains the reversal documentation; the temple is not just Ko'jiri's personal treasure hunt — it is the key to undoing the Gekko disaster
  • The Nagaji transformation ritual — connected to the same Kokuryu source material as the necromantic cache buried by the Eikyu Yami Clan (see side-nightfall-ambush)
  • The political calculation — when the truth becomes public, Clan Gekko is functionally destroyed; the alliance balance shifts; every faction responds differently
