"The machine does not care who repairs it. It only cares that someone does."

Background

Deep within the Temple of Kinryū, on the second floor, the Golden Dragon Clan built the Hoshikagami no Ma — the Chamber of the Star Mirror. At its center stands a mechanical-arcane orrery: a system of bronze armatures, gear tracks, and arcane projection lenses that together model the full Miyosai celestial system. Stars, moons, and planets tracked across millennia by a device of extraordinary precision.

The orrery has not been operational since the temple fell in 13088. Its components are scattered — some still in the observatory, seized or cracked; others removed for safekeeping and left in rooms throughout the temple by priests who never returned for them. Nine components are required for full restoration: five found on the first floor, four on the second.

The observatory is integrated with the temple's foundational magic. When fully restored, its sei resonance propagates through the construction-level enchantment that permeates the entire structure — awakening the ori-kioku tapestries in the South Entrance below. Four tapestries survive. They hold records the Golden Dragon order considered important enough to weave into fabric that would outlast stone.

Objectives

  • Assess the observatory and identify what repairs are needed
  • Locate the 5 first-floor components
    • Susanoo projection lens (Grand Hall)
    • Planetary gear assembly (Dormitories)
    • Calibration disc (Dormitories — sealed room)
    • Tsukuyomi projection lens (Mess Hall)
    • Sei conduit filament (Inner Sanctum)
  • Locate the 4 second-floor components
    • Repair the cracked Amaterasu projection lens (Observatory)
    • Free the seized stellar drive mechanism (Observatory)
    • Find the lunar armature set (Scriptorium)
    • Find the operator's manual (Scriptorium)
  • Restore the orrery through 5 repair stages
  • Descend to the South Entrance and witness the activated tapestries
  • Study the four surviving tapestries for information

Known Information

Populated as the party discovers components and makes checks. Initially empty — the quest begins with assessment.

Hidden Truth

The orrery is not merely an astronomical curiosity. It is the operational heart of a network that connects this temple to at least three other sanctuary sites across Hokori. Restoring it does not just activate the tapestries — it brings the hub node of a millennia-old communication system back online.

Tapestry III is not a historical record like the other three. It is a monitoring surface — a live feed of the sanctuary network's current state. When activated, it shows:

  • This temple: operational (steady gold pulse)
  • Sora province site: acknowledged — a distress signal was received and answered, but help never came (slow double-beat)
  • Kaze province site: distress, unacknowledged — the signal has been running into silence since the fall of 13088 (rapid pulse)
  • Hi/Tsuchi border site: offline — severed, not dormant (cold fabric, no signal)

These signals were set by practitioners during the fall. They have been running for over three thousand years. The party is the first entity capable of receiving them.

The other three tapestries hold equally significant information:

  • Tapestry I: Records Kinryū's voluntary binding to this mountain — the founding moment of the temple, cosmologically timed
  • Tapestry II: Preserves the consecration ceremony that laid the temple's foundational enchantments — and evidence of infiltration within the order itself (a Kokuryu-aspected sei signature hidden within the golden working)
  • Tapestry IV: Depicts the first head priest receiving a direct commission from Kinryū, with a theological border encoding the order's founding obligations: creation, covenant, stewardship, silence

NPC Knowledge

  • Head Priest Kinjiro's spirit (priest's chamber): Knows the full history of the orrery, the sanctuary network, and the tapestries' contents. Can explain the network protocol if the party engages peacefully. His operational ledger in the bronze box contains records of significant network events.
  • Ko'jiri: His Golden Dragon Clan research gives him advantage throughout — the orrery validates everything he has studied. The operator's manual is readable at reduced DC for him.
  • Benkei (traveling, not present): Would recognize the sanctuary network as connected to the Ancient Guard's mission. The sites marked on Tapestry III overlap with the locations the Warden's Wisdom points toward.

Discovery Paths

  • Assessment in the observatory: DC 14 History (DC 11 Ko'jiri) connects the device to Golden Dragon records. DC 14 Tinker's Tools identifies what specific repairs are needed.
  • Component discovery: Each component found on the first floor gains context when the party reaches the observatory — the "aha" moment when mysterious crystals and bronze rings suddenly have purpose.
  • Tapestry examination (static): Available before orrery restoration. Two skill tracks per tapestry yield different information layers. Tapestry III's Track One Critical Success identifies the three sanctuary markers and their approximate geographic locations.
  • Tapestry activation (orrery restored): The living tapestries reveal information invisible in the static state — Tapestry I tracks Ko'jiri's presence, Tapestry III shows the live network, Tapestry IV's activation cycle includes the head priest glancing toward Tapestry III mid-ceremony.
  • Relc's presence during Tapestry III activation: He feels Solas's presence — not here, but at one of the other sanctuary sites shown on the map. This connects his personal quest directly to the sanctuary network.

Full Truth

The sanctuary network is an Ancient Guard infrastructure. The four sites on Tapestry III are not random temples — they are guardianship sites positioned near Progenitor resting locations. This temple is the hub. The orrery is not just an astronomical tool; its sei resonance is what keeps the network alive.

The party, by restoring the orrery, has done something with consequences beyond this temple:

  • The hub is online for the first time in three millennia
  • Any entity sensitive to the network (including the awakened Murasakiryū) may notice the signal change
  • The Kaze site's distress signal has been broadcasting into silence — restoring the hub makes the signal receivable, and the party can acknowledge it
  • The Hi/Tsuchi site's offline/severed state suggests something happened there recently (the fabric retains residual warmth — days or weeks, not centuries)

The orrery's visualization of the Great Aphelion — watching two stars go dark while the mechanism keeps running — is the sei drought made visible. A party that understands what they are seeing has the first concrete evidence that the return of magic was not a natural restoration but the waking of a single source.

Resolution Options

  1. Full restoration + tapestry study: The party takes time to repair the orrery completely, studies all four tapestries, and leaves the temple with geographic leads on three sanctuary sites, knowledge of the network protocol, and the understanding that this temple is a functioning hub. This is the richest outcome and feeds directly into future quests at each sanctuary site.

  2. Partial restoration: The party repairs the orrery enough for partial projection (impressive but no tapestry activation) and moves on. They miss the sanctuary network revelation but may return later. The components they found but couldn't use remain available.

  3. Full restoration, limited study: The party activates the tapestries but doesn't invest time in deep examination. They get the dramatic moment but miss discoverable content. Available on return visits.

Timing

  • No hard deadline. The orrery repair is designed to span the second-floor exploration, interleaved with other activities.
  • Each repair stage: 15-30 minutes of table time
  • Tapestry activation scene: budget 45-60 minutes for the full experience
  • The tapestries remain active as long as the orrery runs — the party can return

Connections

  • main-gekko-investigation: The temple contains reversal documentation for the Nagaji transformation. The orrery quest and the Gekkō quest share a location but have separate payoffs — one reveals the sanctuary network and the world's deeper history; the other provides the means to undo the Gekkō disaster.
  • personal-relc-sacred-grove: Tapestry III's sanctuary sites overlap with the Warden's Wisdom locations. Solas's presence at one of those sites gives Relc a personal, urgent reason to pursue them. The orrery restoration is the mechanism that surfaces this connection.
  • Future quest — Kaze sanctuary: The distress signal. The site in the Kaze highlands the party is already traveling toward for the Gekkō investigation. Two quests converge on one location.
  • Future quest — Sora sanctuary: The acknowledged signal. A promise made and not kept. Stone 3 of Relc's cipher is on the Hoshimori Plateau in Sora.
  • Future quest — Hi/Tsuchi site: The severed node. Recent activity. The Akaho Sanmyaku eruption is ongoing in Hi province. Something happened at this site recently.
  • Murasakiryū thread: The orrery's Great Aphelion visualization is the first evidence the party can encounter that magic's return was not natural. The Kokuryu-aspected sei signature in Tapestry II's fabric (and on the Inner Sanctum ward anchors) is the same fingerprint — a trail that eventually leads to the masquerade.
  • Ko'jiri's arc: The orrery is the first time Ko'jiri's performed scholarship proves to be genuine expertise. The observatory does not judge him. It just needs someone who knows what it is.

"In the world of commerce and counsel, every venture has its share of challenges."

Background

Ko'jiri's entrepreneurial approach to the provision of wisdom and guidance in the city of Kikyo attracted the attention of local authorities in a manner inconsistent with continued free operation. Specifically: a formal writ was served outlining offenses committed within Kikyo — fraud, unlawful coin gathering, false prophecies, and exploitation.

Rather than simple prosecution, Shicho Ren Nakamura identified an opportunity. Ko'jiri's particular skillset — persuasion, information gathering, and the ability to move through situations without attracting official attention — was potentially useful for an assignment that required someone deniable. A conditional pardon was offered: complete the tasks assigned by Taisho Hideo Nakamura, and all charges are set aside.

Ko'jiri reported to Taisho Nakamura. The assignment: travel to the Kaze region and determine what has happened to Daimyo Masota no Gekko of Clan Gekko. An independent clan's leadership has gone silent. The political implications of that silence are significant. The party is the official — if unofficial — investigative body.

Objectives

  • Ko'jiri has been served with a writ outlining offenses committed within Kikyo. Shicho Nakamura Ren offers a pardon upon completion of tasks for Taisho Hideo Nakamura.
    • Report to Taisho Hideo Nakamura for assignment
    • Taisho Nakamura has assigned Ko'jiri to venture to Akatsuki and the Kaze region to determine what has happened to the Daimyo of Clan Gekko

Known Information

Official Objective: Determine the fate of Daimyo Masota no Gekko of Clan Gekko.

Context provided by Taisho Nakamura:

  • Clan Gekko, one of Hokori's three independent clans, has ceased communication with external parties
  • Provincial administration in Kaze has stopped responding to Heian correspondence
  • The clan's last confirmed communication was several months ago — a routine dispatch that mentioned nothing unusual
  • Clan Kurohana's Imperial Seal (held by the party) calls on independent Kaminari support to investigate this silence
  • The target location is Akatsuki in Kaze province, and the broader Kaze region

The Party's Current Position — The party is at the gold doors in Tenchusan Ren. The mountains form the boundary between Hana and Kaze province. Completing the temple may bring them out on the Kaze side — or provide information that directly advances this quest.

Known Complications:

  • Ko'jiri's Forged Letter — Ko'jiri carries two versions of correspondence from Ren Nakamura: the legitimate envoy letter and a forged version requesting additional materials. The real letter was sent to Heian through official channels simultaneously. The window during which the discrepancy remains undiscovered is closing.
  • The Conditional Pardon's Terms — Failure to complete the assignment reactivates all original charges immediately. The pardon has no partial credit — completion is required.

Hidden Truth

The Nagaji — the transformed Clan Gekko members the party has been fighting — are the answer to the assignment. Masota no Gekko is alive, transformed, somewhere in the Kaze highlands. The full truth is available at the Monastery of the Black Lily above Akatsuki. The quest's nominal completion (report back what happened to the daimyo) is achievable. The deeper question — what do they do about it — is where the quest becomes something larger.

NPC Knowledge

  • Hideo Nakamura — Assigned this mission not only because the Gekko investigation is strategically important but because he wanted a deniable party with no official Clan Kaminari affiliation. If things go wrong in Kaze, Clan Kaminari needs to not be officially responsible. Ko'jiri (and by extension the party) is that deniability. Hideo is pragmatic about this. He will support the party within limits, but those limits are defined by what he can defend politically.
  • Ren Nakamura — Sent the legitimate letter to Heian through official channels; the administrative queue will eventually cross-reference it against Ko'jiri's presented version.

Discovery Paths

  • Inside the temple, Ko'jiri's research notes become directly useful — his documented knowledge of Kinkokyou's layout gives the party an edge navigating the buried sections; his advantage on History checks (Golden Dragon Clan) is active throughout
  • A message from Heian reaches the party through Oshiro Masahiro in Ayame (routed through the Inspector's network): there is an administrative query about Ko'jiri's letters; the clock has started
  • Hideo Nakamura sends a discreet secondary message: regardless of what the party finds, he needs a report before it goes anywhere else; he implies that certain information in the wrong hands at the wrong moment would be catastrophic

Full Truth

Ko'jiri is about to walk into the temple that is the subject of years of his own research. The narrative irony is complete: the con artist who built a career on faking Golden Dragon authority is standing at the actual door of the Golden Dragon Clan's lost sanctuary. Whatever happens inside will be real in ways his performances never were.

The forged letter timeline: Ren Nakamura's legitimate letter arrived in Heian's administrative processing queue approximately when the party did, or shortly after. Heian's administrative function is slowed by the political vacuum — the legitimate letter has been logged but not yet actively cross-referenced against Ko'jiri's presence in Heian. Estimate: 2-4 sessions before someone notices the discrepancy. Hideo Nakamura's office would be the first to catch it — creating a direct conflict between Ko'jiri's handler and Ko'jiri's legal situation.

Resolution Options

  • Delivering a clear account of the Gekko situation to Hideo Nakamura closes the formal assignment — but "a clear account" requires revealing the Nagaji situation, which has political consequences Hideo was trying to avoid by using deniable agents
  • Hideo will honor the pardon but may need a serious conversation about what the party tells, who they tell, and when
  • The deeper question — can the Gekko transformation be reversed, and will Ko'jiri be part of making that happen — extends well beyond the assignment's formal completion
  • The temple contains the reversal documentation; Ko'jiri's research is directly relevant to finding it; he may be the most prepared person in the party for what lies inside

Timing

  • Forged letter clock: ~2-4 sessions from Heian arrival before the discrepancy is discovered
  • The temple visit is happening now — Ko'jiri's research advantage is active throughout
  • Report to Hideo needed before the political situation escalates

Connections

  • main-gekko-investigation — Ko'jiri's personal quest IS the main investigation; his pardon depends on completing it
  • Temple of Kinryu — contains information directly relevant to Ko'jiri's research; the temple will test whether there is anything genuine beneath the performance
  • The forged letter — a ticking clock that will create a confrontation scene when the discrepancy surfaces

Quest Giver

"He knew what was coming. He chose to face it anyway. Now he is asking you to face it for him."

Background

Solas Evergreen, Guardian of the Order of the Sacred Grove, was found dead among the ancient trees he had sworn to protect. The death showed signs of a struggle against something powerful and unknown. To most, it was a tragedy. To Relc — his devoted apprentice — it was the beginning of an unwanted and necessary journey.

Solas appeared to Relc in fragmented visions following his death, guiding him toward Heian. The posthumous letter Solas had prepared before his death, held by Benkei of the Order of the Tranquil Lotus, named Relc as the next Guardian of the Sacred Grove — a role Solas had prepared him for, even if Relc did not know it. The letter contained not just the appointment but a cipher poem pointing toward something Solas called the Warden's Wisdom.

Solas knew danger was coming. He prepared for his death before it arrived. He did not tell Relc directly. He is still communicating — in the only way he can now.

Objectives

  • Investigate the death of Solas Evergreen
    • Follow the visions of Solas to Heian
    • Meet with Benkei and receive the letter
    • Await the next vision to appear

Known Information

The Letter from Solas Evergreen — Formally appoints Relc as Guardian of the Sacred Grove. Written in advance of death — Solas knew danger was coming. Instructs Relc to seek friends, forge alliances, and find answers through the journey rather than by staying still. The letter's reverse side contains a cipher poem.

The Cipher Poem (reverse side of the letter): Ancient sighing trees → still mirror of water → three stones (past / present / future) → align with rising sun → glade with phoenix fern → unlocks Warden's Wisdom

The Three Stones — Three specific stones that must be located and oriented toward the rising sun. Their locations are not specified in the poem; finding them is part of the quest. One is believed to be near Koriwara (Relc's home village). The others are unknown.

Phoenix Fern Glade — A specific location identifiable by the presence of phoenix fern — a rare plant associated with renewal and sacred grove sites. The final destination once the stones are oriented.

The Warden's Wisdom — What the cipher poem ultimately unlocks. Its nature is not yet known to Relc.

Benkei's Role — The Elder of the Order of the Tranquil Lotus held Solas's letter for Relc. His own membership in the Order of the Ancient Guard suggests a connection between Solas's death and threats to something much larger than a single grove guardian.

Solas's Spirit — Has appeared to Relc in visions at least twice. The visions have been directional rather than explanatory — pointing toward Heian, toward Benkei. The next vision is expected when Relc reaches a point where direction is needed again.

Hidden Truth

The Warden's Wisdom is protected knowledge held by the Order of the Sacred Grove on behalf of the Order of the Ancient Guard. Specifically: it is a set of location coordinates — described in symbolic rather than literal geographic terms — pointing toward the hidden sanctuaries of three of the seven founding dragons. The Sacred Grove Order was entrusted with this knowledge as a failsafe: if the Ancient Guard was ever compromised, someone outside the order would know where to find the dragons without depending on Ancient Guard infrastructure. Solas was the primary keeper of this information. Relc is now.

NPC Knowledge

  • Benkei — Knows more than he has shared with Relc. He is aware of the Warden's Wisdom's existence and importance, though he does not know its specific content. He is watching Relc's development carefully. If Relc demonstrates readiness (accepting the weight of the Guardian role rather than simply carrying the title), Benkei will share more.
  • Elder Sato Hideaki — Knows the location of the first stone in the sacred grove above Koriwara.
  • Forest of Spirits faction (Kusa province) — Know what Stone 2 is, and accessing it will require a relationship with the faction.

Discovery Paths

  • The next vision arrives at the gold doors or shortly after entering the temple: Solas in the grove above Koriwara, hand resting on a specific stone, dawn light hitting it from the east — points Relc toward going home after the temple
  • Benkei sends a message to Relc: he needs to speak before they lose contact; he has something to say that couldn't be said in Heian with other ears present
  • At the Temple of Kinryu, something inside recognizes Relc's role as Guardian — the Sacred Grove and the Golden Dragon Clan had a historical relationship that will be relevant within the temple

Full Truth

Solas was killed because someone was hunting the Warden's Wisdom — the locations of the Progenitors. They did not get it. Solas had distributed the cipher poem as a secondary protection; the actual Warden's Wisdom cannot be accessed without completing the three-stone sequence, and completing that sequence requires presence at specific locations that the killer did not know. The killer knew Solas had the information but did not know how it was protected. They killed him hoping to find documentation that did not exist in accessible form.

The killer was someone within the overlap between the Order of the Sacred Grove and the Order of the Ancient Guard — someone who knew Solas was on a specific mission to wake Kinryu (the Golden Progenitor) and could get close enough to catch him. The motive: preventing Kinryu's awakening, which serves the interests of the awakened dark Progenitor (Murasakiryu, masquerading as Kokuryu).

The killer believed the mission died with Solas. Relc has an unknown head start.

Resolution Options

  • Complete the three-stone sequence: Stone 1 (Koriwara, Elder Sato), Stone 2 (Yousei Mori, Forest of Spirits, Kusa province), Stone 3 (Hoshimori Plateau, Sora province — near abandoned Golden Age observatories, watched by something)
  • Access the Warden's Wisdom — the dragon sanctuary locations
  • Pursue Solas's original mission: wake Kinryu to restore balance against the awakened Murasakiryu

Timing

  • The next vision triggers at the gold doors or inside the temple — pointing Relc home to Koriwara and Stone 1
  • Benkei is traveling toward Heian; the window to communicate with him is closing
  • If the killer learns Solas had a designated successor, Relc inherits a target on his back

Connections

  • The Order of the Ancient Guard — compromised; Solas's location was known to someone; the organization may be down to a handful of members
  • The Progenitor arc — the campaign's deepest thread; Relc's quest connects directly to the endgame
  • main-gekko-investigation — the temple the party is entering contains information relevant to both quests; the Sacred Grove and Golden Dragon Clan had a historical relationship
  • Murasakiryu — the awakened Amethyst Progenitor masquerading as Kokuryu; every sei use passes through its awareness; Solas was killed to prevent Kinryu from being woken as a counterbalance

quests.name: A Mother's Redemption: Journey to New Beginnings

text.content:
Type
quest
Status
active
Location
sunsato
Quest Type
side
Quest Giver
yasutake-mai

"The road north is long, but some burdens are worth carrying."

Background

On the first day of travel north from Heian toward Ayame, the party encountered a woman on the highway — Yasutake Mai — out of breath and visibly distressed. The conversation that followed was brief and somewhat chaotic. She claimed to be carrying a precious package and asked the party to hold it for her.

Within moments she spotted a group of figures running down the road toward her, tossed the package to the party, and bolted. The package was her infant child. The running figures turned out to be boys simply out for a run — not the threat she apparently believed them to be. Relc, in a moment of remarkable speed and determination (and equally remarkable dice luck), managed to catch and return the fleeing mother to the situation.

With child and mother reunited, the party learned enough of her circumstances to understand she was fleeing something — or someone — and had nowhere safe to go. The offer was made: the party would take her north through the Tenchusan Ren, to Sunsato on the far side, where she might find safety and a new beginning in the region where Relc's roots lie.

Objectives

  • Reunite mother and child
  • Safely transport Yasutake Mai and her infant to Sunsato

Known Information

Yasutake Mai — A young woman, clearly under significant stress at the time of the encounter. She has not fully explained her circumstances or what she was fleeing. The infant appears healthy. Mai is capable of managing independently under normal conditions but was operating in a state of fear-driven poor decision making when the party found her.

Sunsato — A settlement on the north side of the Tenchusan Ren, described as being near Relc's home region of Mizu province. The party offered this as a destination and it was accepted.

Current Status — The party entered the Tenchusan Ren mountain pass. Mai is currently traveling with the party inside the temple — she is a civilian in a dungeon and cannot fight.

Hidden Truth

Mai is not simply a woman in difficult circumstances. She is the estranged daughter-in-law of a minor merchant family in the Hana region — estranged because she took the infant and left after becoming aware that her husband's family was involved in illegal activity (specifically: participation in unlicensed Bronze Wood poaching, connected tangentially to the merchant guild operating out of Kikyo). She did not report this and has no intention of reporting it; she simply wants to disappear with her child.

The "group of men" she feared on the highway were not those people. They were coincidental. But the people she is actually afraid of are real and have noticed she is gone. They are not currently actively searching — they are waiting to see if she surfaces somewhere that matters to their operations.

NPC Knowledge

  • Yasutake Mai — Knows her husband's family was involved in unlicensed Bronze Wood poaching. Does not realize she knows things she doesn't know she knows — she lived in that household for three years and heard conversations she didn't fully understand about the underground Bronze Wood sourcing beneath Seidorin Mori.
  • Elder Sato Hideaki (Koriwara) — Knows the community network near Sunsato and could help establish Mai there, if the party makes that connection.

Discovery Paths

  • A merchant courier passing through Ayame or Sunsato is asking discreet questions about a young woman with an infant who has gone missing from a family in southern Hana — not aggressive, not official, just persistent
  • Mai, once settled, sends a message to the party: she has remembered something from her former household that she thinks might matter to them

Full Truth

The infant is a healthy baby boy with no apparent significance beyond being a mother's reason to flee. However, as a long-term seed: the merchant family she left was involved in Bronze Wood sourcing. If the underground canal source beneath Seidorin Mori ever becomes a significant plot point, Mai knows things she doesn't know she knows.

Sunsato exists near Relc's home region and is a viable destination. It is small enough that a newcomer will be noticed, but the community near Koriwara is historically accepting of people who arrive asking for honest work and quiet lives.

Resolution Options

  • Safe delivery to Sunsato closes this quest. Optional extension: the party introduces Mai to Elder Sato's community network, which earns them a favor with Sato and plants a contact in the north Mizu foothills region.
  • If the quest is abandoned — Mai will eventually find her way there through other means. She is more capable than she appeared in crisis. She will survive. But she will remember whether the party kept their word.

Timing

  • Mai is currently with the party inside the temple — a civilian in a dungeon; she needs protection or a defensible position during encounters
  • No hard deadline; the merchant family is not actively searching yet

Connections

  • Elder Sato Hideaki — introducing Mai to his network earns a favor and plants a useful northern contact
  • Bronze Wood poaching thread — long-term seed connecting to Seidorin Mori and the Kikyo merchant guild
  • Relc's home region — delivering Mai to Sunsato takes the party near Koriwara, where Relc's personal quest (first stone) also points

Type
quest
Status
active
Location
tenchusan-ren
Quest Type
side
Quest Giver
discovered

"Someone sent those bandits with instructions. Someone is expecting a delivery that will never arrive."

Background

The party was ambushed overnight by bandits on the Emperor's Highway north of Heian. The attack was repelled. During the aftermath, a letter was found concealed on the body of the bandit leader — written in an unfamiliar language and clearly of some significance, given the care taken to hide it.

The letter was subsequently translated. Its contents are a set of directional instructions — a treasure location cipher, written in obscure but decipherable terms — pointing toward a hidden cache or discovery of notable value.

The ambush itself raises questions beyond the letter: were the bandits operating independently and the letter is their own, or were they hired? If hired, by whom and for what purpose? The letter may be a lead the bandits were following, or a map they were transporting for someone else.

Objectives

  • Survive the ambush
  • Discover the letter on the bandit leader
  • Translate the letter
  • Find where "the earth feels soft"

Known Information

The Translated Letter:

"In the shadow of the great cedar, where the sun's light barely touches, lies the path to fortune."

"Seek the stone that stands alone, marked with the kanji of the moon; beneath it, the first secret is revealed."

"Follow the stream that sings through the night, its waters whispering tales of hidden gold."

"At the fork where the wildflowers bloom, choose the path guarded by the fox's den."

"When you hear the owl's call, count seven paces from the ancient oak and dig where the earth feels soft."

Analysis of the Letter: The instructions are sequential — each line depends on the previous. The final destination is reached by following a specific route through landmarks described in order. Key identifiers:

  • A great cedar in shadow — large, old cedar tree in a location where direct sunlight doesn't reach; likely north-facing slope or deep forest interior
  • A lone standing stone marked with the moon kanji — a deliberate marker; someone placed or marked this stone intentionally
  • A stream audible at night — moving water with enough volume to be heard in quiet conditions
  • A wildflower fork with a fox's den — a trail junction near a known fox habitat
  • An ancient oak, seven paces, soft earth — the final cache location

Geographic candidates: The letter's language and style suggest origin in the central or northern Hokori region. The Tenchusan Ren and surrounding foothills contain all the described terrain types, but so does the Kaze province interior and the Kusa lowland forests.

The unknown language: What language was the letter written in? Identifying the script would narrow down who wrote it and potentially where the described location lies.

Hidden Truth

The bandits were not independent treasure hunters. They were hired. The employer is a mid-level operative working for a splinter cell of the Eikyu Yami Clan — Kuroyami no Akuma's organization, which persists in fragmentary form following the Plague Campaign. The cache is not gold. It is magical in nature.

The letter was written in an old variant of the Eikyu Yami Clan's internal cipher language — a constructed language used for operational communication. A scholar of ancient languages or a practitioner familiar with Dark Ages-era arcane traditions would recognize it as related to certain pre-Reformation shadow magic writings.

NPC Knowledge

  • The Kitsune at the fox's den — An actual fox spirit who has occupied a particular burrow system at a trail junction in the Tenchusan Ren foothills for approximately two hundred years. She knows the junction is used as a landmark in certain documents and finds this mildly amusing. She also knows approximately where the cache is. She is not hostile but is not forthcoming without reason — she can be a source of information or a complication depending on the party's approach.
  • A linguist in Heian's Hikari Zon — recognizes the script when shown it and becomes very quiet; she asks where the party found it and seems genuinely frightened by the answer.

Discovery Paths

  • A linguist in Heian recognizes the script and provides context about the Eikyu Yami Clan's cipher language
  • The kitsune at the fox's den has been waiting for someone worth talking to; she has information she's been holding for some time
  • A second group is following the same letter's directions — they are further behind the party but moving with purpose and professional competence

Full Truth

The cache is a sealed container — a lacquered iron box, buried and warded — holding a fragmentary copy of the necromantic tome that Kuroyami originally found in Kuroshi Temple on Yurei. The original tome went with Kuroyami when he escaped. What the party would find is a hand-copied excerpt — several pages of the original text, copied by an early follower who then buried their copy here when they realized what following this path would cost them. The excerpt covers transformation rituals — dark ones — and is connected to the same tradition that the Gekko seimasters eventually discovered (through a different branch of the same source material).

Resolution Options

  • Finding the cache completes the treasure-hunt objective but opens a much larger question: what is this fragment, who else is looking for it, and what does its existence imply about how widely Kuroyami's knowledge has spread?
  • The Eikyu Yami Clan operatives who hired the bandits will eventually realize the bandits failed and send someone more capable
  • The fragment's content — transformation rituals connected to the Gekko disaster — makes it directly relevant to the main investigation

Timing

  • The Eikyu Yami follow-up operative will arrive when the bandit failure is confirmed; timeline flexible
  • A second group following the letter's directions is further behind but moving with professional competence
  • No hard deadline; the cache has been there for a long time and is not going anywhere

Connections

  • main-gekko-investigation — the necromantic fragment covers the same transformation rituals that created the Nagaji; different branch of the same source material
  • Eikyu Yami Clan / Kuroyami no Akuma — the persistent remnant of the Plague Campaign villain; the cache is their buried knowledge
  • The kitsune — a 200-year-old fox spirit who serves as both resource and potential complication; needs name, personality, and stat block before encounter
  • Murasakiryu connection — open question whether Kuroyami's original discovery on Yurei was arranged by the Amethyst Progenitor

quests.name: Spoils of Justice: The Thieves' Hoard

text.content:
Type
quest
Status
resolved
Location
ayame
Quest Type
side
Quest Giver
discovered

"The goods found a more deserving home. The thieves found a faster route to their destinations."

Background

Traveling north on the Emperor's Highway, the party passed a group of men taking a roadside break from travel — seated around a card game, apparently at leisure. Sun Wukong overheard a fragment of conversation referencing "the daimyo's men hitting the road by nightfall" — the kind of information that only matters if you're trying to avoid official attention. A closer look revealed goods in their wagon, mostly concealed under canvas.

Ko'jiri, characteristically, engaged them. The conversation that followed was a masterpiece of social engineering: two of the men were talked into turning on the other two. The group dissolved into conflict, and the survivors scattered in opposite directions as the party made clear they were not going to let the matter rest.

The stolen goods were recovered and subsequently turned over to Chief Inspector Oshiro Masahiro of the Teikoku Keisatsu in Ayame, who received them without excessive questions and confirmed the party's good-faith engagement with legal authority. This interaction contributed meaningfully to Oshiro's decision to confirm the party as trustworthy when the wagon impoundment situation arose shortly thereafter.

Objectives

  • Relieve the thieves of the burden of having to manage the ill-gotten gains
  • Decide what to do with the goods
  • Goods turned in to the Imperial Police in Ayame

Known Information

Outcome & Consequences — The goods were returned through official channels. Oshiro Masahiro's positive assessment of the party — which later resulted in the return of the impounded wagon and a reward — was influenced in part by this demonstration of law-abiding intent. The party gained a confirmed ally in the Chief Inspector.

The two surviving thieves are somewhere on the road. They know what the party looks like. Whether this matters is an open question — professional thieves who escaped a bad situation typically prioritize distance over revenge, but the fragment of conversation about "the daimyo's men" suggests they may have been operating under someone else's direction.

Hidden Truth

The goods were not random opportunistic theft. The thieves were part of a small, loosely organized network of independent contractors working for a merchant in Heian's Ichiba Chiku — a legitimate-seeming trading operation that runs a side business in redirected goods. "Redirected" meaning: items that were supposed to arrive at one destination are intercepted and sold to a different buyer who doesn't ask where they came from. The daimyo's men reference meant a Clan Kaminari supply transport was expected on the road by nightfall and the thieves were either planning to avoid it or had originally intended to intercept it.

NPC Knowledge

  • The card-player thief — Headed back toward Heian; has put the entire incident out of his mind as a professional hazard.
  • The talking thief — More enterprising; has been thinking about the party since the encounter; quietly asking around about who they are. Not planning revenge. Considering whether the party might be useful to know, or whether there might be money in information about where they went. Not a significant threat but is a loose thread.
  • Oshiro Masahiro — Official report noted the party by description (not by name at that point) and flagged them as "travelers of apparent good character and law-abiding intent operating in the Hana northern highway corridor." This report is in the Teikoku Keisatsu's Ayame file.

Discovery Paths

  • The enterprising thief's inquiries could surface if someone else is also looking for information about the party
  • Oshiro's report in the Ayame file is accessible to anyone with Teikoku Keisatsu access

Full Truth

The merchant operation in Heian's Ichiba Chiku continues. The thieves were low-level contractors; losing them is a minor operational hiccup, not a crisis. The "daimyo's men" reference points to a Clan Kaminari supply transport — suggesting the network has enough intelligence on military logistics to plan around official movements.

Resolution Options

Quest is resolved. The goods were returned. Oshiro is an ally. The remaining loose threads (the surviving thieves, the Heian merchant operation) are background elements available for future use.

Timing

No active timing pressures. The enterprising thief's inquiries are ongoing but low-priority.

Connections

  • Chief Inspector Oshiro Masahiro — confirmed ally; his positive assessment of the party has practical value in Ayame and the broader Hana region
  • The enterprising thief — a loose thread who is gathering information about the party; could be a minor complication or a contact depending on future developments
  • Heian's Ichiba Chiku merchant network — background criminal operation that could resurface if the party returns to Heian

description.value:
Type
race

Simian people of Seizan — see core/races.md for the canonical Kagekuni entry and npcs/elder-benkei.md for the exemplar elder.

Description

The Guhuza are the ape-folk of Seizan: tall, fur-covered humanoids who walk upright, speak the old tongues, and live remarkably long lives by human reckoning. In Kagekuni they are most often encountered as monks, scholars, and forest-wardens, though the two subraces — the burly Kwita and the lithe, tailed Izina — carry very different bearings. Their native speech cannot be written in Common script, so Guhuza who travel beyond Seizan typically adopt a name from the language of their hosts.

Guhuza are a setting-native race in Kagekuni (see core/races.md). Elder Benkei of the Order of the Tranquil Lotus is 198 years old, establishing longevity as a canon trait — Guhuza mature between ages 10 and 14 but may live for centuries.

Racial Traits Summary

  • Ability Score Increase: Intelligence +2 (plus subrace modifier)
  • Age: mature at 10–14; long-lived
  • Size: Medium (roughly human-sized; Kwita tend larger, Izina smaller)
  • Speed: 30 ft walking
  • Darkvision: 60 ft
  • Adept Learner: proficiency with two artisan's tools of your choice
  • Languages: Common plus two languages of your choice
  • Subrace: choose Kwita or Izina

Kwita (great-ape lineage)

  • Ability Score Increase: Strength +1
  • Thunderwave (innate): cast the thunderwave spell once per short/long rest; Intelligence is the spellcasting ability
  • Great Build: proficient in Athletics and Intimidation

Izina (tailed-monkey lineage)

  • Ability Score Increase: Dexterity +1
  • Agile: advantage on Dex (Acrobatics) checks to escape a grapple
  • Prehensile Tail: proficient in Acrobatics
  • Nimble Climbers: climbing speed equal to walking speed

text.content:
Type
recipe

A demonstration recipe used to validate the Mastercrafted export pipeline. Mirrors the live "Test → Recipe" page dumped from the world: three ingredient slots, one product slot, cooking + survival check.

Ingredients

Products

Description

Round-trip test recipe. When the export pipeline writes this file into the kagekuni-recipes compendium pack, the resulting Mastercrafted recipe page should be byte-equivalent to the live one we dumped from the world.

Reference Format

The ref: field on each component supports three forms:

  • world:Item.<world-id> — references an existing world-level item by its Foundry-assigned ID. Used for items that haven't been migrated to markdown yet. Will not survive a fresh world.
  • item:<slug> — references a Kagekuni item file by its markdown slug (e.g. item:katana). The build pipeline resolves this to the stable compendium UUID.
  • compendium:<pack>.<id> — direct reference to a compendium item by its _id. Use sparingly.

For new recipes, prefer item:<slug> so the recipe survives world rebuilds and renames.
